qa_dataset.answer: Hady refers specifically to livestock or offerings that are brought to the Haram (sacred precincts of Makkah) and slaughtered there as a devotion, whereas Ud-hiyah refers to the sacrifice slaughtered for Allah on the Day of Eid al-Adha and the Days of Tashriq, which can be done anywhere as a means of seeking nearness to Him.
qa_dataset.question: What is the key linguistic and legal distinction between the terms 'Hady' and 'Ud-hiyah' as discussed in the text?

qa_dataset.answer: According to the Hadith of Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, four main defects render an animal invalid: 1) a one-eyed animal with evident blindness; 2) an animal with an evident illness; 3) a lame animal with evident lameness; and 4) an emaciated animal with no fat/marrow on its bones. Additional defects mentioned by scholars in the text include complete blindness, missing front teeth, and dried-up udders due to old age.
qa_dataset.question: Which physical defects disqualify an animal from being used as a valid sacrifice (Ud-hiyah or Hady)? Support your answer with the text's referenced Hadith.

qa_dataset.answer: A sheep is only sufficient for one person (or one person and their family for Ud-hiyah), and it must be a Jadh'ah (at least six months old). A camel (Badanah) or a cow can be shared by up to seven people for both Hady and Ud-hiyah. The age requirement for a cow is Thaniyyah (at least two years old), and for a camel, it is Thaniyyah (at least five years old).
qa_dataset.question: Explain the sharing rules and minimum age requirements for camels, cows, and sheep when offered as sacrifices.

qa_dataset.answer: It is highly recommended and permissible for the offerer to eat from, gift, and give charity from the Hady of Tamattu‘, Qirān, or voluntary Ud-hiyah. However, for a compensatory offering (Hady al-Jubran)—which is mandatory due to committing a violation during Ihram or omitting a mandatory pilgrimage ritual—the offerer is strictly forbidden from eating any part of it; it must be distributed entirely to others.
qa_dataset.question: What is the difference in ruling regarding eating from a voluntary/pilgrimage offering (Hady of Tamattu' or Qiran) versus a compensatory offering (Hady al-Jubran)?

qa_dataset.answer: The first level (most complete) requires cutting the windpipe, esophagus, and both jugular veins. The second level requires cutting the windpipe, esophagus, and one of the two jugular veins, which is valid but less complete. The third level requires cutting only the windpipe and esophagus without the jugular veins, which is still legally valid and represents the chosen, facilitating opinion in the text.
qa_dataset.question: Based on the decree of Imam Ibn Baz, compare the three levels of anatomical cuts during slaughtering (Tadhkiyah) and state which is considered the most complete.

qa_dataset.answer: Once the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah begin, the person intending to offer a sacrifice is restricted from cutting, trimming, or removing any of their hair or nails until the animal has been slaughtered. If they do violate this restriction, they must seek Allah's forgiveness, but no material expiation (fidyah) or penalty is required.
qa_dataset.question: What behavioral restrictions apply to a person intending to sacrifice during the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah, and what is the ruling if they violate these restrictions?

# Rulings on Sacrificial Animals, Offerings, and Slaughtering
### اللَّجْنَةُ العِلْمِيَّةُ ### بِرِئَاسَةِ الشُّؤُونِ الدِّينِيَّةِ بِالْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَالْمَسْجِدِ النَّبَوِيِّ
**The Scientific Committee under the Presidency of Religious Affairs at the Sacred Mosque and the Prophet's Mosque** ::: --- ### Page 4 ::: {style="text-align: center;"} ## بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ ::: ### Rulings on Sacrificial Animals, Offerings, and Slaughtering #### Introduction All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. May the peace and blessings of Allah be upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, his family, his Companions, and those who adhere to his Sunnah and follow his guidance until the Day of Judgment. To proceed: This is a concise treatise encompassing the most essential needs of a Muslim regarding the rulings of sacrificial animals, offerings, and slaughtering. We have compiled it for the visitors of the Two Holy Mosques, so they may be informed and insightful about their religious matters. We implore the Generous Bestower to make it beneficial, righteous, and sincere for His sake. Indeed, He is the best to be asked and the most generous to be hoped for. **The Scientific Committee of the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages** #### The Rulings on Hady and Ud-hiyah **Hady:** Everything that is offered to the Haram (sacred precincts) and slaughtered therein from livestock and others. It is named as such because it is offered to Allah, the Exalted. ::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 20px;"} — 2 — ::: --- ### Page 5 **'Ud'hiyah:** with the hamzah pronounced with a dammah or kasrah, refers to that which is slaughtered for Allah on the Day of Eid and the Days of Tashrīq as a means of getting close to Allah Almighty. Muslims have unanimously agreed on their legitimacy. The best sacrificial offerings are camels, then cows, if offered fully due to their higher value and the benefit to the needy with abundant meat, then sheep. The best of each type is the one with the most meat, followed by the most expensive, as Allah Almighty says: ::: {style="text-align: center; direction: rtl; font-family: 'Amiri', serif; font-size: 1.2em; margin: 15px 0;"} ﴿ ذَٰلِكَ وَمَن يُعَظِّمْ شَعَائِرَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّهَا مِن تَقْوَى الْقُلُوبِ ٣٢ ﴾ ::: *{This is so. And whoever honors the rituals of Allah, it is from the piety of the hearts.} [Surat al-Hajj: 32]* It is only permissible to offer a Jadh‘ah sheep, which is six months old, and a Thaniyyah from other cattle such as camels, cows, and goats. A Thaniyyah camel is five years old, a Thaniyyah cow is two years old, and a Thaniyyah goat is one year old. A sheep is sufficient as Hady for one person, and as Ud-hiyah, it suffices for one person and his family. A Badanah or a cow suffices as Hady and Ud-hiyah for seven persons, according to the Hadīth of ::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 20px;"} — 3 — ::: --- ### Page 6 Jābir ibn ‘Abdullāh (may Allah be pleased with both of them), who said: ::: {style="text-align: justify; direction: rtl; font-family: 'Amiri', serif; font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 1.6; margin: 15px 0;"} «نَحَرْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَامَ الْحُدَيْبِيَةِ الْبَدَنَةَ عَنْ سَبْعَةٍ، وَالْبَقَرَةَ عَنْ سَبْعَةٍ». ::: *“In the year of Al-Hudaybiyah, we slaughtered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a camel on behalf of seven persons and a cow on behalf of seven persons.”* In another version: ::: {style="text-align: justify; direction: rtl; font-family: 'Amiri', serif; font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 1.6; margin: 15px 0;"} «خَرَجْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مُهِلِّينَ بِالْحَجِّ فَأَمَرَنَا رَسُولُ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنْ نَشْتَرِكَ فِي الْإِبِلِ وَالْبَقَرِ كُلُّ سَبْعَةٍ مِنَّا فِي بَدَنَةٍ». ::: *“We set out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while proclaiming the intention for Hajj. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded us that every seven of us should share in one camel or one cow.”* In another version: ::: {style="text-align: justify; direction: rtl; font-family: 'Amiri', serif; font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 1.6; margin: 15px 0;"} «حَجَجْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَنَحَرْنَا الْبَعِيرَ عَنْ سَبْعَةٍ، وَالْبَقَرَةَ عَنْ سَبْعَةٍ». ::: *“We performed Hajj with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and we slaughtered a camel on behalf of seven persons and a cow on behalf of seven persons.”* [^1] Abu Ayyūb al-Ansāri (may Allah be pleased with him) reported, when asked: “How were the sacrifices during the Messenger of Allah’s (ﷺ) time?” he said: [^1]: Narrated by Muslim. ::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 20px;"} — 4 — ::: --- ### Page 7 ::: {style="text-align: justify; direction: rtl; font-family: 'Amiri', serif; font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 1.6; margin: 15px 0;"} «كَانَ الرَّجُلُ يُضَحِّي بِالشَّاةِ عَنْهُ وَعَنْ أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ، فَيَأْكُلُونَ، وَيُطْعِمُونَ، حَتَّى تَبَاهَى النَّاسُ فَصَارَتْ كَمَا تَرَى». ::: *“A man would sacrifice a sheep for himself and his family, and they would eat from it and feed others, until people began to boast, and it became as you see.”* [^2] A sheep is better than the seventh part of a camel and a cow. Only a sound animal, free from disease, missing limbs, or emaciation, suffices for Hady and Ud-hiyah. Thus, a one-eyed animal with evident blindness, a blind animal, an emaciated animal with no marrow, a lame animal unable to walk with healthy ones, a toothless animal whose front teeth are missing, an animal whose udder has dried up due to old age, or a sick animal with obvious illness does not suffice. This is based on the Hadīth of Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us and said: ::: {style="text-align: justify; direction: rtl; font-family: 'Amiri', serif; font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 1.6; margin: 15px 0;"} «أَرْبَعٌ لَا تَجُوزُ فِي الْأَضَاحِي: الْعَوْرَاءُ الْبَيِّنُ عَوْرُهَا، وَالْمَرِيضَةُ الْبَيِّنُ مَرَضُهَا، وَالْعَرْجَاءُ الْبَيِّنُ ظَلْعُهَا، وَالْعَجْفَاءُ الَّتِي لَا تُنْقِي». ::: *“Four animals are not valid for Ud-hiyah: a one-eyed animal whose defect is evident; an animal which is evidently ill; a lame animal whose* [^2]: Narrated by At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Mājah. ::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 20px;"} — 5 — ::: --- ### Page 8 *lameness is evident; and an emaciated animal with no fat on it.”* [^3] Imam At-Tirmidhi (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “This is acted upon according to the scholars.” [^4] The time for slaughtering the Hady of Tamattu‘ and the Ud-hiyah is from after the Eid prayer until the last of the Tashrīq Days, according to the correct opinion. It is recommended to eat from his Hady if it is Hady of Tamattu‘ or Qirān, and from his ’Ud-hiyah, and to give some as gifts and some as charity in thirds; as Allah Almighty says: ::: {style="text-align: center; direction: rtl; font-family: 'Amiri', serif; font-size: 1.2em; margin: 15px 0;"} ﴿ ... فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا الْبَائِسَ الْفَقِيرَ ٢٨ ﴾ ::: *{Then eat from it and feed the desperately poor.} [Surat al-Hajj: 28]* As for the compensatory offering (Hady al-Jubrān), which is due to a prohibited act committed during Ihrām or for omitting an obligation, one must not eat from it. Whoever intends to offer a sacrifice, once the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah begin, he should not take anything from his hair or his nails until he slaughters the sacrificial animal, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: [^3]: Narrated by Abu Dāwūd, Al-Tirmidhi, An-Nasā’i, and Ibn Mājah. [^4]: Narrated by At-Tirmidhi. ::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 20px;"} — 6 — ::: --- ### Page 9 ::: {style="text-align: justify; direction: rtl; font-family: 'Amiri', serif; font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 1.6; margin: 15px 0;"} «إِذَا دَخَلَ الْعَشْرُ، وَأَرَادَ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ يُضَحِّيَ؛ فَلَا يَأْخُذْ مِنْ شَعْرِهِ وَلَا مِنْ أَظْفَارِهِ شَيْئًا، حَتَّى يُضَحِّيَ». ::: *“When the ten days begin, and one of you wants to offer ’Ud-hiyah, let him not cut anything from his hair or nails until he offers the sacrifice.”* [^5] If he does any of that, he should ask Allah for forgiveness, and no expiation is due upon him. The manner of slaughtering the sacrificial animals, offerings, and others that are to be slaughtered is as follows: 1. Only a discerning, sane Muslim or a person from the People of the Book may perform the slaughter, intending the act of "tadhkiyah" (slaughtering). He must not slaughter for anyone other than Allah, nor invoke the name of anyone other than Allah. He should mention the name of Allah at the time of slaughter or "nahr" (slaughtering camels), and use a sharp tool that is neither a tooth nor a nail, ensuring the blood flows at the designated place. The slaughterer must be legally permitted to perform the slaughter according to Shariah. [^6] 2. He chooses the Ud-hiyah, ensuring to select the finest Ud-hiyah; for indeed [^5]: Narrated by Muslim. [^6]: The Rulings on Ud-hiyah by the esteemed scholar Muhammad ibn ‘Uthaymīn, (pp. 56 – 87). ::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 20px;"} — 7 — ::: --- ### Page 10 ::: {style="text-align: justify; direction: rtl; font-family: 'Amiri', serif; font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 1.6; margin: 15px 0;"} «ضَحَّى رَسُولُ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِكَبْشَيْنِ أَمْلَحَيْنِ، أَقْرَنَيْنِ، ذَبَحَهُمَا بِيَدِهِ، وَسَمَّى، وَكَبَّرَ، وَوَضَعَ رِجْلَهُ عَلَى صِفَاحِهِمَا». ::: *“The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sacrificed two black and white horned rams, which he slaughtered with his hand. He mentioned Allah's name and proclaimed His greatness, and placed his foot on their necks.”* [^7] 3. Kindness toward the animal to be slaughtered involves doing everything to ease its suffering during the act of slaughter. This includes using a sharp tool and passing it over the area of slaughter quickly and strongly, as the aim is to swiftly end the life in the best manner without causing unnecessary pain. This is based on the Hadīth of Shaddād ibn Aws (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "I have preserved two things from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who said: ::: {style="text-align: justify; direction: rtl; font-family: 'Amiri', serif; font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 1.6; margin: 15px 0;"} «إِنَّ اللهَ كَتَبَ الْإِحْسَانَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، فَإِذَا قَتَلْتُمْ فَأَحْسِنُوا الْقِتْلَةَ، وَإِذَا ذَبَحْتُمْ فَأَحْسِنُوا الذَّبْحَ، وَلْيُحِدَّ أَحَدُكُمْ شَفْرَتَهُ، وَلْيُرِحْ ذَبِيحَتَهُ». ::: *“Verily, Allah has enjoined kindness in all things. So, when you kill, kill with kindness; and when you slaughter, slaughter with kindness. Let one of you sharpen his blade and spare the slaughtered animal the suffering.”* [^8] [^7]: Narrated by Al-Bukhāri and Muslim. [^8]: Narrated by Muslim. ::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 20px;"} — 8 — ::: --- ### Page 11 It is disliked to sharpen the knife while the animal is looking at it, as reported from Ibn ‘Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) who said: ::: {style="text-align: justify; direction: rtl; font-family: 'Amiri', serif; font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 1.6; margin: 15px 0;"} أَمَرَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِحَدِّ الشِّفَارِ، وَأَنْ تُوَارَى عَنِ الْبَهَائِمِ، وَقَالَ: «إِذَا ذَبَحَ أَحَدُكُمْ؛ فَلْيُجْهِزْ». ::: The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded that blades be sharpened and kept out of sight of the animals, and said: *“When one of you slaughters, let him do so swiftly.”* [^9] 4. If the sacrificial animal is a camel, it should be slaughtered by Nahr while standing with its left foreleg tied, as per the Hadith of ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both). He came upon a man who had made his camel kneel down to slaughter it. He said: Slaughter it while it is standing with one leg tied up, as this is the Sunnah of Muhammad (ﷺ). [^10] 5. If the sacrificial animal is not a camel, it should be slaughtered while lying on its left side, and the slaughterer should place his foot on its neck to control it, as in the Hadīth narrated by Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: ::: {style="text-align: justify; direction: rtl; font-family: 'Amiri', serif; font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 1.6; margin: 15px 0;"} «ضَحَّى رَسُولُ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِكَبْشَيْنِ أَمْلَحَيْنِ، أَقْرَنَيْنِ، ذَبَحَهُمَا بِيَدِهِ، وَسَمَّى، وَكَبَّرَ، وَوَضَعَ رِجْلَهُ عَلَى صِفَاحِهِمَا». ::: [^9]: Narrated by Ahmad and Ibn Mājah. [^10]: Narrated by Al-Bukhāri and Muslim. ::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 20px;"} — 9 — ::: --- ### Page 12 *“The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sacrificed two black and white horned rams, which he slaughtered with his hand. He mentioned Allah's name and proclaimed His greatness, and put his foot on their necks.”* [^11] Mentioning the name of Allah Almighty upon slaughtering and doing Nahr (sacrificing a camel) is obligatory, for Allah Almighty says: ::: {style="text-align: center; direction: rtl; font-family: 'Amiri', serif; font-size: 1.2em; margin: 15px 0;"} ﴿ فَكُلُوا مِمَّا ذُكِرَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ إِن كُنتُم بِآيَاتِهِ مُؤْمِنِينَ ١١٨ ﴾ ::: *{So eat of that [meat] over which the name of Allah is mentioned if you [truly] believe in his verses.} [Surat al-An‘ām: 118]* And Allah Almighty says: ::: {style="text-align: center; direction: rtl; font-family: 'Amiri', serif; font-size: 1.2em; margin: 15px 0;"} ﴿ وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا مِمَّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَفِسْقٌ ۗ وَإِنَّ الشَّيَاطِينَ لَيُوحُونَ إِلَىٰ أَوْلِيَائِهِمْ لِيُجَادِلُوكُمْ ۖ وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ ١٢١ ﴾ ::: *{Do not eat of that [meat] over which the name of Allah is not mentioned, for this is a grave disobedience. But the devils whisper to their [human] friends to argue with you; if you were to obey them, you would surely become polytheists.} [Surat al-An‘ām: 121]* And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: ::: {style="text-align: justify; direction: rtl; font-family: 'Amiri', serif; font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 1.6; margin: 15px 0;"} «مَا أَنْهَرَ الدَّمَ وَذُكِرَ اسْمُ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ؛ فَكُلُوهُ مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ سِنًّا وَلَا ظُفُرًا». ::: *“Whatever causes the blood to flow and the name of Allah is mentioned over it, then eat it,* [^11]: Narrated by Al-Bukhāri and Muslim. ::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 20px;"} — 10 — ::: --- ### Page 13 *unless it is with teeth or claws.”* [^12] It is recommended to say "Allāhu Akbar" (Allah is the Greatest) along with Tasmiyah (saying Bismillah), based on the Hadīth of Jābir (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "I attended the Eid al-Adhā prayer with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the prayer place. When he finished his sermon, he descended from his pulpit, and a ram was brought to him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slaughtered it with his hand and said: ::: {style="text-align: justify; direction: rtl; font-family: 'Amiri', serif; font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 1.6; margin: 15px 0;"} «بِسْمِ اللهِ وَاللهُ أَكْبَرُ، هَذَا عَنِّي وَعَنْ مَنْ لَمْ يُضَحِّ مِنْ أُمَّتِي». ::: *“In the name of Allah and Allah is the Greatest, this is on behalf of myself and those of my Ummah who have not offered a sacrifice.”* [^13] 7. Cutting the throat, esophagus, and the two jugular veins, and causing the blood to flow: Imam Ibn Bāz (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “The lawful slaughtering of camels, cattle, and sheep is of three types: **The first case:** The slaughterer cuts the windpipe, the pharynx, and the jugular veins, which is the most complete and best form of slaughter. If these four are cut, the slaughter is lawful according to all scholars. **The second case:** Cutting the throat, esophagus, [^12]: Narrated by Al-Bukhāri and Muslim. [^13]: Narrated by Abu Dāwūd and At-Tirmidhi; Al-Albāni classified it as Sahīh (authentic). ::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 20px;"} — 11 — ::: --- ### Page 14 and one of the two jugular veins; this is lawful, valid, and good, though it is less than the first. **The third case:** Cutting only the throat and esophagus without the two large veins, which is also valid. # Rulings on Sacrificial Animals, Offerings, and Slaughtering

## Introduction

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. May the peace and blessings of Allah be upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, his family, his Companions, and those who adhere to his Sunnah and follow his guidance until the Day of Judgment. To proceed:

This is a concise treatise encompassing the most essential needs of a Muslim regarding the rulings of sacrificial animals, offerings, and slaughtering. We have compiled it for the visitors of the Two Holy Mosques, so they may be informed and insightful about their religious matters. We implore the Generous Bestower to make it beneficial, righteous, and sincere for His sake. Indeed, He is the best to be asked and the most generous to be hoped for.

**The Scientific Committee of the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages**

---

## The Rulings on Hady and Ud-hiyah

* **Hady:** Everything that is offered to the Haram (sacred precincts) and slaughtered therein from livestock and others. It is named as such because it is offered to Allah, the Exalted.
* **Ud-hiyah:** (pronounced with a *dammah* or *kasrah* on the *hamzah*) refers to that which is slaughtered for Allah on the Day of Eid and the Days of Tashrīq as a means of getting close to Allah Almighty.

Muslims have unanimously agreed on their legitimacy.

### Preference of Animals
The best sacrificial offerings are camels, then cows (if offered fully due to their higher value and the benefit to the needy with abundant meat), and then sheep. 

The best of each type is the one with the most meat, followed by the most expensive, as Allah Almighty says:

$$\text{\RL{﴿ ذَٰلِكَ وَمَن يُعَظِّمْ شَعَائِرَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّهَا مِن تَقْوَى الْقُلُوبِ ٣٢ ﴾}}$$

> *{This is so. And whoever honors the rituals of Allah, it is from the piety of the hearts.}* [Surat al-Hajj: 32]

### Age Requirements
It is only permissible to offer a *Jadh‘ah* sheep, which is six months old, and a *Thaniyyah* from other cattle such as camels, cows, and goats. 
* **Thaniyyah camel:** Five years old
* **Thaniyyah cow:** Two years old
* **Thaniyyah goat:** One year old

### Shares of the Sacrifice
A sheep is sufficient as Hady for one person, and as Ud-hiyah, it suffices for one person and his family. A *Badanah* (camel) or a cow suffices as Hady and Ud-hiyah for seven persons, according to the Hadīth of Jābir ibn ‘Abdullāh (may Allah be pleased with both of them), who said:

$$\text{\RL{«نَحَرْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَامَ الْحُدَيْبِيَةِ الْبَدَنَةَ عَنْ سَبْعَةٍ، وَالْبَقَرَةَ عَنْ سَبْعَةٍ».}}$$

> *“In the year of Al-Hudaybiyah, we slaughtered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a camel on behalf of seven persons and a cow on behalf of seven persons.”* 

In another version:

$$\text{\RL{«خَرَجْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مُهِلِّينَ بِالْحَجِّ فَأَمَرَنَا رَسُولِ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنْ نَشْتَرِكَ فِي الْإِبِلِ وَالْبَقَرِ كُلُّ سَبْعَةٍ مِنَّا فِي بَدَنَةٍ».}}$$

> *“We set out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while proclaiming the intention for Hajj. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded us that every seven of us should share in one camel or one cow.”*

In a third version:

$$\text{\RL{«حَجَجْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَنَحَرْنَا الْبَعِيرَ عَنْ سَبْعَةٍ، وَالْبَقَرَةَ عَنْ سَبْعَةٍ».}}$$

> *“We performed Hajj with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and we slaughtered a camel on behalf of seven persons and a cow on behalf of seven persons.”* (Narrated by Muslim)

Abu Ayyūb al-Ansāri (may Allah be pleased with him) reported, when asked: “How were the sacrifices during the Messenger of Allah’s (ﷺ) time?” he said:

$$\text{\RL{«كَانَ الرَّجُلُ يُضَحِّي بِالشَّاةِ عَنْهُ وَعَنْ أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ، فَيَأْكُلُونَ، وَيُطْعِمُونَ، حَتَّى تَبَاهَى النَّاسُ فَصَارَتْ كَمَا تَرَى».}}$$

> *“A man would sacrifice a sheep for himself and his family, and they would eat from it and feed others, until people began to boast, and it became as you see.”* (Narrated by At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Mājah)

A single sheep is better than sharing a seventh part of a camel or a cow.

---

## Defects that Disqualify an Animal

Only a sound animal, free from disease, missing limbs, or emaciation, suffices for Hady and Ud-hiyah. Thus, the following do not suffice:
1. A one-eyed animal with evident blindness.
2. A completely blind animal.
3. An emaciated animal with no marrow.
4. A lame animal unable to walk with healthy ones.
5. A toothless animal whose front teeth are missing.
6. An animal whose udder has dried up due to old age.
7. A sick animal with obvious illness.

This is based on the Hadīth of Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us and said:

$$\text{\RL{«أَرْبَعٌ لَا تَجُوزُ فِي الْأَضَاحِي: الْعَوْرَاءُ الْبَيِّنُ عَوْرُهَا، وَالْمَرِيضَةُ الْبَيِّنُ مَرَضُهَا، وَالْعَرْجَاءُ الْبَيِّنُ ظَلْعُهَا، وَالْعَجْفَاءُ الَّتِي لَا تُنْقِي».}}$$

> *“Four animals are not valid for Ud-hiyah: a one-eyed animal whose defect is evident; an animal which is evidently ill; a lame animal whose lameness is evident; and an emaciated animal with no fat on it.”* (Narrated by Abu Dāwūd, Al-Tirmidhi, An-Nasā’i, and Ibn Mājah)

Imam At-Tirmidhi said: *“This is acted upon according to the scholars.”*

---

## Timing and Distribution

### Timeframe
The time for slaughtering the Hady of *Tamattu‘* and the *Ud-hiyah* starts from after the Eid prayer until the sunset of the last day of the Days of Tashrīq (13th of Dhul-Hijjah), according to the correct opinion.

### Distribution
It is recommended to eat from the Hady of *Tamattu‘* or *Qirān*, and from the *Ud-hiyah*, and to divide it into three parts: one-third for eating, one-third for gifts, and one-third for charity. Allah Almighty says:

$$\text{\RL{﴿ ... فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا الْبَائِسَ الْفَقِيرَ ٢٨ ﴾}}$$

> *{Then eat from it and feed the desperately poor.}* [Surat al-Hajj: 28]

* **Compensatory Offerings (Hady al-Jubrān):** If the offering is due to a prohibited act committed during Ihrām or for omitting an obligatory ritual, the offerer must not eat from it.

### Restrictions on the Sacrificer
Whoever intends to offer a sacrifice, once the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah begin, he should not take anything from his hair or his nails until he slaughters the sacrificial animal, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

$$\text{\RL{«إِذَا دَخَلَ الْعَشْرُ، وَأَرَادَ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ يُضَحِّيَ؛ فَلَا يَأْخُذْ مِنْ شَعْرِهِ وَلَا مِنْ أَظْفَارِهِ شَيْئًا، حَتَّى يُضَحِّيَ».}}$$

> *“When the ten days begin, and one of you wants to offer ’Ud-hiyah, let him not cut anything from his hair or nails until he offers the sacrifice.”* (Narrated by Muslim)

If he does any of that out of forgetfulness or error, he should ask Allah for forgiveness, and no expiation (*fidyah*) is due upon him.

---

## The Manner and Etiquettes of Slaughtering (Tadhkiyah)

1. **The Slaughterer:** Only a discerning, sane Muslim or a person from the People of the Book may perform the slaughter, intending the act of *Tadhkiyah* (lawful slaughtering). He must not slaughter for anyone other than Allah, nor invoke the name of anyone other than Allah.
2. **The Tool:** He must use a sharp tool that is neither a tooth nor a nail, ensuring the blood flows rapidly at the designated place.
3. **Choosing the Animal:** One should select the finest animal. Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated:

   $$\text{\RL{«ضَحَّى رَسُولِ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِكَبْشَيْنِ أَمْلَحَيْنِ، أَقْرَنَيْنِ، ذَبَحَهُمَا بِيَدِهِ، وَسَمَّى، وَكَبَّرَ، وَوَضَعَ رِجْلَهُ عَلَى صِفَاحِهِمَا».}}$$

   > *“The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sacrificed two black and white horned rams, which he slaughtered with his hand. He mentioned Allah's name and proclaimed His greatness, and placed his foot on their necks.”* (Narrated by Al-Bukhāri and Muslim)

4. **Kindness to the Animal (*Ihsān*):** One should ease the suffering of the animal by sharpening the blade beforehand and passing it swiftly and strongly. It is disliked to sharpen the knife while the animal is watching. Shaddād ibn Aws (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

   $$\text{\RL{«إِنَّ اللهَ كَتَبَ الْإِحْسَانَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، فَإِذَا قَتَلْتُمْ فَأَحْسِنُوا الْقِتْلَةَ، وَإِذَا ذَبَحْتُمْ فَأَحْسِنُوا الذَّبْحَ، وَلْيُحِدَّ أَحَدُكُمْ شَفْرَتَهُ، وَلْيُرِحْ ذَبِيحَتَهُ».}}$$

   > *“Verily, Allah has enjoined kindness in all things. So, when you kill, kill with kindness; and when you slaughter, slaughter with kindness. Let one of you sharpen his blade and spare the slaughtered animal the suffering.”* (Narrated by Muslim)

   The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded that blades be sharpened and kept out of sight of the animals, saying:

   $$\text{\RL{«إِذَا ذَبَحَ أَحَدُكُمْ؛ فَلْيُجْهِزْ».}}$$

   > *“When one of you slaughters, let him do so swiftly.”* (Narrated by Ahmad and Ibn Mājah)

5. **Positioning Camels (*Nahr*):** Camels should be slaughtered standing up with the left foreleg tied, as is the Sunnah. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) saw a man who made his camel kneel to slaughter it and told him: *“Slaughter it while it is standing with one leg tied up, as this is the Sunnah of Muhammad (ﷺ).”*
6. **Positioning Other Animals:** Sheep, goats, and cows should be laid down gently on their left side, and the slaughterer should place his foot on the side of the animal's neck to control it.
7. **Obligatory Mention of Allah's Name (*Tasmiyah*):** It is obligatory to say *Bismillah* (In the name of Allah) at the time of slaughter. Allah Almighty says:

   $$\text{\RL{﴿ فَكُلُوا مِمَّا ذُكِرَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ إِن كُنتُم بِآيَاتِهِ مُؤْمِنِينَ ١١٨ ﴾}}$$

   > *{So eat of that [meat] over which the name of Allah is mentioned if you [truly] believe in his verses.}* [Surat al-An‘ām: 118]

   And He says:

   $$\text{\RL{﴿ وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا مِمَّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَفِسْقٌ ۗ ... ١٢١ ﴾}}$$

   > *{Do not eat of that [meat] over which the name of Allah is not mentioned, for this is a grave disobedience...}* [Surat al-An‘ām: 121]

   It is recommended to add the *Takbīr* (*Allāhu Akbar*) after *Tasmiyah*, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

   $$\text{\RL{«بِسْمِ اللهِ وَاللهُ أَكْبَرُ، هَذَا عَنِّي وَعَنْ مَنْ لَمْ يُضَحِّ مِنْ أُمَّتِي».}}$$

   > *“In the name of Allah and Allah is the Greatest, this is on behalf of myself and those of my Ummah who have not offered a sacrifice.”* (Narrated by Abu Dāwūd and At-Tirmidhi)

---

## Anatomical Requirements for Lawful Slaughtering

Imam Ibn Bāz (may Allah have mercy on him) detailed three valid scenarios of cutting during *Tadhkiyah*:

| Case | Parts Cut | Ruling |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **First Case** | Windpipe (throat), pharynx (esophagus), and both jugular veins. | **Most complete & best form** of slaughter. Valid by consensus. |
| **Second Case** | Windpipe, pharynx, and one of the two jugular veins. | **Lawful, valid, and good** (slightly less complete than the first). |
| **Third Case** | Windpipe and pharynx only (without the two jugular veins). | **Valid** according to a group of scholars, based on the Hadīth: *“If the blood is shed and the name of Allah is mentioned, then eat...”* (This is the chosen opinion). |

We ask Allah to benefit us with what He has taught us and to teach us what will benefit us; indeed, He is Most Generous and Most Bountiful. May Allah’s peace and blessings be upon our Prophet Muhammad and his family, and may He grant them abundant peace.

qa_dataset.answer: The Nisāb for agricultural produce (such as dates, raisins, wheat, rice, and barley) is five Wasqs, which equals three hundred Prophet's Sā‘s (equivalent to four average double-handed scoops). The deduction rate depends on the irrigation method: a 10% (one-tenth) levy is applied if irrigated naturally (rain, rivers, or natural springs) without financial expense, whereas a 5% (half of one-tenth) levy is applied if artificial irrigation devices or manual labor-intensive machinery are utilized.
qa_dataset.question: What are the specific parameters and threshold metrics (Nisāb) for Zakah on agricultural produce according to the text?

qa_dataset.answer: Modern paper banknotes (dollars, dinars, riyals) are treated with the exact same legal rulings as gold and silver. If their total value reaches the silver Nisāb (which is 140 Mithqāls, equivalent to 56 Saudi silver Riyals) or the gold Nisāb (20 Mithqāls, equivalent to 92 grams or 11 and 3/7 Saudi gold pounds) and a lunar year (Hawl) has passed over the sum, a 2.5% (one-fourth of one-tenth) Zakah rate must be paid. Profit is treated as subordinate to the original capital and does not require a separate lunar year calculation.
qa_dataset.question: How does the author resolve the contemporary ruling on banknotes, and what are the specific metrics for gold and silver Nisāb?

qa_dataset.answer: According to the most correct of the two scholarly opinions presented by the author, Zakah is obligatory on women's gold and silver jewelry once it reaches the specified Nisāb and a lunar year has elapsed, even if the jewelry is explicitly intended for personal use or lending. This is supported by general textual evidence warning of punishment for unpaid gold and silver, and the specific narration where the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) told a woman wearing two gold bracelets that she would be adorned with bracelets of fire if she did not pay their Zakah.
qa_dataset.question: What is the scholarly ruling presented by Shaykh Ibn Baz regarding paying Zakah on women's personal jewelry?

qa_dataset.answer: No. The correct scholarly consensus cited in the treatise is that outstanding debts do not prevent the obligation of paying Zakah. A Muslim must calculate and pay the Zakah due on the taxable assets currently in their possession once the Nisāb and lunar year conditions are met, regardless of their liabilities.
qa_dataset.question: Does an outstanding debt relieve an individual from their obligation to pay Zakah on assets in their possession?

qa_dataset.answer: Involuntary occurrences such as nosebleeds, wounds, accidental inhalation of water or gasoline, and involuntary vomiting do not invalidate the fast. Non-nutritive medical injections and blood tests also do not break the fast (though delaying them to the night is preferred). However, deliberate, self-induced vomiting does invalidate the fast, and the individual must make up that day.
qa_dataset.question: Identify which bodily fluids or external substances invalidate the fast, and which do not, according to the second treatise.

qa_dataset.answer: It is completely valid to initiate the fast in a state of Janābah or post-menstrual purity before performing Ghusl, provided the status of purity from menstruation or bleeding was reached before the break of dawn. The individual may delay taking the ritual bath (Ghusl) until after the break of dawn, but they must complete it and pray the Fajr prayer before sunrise.
qa_dataset.question: What is the ruling on starting a fast while in a state of major ritual impurity (Janābah) or post-menstrual status if Ghusl has not yet been performed?

qa_dataset.answer: The text explains that the night prayer is highly flexible and has no strict limit. The belief that Tarāwīh must be exactly twenty Rak'ahs, or cannot exceed eleven or thirteen, is incorrect. The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) did not set a rigid number but stated 'the night prayer is two and two.' The Companions under 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) practiced both twenty-three and eleven Rak'ahs, while the Salaf practiced thirty-six or forty-one. The preferred approach depends on the length of physical standing: longer recitations warrant fewer Rak'ahs (eleven or thirteen), while shorter recitations can be balanced by increasing the number of Rak'ahs.

### The First Treatise
### Important Researches on Zakah

All praise is due to Allah Alone, and may Allah’s peace and blessings be upon the one after whom there is no prophet, and upon his family and Companions. To proceed:

The motivation for writing this discourse is to offer advice and remind Muslims about the obligation of Zakah, which many Muslims have neglected and have not fulfilled in the prescribed manner, despite its great importance and being one of the five pillars of Islam without which its structure cannot stand, as per the Hadīth of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم):

> «بُنِيَ الإِسْلاَمُ عَلَى خَمْسٍ: شَهَادَةِ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللهِ، وَإِقَامِ الصَّلاَةِ، وَإِيتَاءِ الزَّكَاةِ، وَصَوْمِ رَمَضَانَ، وَحَجِّ الْبَيْتِ».

“Islam was built on five (pillars): testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing prayer, giving Zakah, fasting Ramadan, and pilgrimage to the House.”[^1] [Its authenticity is agreed upon]

[^1]: Narrated by Al-Bukhāri, no. (8) and Muslim, no. (16).

---

## Page 5

The obligation of Zakah on Muslims is one of the most evident virtues of Islam, demonstrating its care for the affairs of its followers due to its numerous benefits and the dire need of the poor Muslims for it.

Among its benefits is strengthening bonds of affection between the rich and the poor, for souls are naturally inclined to love those who do good to them.

Among its benefits are: purifying and refining the soul, distancing it from the traits of stinginess and miserliness, as the Noble Qur'an alludes to this meaning in His Almighty saying:

> ﴿خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِم بِهَا...﴾

{Take charity from their wealth to cleanse and purify them...} [Surat at-Tawbah: 103].

Among them are: training the Muslim with qualities of generosity, kindness, and compassion towards those in need.

And among them are: seeking blessing, increase, and recompense from Allah, as He Almighty says:

> ﴿...وَمَا أَنفَقْتُم مِّن شَيْءٍ فَهُوَ يُخْلِفُهُۥۖ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ ٱلرَّٰزِقِينَ﴾

{Whatever you spend in charity, He will compensate for it, for He is the Best of Providers.} [Surat Saba’: 39] And in the authentic Hadīth, the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: “Allah Almighty says:

> «يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ أَنْفِقْ أُنْفِقْ عَلَيْكَ...».

**Zakah is obligatory on four categories:** the produce of the earth, including grains and fruits; Sā’imah (freely-grazing) livestock; gold and silver; and merchandise.

Each of these four categories has a specific Nisāb (minimum Zakatable amount), below which Zakah is not obligatory. The Nisāb for grains and fruits is five Wasqs, with each Wasq being sixty Sā‘s according to the Sā‘ of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم). This applies to dates, raisins, wheat, rice, barley, and similar items, totaling three hundred Sā‘s according to the Sā‘ of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم), which is equivalent to four handfuls by the hands of a man of average build when both hands are full.

One-tenth is due if the date palms and crops are irrigated without expenses, i.e., by rain, rivers, flowing springs, and the like.

If they are irrigated with expenses and labor, such as by water-lifting devices and machines, then

As for the Nisāb of freely-grazing camels, cows, and sheep, it is detailed in the authentic Hadīths of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم). Those who wish to know about it can ask the people of knowledge. Were it not for intending brevity, we would have mentioned it for completion of benefit.

The Nisāb of silver is one hundred and forty Mithqāls, and its amount in Saudi Arabian dirhams is fifty-six riyals.

The Nisāb of gold is twenty Mithqāls, which is equivalent to 11 Saudi pounds and 3 sevenths of a pound, or 92 grams. Zakah on them is one-fourth of one-tenth, or 2.5%, for anyone who possesses the Nisāb of either or both, and a Hawl (lunar year) has passed over it.

Profit is subordinate to the principal and does not require a new year, just as the produce of freely-grazing livestock is subordinate to its principal and does not require a new year if its principal amounts to the Nisāb.

Banknotes, which people use today, whether called dirham, dinar, dollar, or any other name, take the same ruling as gold and silver. If their value reaches the Nisāb of silver or gold, and a year has passed, Zakah becomes due on them.

Women's jewelry made of gold or silver is treated like money, especially if it reaches the Nisāb

### The Second Treatise
### The merit of fasting and Qiyām (voluntary night prayer) during Ramadan, along with important rulings that may be unknown to some people

From ‘Abdul-‘Azīz ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Bāz to those among the Muslims who observe it—may Allah guide me and them to the path of the people of faith, and grant me and them understanding of the Sunnah and the Qur’an, Amen.

And may Allah’s peace, mercy, and blessings be upon you.

To proceed: This is a concise counsel concerning the virtue of fasting and performing Qiyām during Ramadan, and the merit of competing in it with righteous deeds, along with clarifying important rulings that may be unknown to some people.

It is authentically reported that the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) used to give glad tidings to his Companions about the coming of the month of Ramadan. He (صلى الله عليه وسلم) would inform them that it is a month in which the gates of mercy and the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of Hellfire are closed, and the devils are chained. He would say:

> «إِذَا كَانَتْ أَوَّلُ لَيْلَةٍ مِنْ رَمَضَانَ فُتِّحَتْ أَبْوَابُ الْجَنَّةِ فَلَمْ يُغْلَقْ مِنْهَا بَابٌ، وَغُلِّقَتْ أَبْوَابُ جَهَنَّمَ فَلَمْ يُفْتَحْ مِنْهَا بَابٌ، وَصُفِّدَتِ الشَّيَاطِينُ، وَيُنَادِي مُنَادٍ: يَا

“When the first night of Ramadan arrives, the gates of Paradise are opened, and not a single gate is closed; the gates of Hellfire are closed, and not a single gate is opened; the devils are chained, and a caller announces: O seeker of good, come forward, and O seeker of evil, desist. The Hadīths concerning the merit of fasting and performing Qiyām during Ramadan, as well as the general merit of fasting, are numerous.

A believer should seize this opportunity, which is the blessing Allah has granted him by allowing him to witness the month of Ramadan. He should hasten to perform acts of obedience, avoid sins, and

{And establish prayer, give zakah, and bow [to Allah] with those who bow.} [Surat al-Baqarah: 43] Allah Almighty also says:

> ﴿حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ وَالصَّلَاةِ الْوُسْطَىٰ وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قَانِتِينَ ﴿٢٣٨﴾﴾

{Be mindful of the prayers, especially the middle prayer; and stand before Allah in complete devotion.} [Surat al-Baqarah: 238] Allah Almighty also says:

> ﴿قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ ﴿١﴾ الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي صَلَاتِهِمْ خَاشِعُونَ ﴿٢﴾﴾

{The believers have attained true success: those who humble themselves in their prayers,} [Surat al-Mu’minūn: 1-2] until He said:

> ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَىٰ صَلَوَاتِهِمْ يُحَافِظُونَ ﴿٩﴾ أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْوَارِثُونَ ﴿١٠﴾ الَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ

---

## Page 19

> الْفِرْدَوْسَ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ ﴿١١﴾﴾

{and those who properly observe their prayers. They will be the inheritors, who will inherit Paradise. They will abide therein eternally.} [Surat al-Mu’minūn: 9-11] The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said:

> «الْعَهْدُ الَّذِي بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُمُ الصَّلَاةُ فَمَنْ تَرَكَهَا فَقَدْ كَفَرَ».

“The covenant between us and them is the prayer; whoever abandons it has disbelieved.”

The most important duty after prayer is the giving of Zakah, as Allah Almighty said:

> ﴿وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ حُنَفَاءَ وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكَاةَ ۚ وَذَٰلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ ﴿٥﴾﴾

{although they were commanded only to worship Allah with sincere devotion to Him, being inclined to the true faith, and to establish prayer and give zakah; that is the true religion.} [Surat al-Bayyinah: 5] Allah Almighty also says:

> ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ ﴿٥٦﴾﴾

{Establish prayer, give zakah and obey the Messenger, so that you may be shown mercy.} [Surat an-Nūr: 56]

The Holy Book of Allah and the noble Sunnah of His Messenger indicate that whoever does not pay the Zakah due on his wealth will be punished by it on the Day of Judgment.

The most important matter after prayer and

---

## Page 20

Zakah is fasting of the month of Ramadan, which is one of the five pillars of Islam mentioned in the statement of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم):

> «بُنِيَ الإِسْلاَمُ عَلَى خَمْسٍ: شَهَادَةِ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللهِ، وَإِقَامِ الصَّلاَةِ، وَإِيتَاءِ الزَّكَاةِ، وَصَوْمِ رَمَضَانَ، وَحَجِّ الْبَيْتِ».

“Islam is built upon five pillars: testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing prayer, giving Zakah, fasting the month of Ramadan, and performing Hajj to the House.”

A Muslim must preserve his fasting and Qiyām from what Allah has prohibited him from in terms of words and deeds, because the purpose of fasting is to obey Allah Almighty and to honor His sanctities, to strive against one’s desires in obedience to one’s Lord, and to accustom oneself to patience in refraining from what Allah has forbidden. The purpose is not merely to abstain from food, drink, and other nullifiers of the fast. For this reason, it is authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) that he said:

> «الصِّيَامُ جُنَّةٌ، فَإِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ صَوْمِ أَحَدِكُمْ فَلَا يَرْفُثْ وَلَا يَصْخَبْ، فَإِنْ سَابَّهُ أَحَدٌ أَوْ قَاتَلَهُ فَلْيَقُلْ: إِنِّي صَائِمٌ».

“Fasting is a shield. When any of you is fasting, he should avoid obscene language and loud voice, and if anyone curses him or quarrels with him, he should say: I am fasting.” The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) is

---

## Page 21

authentically reported to have said:

> «مَنْ لَمْ يَدَعْ قَوْلَ الزُّورِ وَالْعَمَلَ بِهِ وَالْجَهْلَ فَلَيْسَ لِلَّهِ حَاجَةٌ فِي أَنْ يَدَعَ طَعَامَهُ وَشَرَابَهُ».

“Whoever does not give up false speech and acting upon it and does not abandon foolishness, Allah is in no need of him giving up his food and drink.” It is understood from these texts and others that it is obligatory for the fasting person to be cautious of everything Allah Almighty has prohibited and to uphold everything He has enjoined. By doing so, it is hoped that he would attain forgiveness, emancipation from Hellfire, and the acceptance of his fasting and Qiyām.

There are matters that may be unknown to some people:

It is obligatory for a Muslim to fast out of faith and in pursuit of reward from Allah, not for showing off, seeking fame, imitating others, or following family or community. The obligation is to fast because of the belief that Allah has enjoined it, and to seek its reward from his Lord. Similarly, performing Qiyām in Ramadan must be done out of faith and in pursuit of reward from Allah, not for any other reason. This is why the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said:

> «مَنْ صَامَ رَمَضَانَ إِيمَانًا وَاحْتِسَابًا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ، وَمَنْ قَامَ رَمَضَانَ إِيمَانًا وَاحْتِسَابًا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ، وَمَنْ قَامَ لَيْلَةَ الْقَدْرِ إِيمَانًا وَاحْتِسَابًا

---

## Page 22

> غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ».

“Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward from Allah will have his past sins forgiven; and whoever performs Qiyām during Ramadan, faithfully and expecting its reward from Allah, will have his past sins forgiven; and whoever offers Qiyām during the Night of Decree, out of faith and in pursuit of divine reward, will have his past sins forgiven.”

Among the matters whose ruling might be unknown to some people are those that may occur to a fasting person, such as wounds, nosebleeds, vomiting, or water or gasoline reaching his throat without his choice. All these matters do not invalidate the fast. However, if one deliberately vomits, his fast becomes invalidated, as the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said:

> «مَنْ ذَرَعَهُ الْقَيْءُ فَلَا قَضَاءَ عَلَيْهِ، وَمَنْ اسْتَقَاءَ فَعَلَيْهِ الْقَضَاءُ».

“Whoever is overcome by vomiting is not required to make up, but whoever vomits intentionally must make up.”

A similar situation arises for a fasting person who delays Ghusl (ritual bath) from Janābah (major ritual impurity) until dawn, and for some women who delay Ghusl from menstruation or post-partum bleeding until dawn if they attain purity before dawn. In this case, she is required to fast, and

---

## Page 23

there is no objection to delaying Ghusl until after the break of dawn. However, she must not delay it until sunrise; rather, she must perform Ghusl and pray Fajr before sunrise. Similarly, the person in the state of major impurity must not delay Ghusl until after sunrise; rather, he is obliged to perform Ghusl and offer the Fajr prayer before sunrise. It is incumbent upon the man to hasten in doing so in order to catch the Fajr prayer with the congregation.

Among the matters that do not invalidate the fast are blood tests and injections that are not intended for nourishment. However, it is preferable and more cautious to delay these until night if possible, as the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said:

> «دَعْ مَا يَرِيبُكَ إِلَى مَا لَا يَرِيبُكَ».

“Leave what you doubt for what you do not doubt.”

Moreover, the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said:

> «مَنِ اتَّقَى الشُّبُهَاتِ فَقَدِ اسْتَبْرَأَ لِدِينِهِ وَعِرْضِهِ».

“Whoever avoids doubtful matters, has indeed cleared his liability regarding his religion and honor.”

Among the matters whose ruling is unknown to some people is the lack of tranquility in prayer, whether obligatory or voluntary. Authentic Hadīths from the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) indicate that

---

## Page 24

tranquility is a pillar of prayer, without which the prayer is invalid. It involves stillness in prayer, Khushū‘ (humility and focus), and avoiding haste until each joint returns to its place. Many people perform Tarāweih prayer (voluntary night prayer in Ramadan) without understanding it or achieving tranquility, rather pecking through it. Such a prayer, in this manner, is invalid, and its performer is sinful and not rewarded.

Among the matters whose ruling may be unclear to some people is the belief held by some that Tarāweih cannot be less than twenty Rak‘ahs (unit of prayer), while others think it cannot exceed eleven or thirteen Rak‘ahs. All of this is a misconception and an error contrary to the evidence.

Authentic Hadiths from the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) indicate that the night prayer is flexible, with no fixed limit that must not be exceeded. It is authentically reported that he (صلى الله عليه وسلم) would pray eleven Rak‘ahs at night, sometimes thirteen Rak‘ahs, and sometimes less than that, both in Ramadan and outside of it. When asked about the night prayer, he said:

> «مَثْنَى مَثْنَى، فَإِذَا خَشِيَ أَحَدُكُمُ الصُّبْحَ صَلَّى رَكْعَةً وَاحِدَةً تُوتِرُ لَهُ مَا قَدْ صَلَّى».

“Two and two, and if any of you fears the approach of dawn, let him offer one Rak‘ah as Witr for what he has prayed.” [Its authenticity is agreed

---

## Page 25

upon]

He did not specify a certain number of Rak‘ahs, neither in Ramadan nor outside it. For this reason, the Companions during the time of ‘Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) sometimes prayed twenty-three Rak‘ahs and at other times eleven Rak‘ahs. All of this has been authentically reported from ‘Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) and from the Companions during his era.

Some of the righteous predecessors used to offer thirty-six Rak‘ahs in Ramadan and perform Witr with three Rak‘ahs, while others would offer forty-one Rak‘ahs. This was mentioned by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah and other scholars. He (may Allah have mercy upon him) also stated that there is a flexibility in this matter. He further mentioned that it is preferable for those who prolong the recitation, bowing, and prostration to reduce the number of Rak‘ahs, and for those who shorten the recitation, bowing, and prostration to increase the number. This is the essence of his words, may Allah have mercy upon him.

Whoever contemplates the Sunnah of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم), will know that the best practice in all of this is to offer eleven or thirteen Rak‘ahs in Ramadan and at other times, as this aligns with the practice of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) in most of his circumstances. It is also more considerate for the worshipers and closer to achieving humility and

---

## Page 26

tranquility. There is no harm or dislike for those who increase beyond this, as previously mentioned.

It is preferable for one who prays Qiyām with the Imam during Ramadan not to leave until the Imam finishes, as the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said:

> «إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ إِذَا قَامَ مَعَ الْإِمَامِ حَتَّى يَنْصَرِفَ كَتَبَ اللهُ لَهُ قِيَامَ لَيْلَةٍ».

“Indeed, when a man performs Qiyām along with the Imam until he (the Imam) leaves, Allah shall record for him the reward of Qiyām for one whole night.”

It is prescribed for all Muslims to strive in various forms of worship during this blessed month, including performing voluntary prayers, reciting the Qur’an with reflection and understanding, increasing in Tasbīh (glorification), Tahlīl (proclamation of Allah’s oneness), Tahmīd (praise), Takbīr (proclamation of Allah’s greatness), seeking forgiveness, and making lawful supplications. Additionally, enjoining good and forbidding evil, calling others to Allah, comforting the poor and needy, striving in dutifulness to parents, maintaining kinship ties, honoring neighbors, visiting the sick, and other acts of goodness are encouraged, as the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said in the aforementioned Hadīth:

> «يَنْظُرُ اللهُ إِلَى تَنَافُسِكُمْ فِيهِ، فَيُبَاهِي بِكُمْ مَلَائِكَتَهُ؛ فَأَرُوا اللهَ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ خَيْرًا، فَإِنَّ الشَّقِيَّ مَنْ حُرِمَ فِيهِ رَحْمَةَ اللهِ».

---

## Page 27

“Allah looks at your competition in it and boasts of you to His angels; so let Allah see something good from yourselves, for indeed, the miserable one is he who is deprived of Allah’s mercy in it.”

Moreover, it is narrated from him (صلى الله عليه وسلم) that he said:

> «مَنْ تَقَرَّبَ فِيهِ بِخَصْلَةٍ مِنْ خِصَالِ الْخَيْرِ كَانَ كَمَنْ أَدَّى فَرِيضَةً فِيمَا سِوَاهُ، وَمَنْ أَدَّى فِيهِ فَرِيضَةً كَانَ كَمَنْ أَدَّى سَبْعِينَ فَرِيضَةً فِيمَا سِوَاهُ».

“Whoever draws close in it with a good deed, it will be as if he has performed an obligatory act in other times, and whoever performs an obligatory act in it, it will be as if he has performed seventy obligatory acts in other times.”

The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) also said in the authentic Hadīth:

> «عُمْرَةٌ فِي رَمَضَانَ تَعْدِلُ حَجَّةً، أَوْ قَالَ: حَجَّةً مَعِي».

“‘Umrah in Ramadan is equivalent to Hajj–or he said: Hajj with me.”

The Hadīths and reports indicating the legitimacy of racing and competing in various acts of goodness during this blessed month are numerous.

---

## Page 28

We ask Allah Almighty to grant us and all Muslims success in all that pleases Him, to accept our fasting and Qiyām, to rectify our affairs, and to protect us all from the trials that lead us astray. We also ask Him, Glorified is He, to reform the Muslims’ leaders and unite their word upon the truth. Indeed, He is the Guardian of that and Capable of it.

And may the peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you all.

# Two Concise Treatises on Zakah and Fasting

**His Eminence Shaykh**  
**‘Abdul-‘Azīz bin ‘Abdullah bin Bāz**  
*(May Allah have mercy upon him)*

---

## The First Treatise: Important Researches on Zakah

All praise is due to Allah Alone, and may Allah’s peace and blessings be upon the one after whom there is no prophet, and upon his family and Companions. To proceed:

The motivation for writing this discourse is to offer advice and remind Muslims about the obligation of Zakah, which many Muslims have neglected and have not fulfilled in the prescribed manner, despite its great importance and being one of the five pillars of Islam without which its structure cannot stand, as per the Hadīth of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم):

> «بُنِيَ الإِسْلاَمُ عَلَى خَمْسٍ: شَهَادَةِ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللهِ، وَإِقَامِ الصَّلاَةِ، وَإِيتَاءِ الزَّكَاةِ، وَصَوْمِ رَمَضَانَ، وَحَجِّ الْبَيْتِ».
> 
> “Islam was built on five (pillars): testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing prayer, giving Zakah, fasting Ramadan, and pilgrimage to the House.”[^1]

[^1]: Narrated by Al-Bukhāri, no. (8) and Muslim, no. (16).

The obligation of Zakah on Muslims is one of the most evident virtues of Islam, demonstrating its care for the affairs of its followers due to its numerous benefits and the dire need of the poor Muslims for it.

### Spiritual and Social Benefits of Zakah

*   **Strengthening Social Bonds:** It strengthens the bonds of affection between the rich and the poor, for souls are naturally inclined to love those who do good to them.
*   **Purification of the Soul:** It purifies and refines the soul, distancing it from the traits of stinginess and miserliness, as the Noble Qur'an alludes to this meaning in His Almighty saying:
    > ﴿خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِم بِهَا...﴾
    > 
    > {Take charity from their wealth to cleanse and purify them...} [Surat at-Tawbah: 103].
*   **Cultivating Generosity:** It trains the Muslim with qualities of generosity, kindness, and compassion towards those in need.
*   **Attracting Divine Blessings:** It brings blessing, increase, and recompense from Allah, as He Almighty says:
    > ﴿...وَمَا أَنفَقْتُم مِّن شَيْءٍ فَهُوَ يُخْلِفُهُۥۖ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ ٱلرَّٰزِقِينَ﴾
    > 
    > {Whatever you spend in charity, He will compensate for it, for He is the Best of Providers.} [Surat Saba’: 39] 

In an authentic Hadīth, the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: “Allah Almighty says:
> «يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ أَنْفِقْ أُنْفِقْ عَلَيْكَ...».
> 
> “O son of Adam, spend, and We will spend on you...”[^2]

[^2]: Narrated by Muslim, no. (993).

### Warning Against Withholding Zakah

A stern warning has been issued regarding those who are stingy with it or fall short in giving it. Allah Almighty says:

> ﴿...وَالَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ الذَّهَبَ وَالْفِضَّةَ وَلَا يُنفِقُونَهَا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ ﴿٣٤﴾ يَوْمَ يُحْمَىٰ عَلَيْهَا فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ فَتُكْوَىٰ بِهَا جِبَاهُهُمْ وَجُنُوبُهُمْ وَظُهُورُهُمْ ۖ هَٰذَا مَا كَنَزْتُمْ لِأَنفُسِكُمْ فَذُوقُوا مَا كُنتُمْ تَكْنِزُونَ ﴿٣٥﴾﴾
> 
> {Those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah, give them tidings of a painful punishment. On the Day when their treasures will be heated up in the Fire of Hell, and their foreheads, sides and backs will be branded therewith. [They will be told], “This is what you hoarded for yourselves; so taste [the punishment of] what you used to hoard.”} [Surat at-Tawbah: 34-35]

Every wealth whose Zakah is not paid is a treasure with which its owner will be punished on the Day of Judgment, as indicated by the authentic Hadīth from the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم), who said:

> «مَا مِنْ صَاحِبِ ذَهَبٍ وَلَا فِضَّةٍ لَا يُؤَدِّي حَقَّهَا إِلَّا إِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ صُفِّحَتْ لَهُ صَفَائِحُ مِنْ نَارٍ، فَأُحْمِيَ عَلَيْهَا فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ، فَيُكْوَى بِهَا جَنْبُهُ وَجَبِينُهُ وَظَهْرُهُ كُلَّمَا بَرَدَتْ أُعِيدَتْ لَهُ فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ حَتَّى يُقْضَى بَيْنَ الْعِبَادِ، فَيُرَى سَبِيلُهُ: إِمَّا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ، وَإِمَّا إِلَى النَّارِ».
> 
> “There is no owner of gold or silver who does not pay what is due on it except that on the Day of Judgment they will be made for him sheets of fire and will be heated in the fire of Hell. His side, forehead, and back will be branded with them. Whenever they cool down, they will be heated again on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is pronounced among the creation, and he will be shown his path, either to Paradise or to Hellfire.”[^3]

[^3]: Narrated by Muslim, no. (987).

The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) then mentioned the owner of camels, cows, and sheep who does not pay their Zakah, and he informed that he will be tormented with them on the Day of Judgment. 

Furthermore, the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) is authentically reported to have said:

> «مَنْ آتَاهُ اللهُ مَالًا فَلَمْ يُؤَدِّ زَكَاتَهُ مُثِّلَ لَهُ شُجَاعًا أَقْرَعَ لَهُ زَبِيبَتَانِ يُطَوَّقُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، ثُمَّ يَأْخُذُ بِلِهْزِمَتَيْهِ (يَعْنِي شِدْقَيْهِ)، ثُمَّ يَقُولُ: أَنَا مَالُكَ، أَنَا كَنْزُكَ»
> 
> “If Allah gives wealth to anyone and he does not pay its Zakah, his wealth will be made to appear to him as a bald-headed snake with two black spots over its eyes. It will encircle his neck on the Day of Judgment, and it will seize his jaws (i.e., his cheeks), then say: ‘I am your wealth; I am your treasure.’"

Then, the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) recited the verse: 

> {Those who greedily withhold what Allah has given them of His grace should not think that it is good for them; rather, it is bad for them; their necks will be chained by what they greedily withheld on the Day of Resurrection...} [Surat Āl ‘Imrān: 180][^4].

[^4]: Narrated by Al-Bukhāri, no. (1338).

### Categories Subject to Zakah and Their Nisāb

Zakah is obligatory on four categories:
1.  **The produce of the earth** (grains and fruits).
2.  **Sā’imah** (freely-grazing) livestock.
3.  **Gold and silver**.
4.  **Merchandise** (commercial goods).

Each of these four categories has a specific *Nisāb* (minimum Zakatable amount), below which Zakah is not obligatory.

#### 1. Produce of the Earth
*   The Nisāb for grains and fruits is five *Wasqs*. Each Wasq is sixty *Sā‘s* according to the Sā‘ of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم).
*   This applies to dates, raisins, wheat, rice, barley, and similar items, totaling three hundred Sā‘s (equivalent to four handfuls by the hands of a man of average build when both hands are full).
*   **Rate Due:**
    *   **One-tenth (10%)** is due if the crops are irrigated without expenses (e.g., by rain, rivers, flowing springs).
    *   **Half of one-tenth (5%)** is due if irrigated with expenses and labor (e.g., by water-lifting devices and machines).

#### 2. Freely-Grazing Livestock
The Nisāb for freely-grazing camels, cows, and sheep is detailed in the authentic Hadīths. Due to space constraints and the pursuit of brevity, the specific matrices are omitted, and readers are referred to the people of knowledge for elaborate calculations.

#### 3. Gold, Silver, and Currency
*   **Silver Nisāb:** One hundred and forty *Mithqāls*, which is equivalent to fifty-six Saudi Arabian silver dirhams.
*   **Gold Nisāb:** Twenty *Mithqāls*, equivalent to 11 and 3/7 Saudi gold pounds, or 92 grams.
*   **Zakah Rate:** One-fourth of one-tenth (2.5%) after a *Hawl* (lunar year) has passed over it.
*   **Subordinates:** Profit is subordinate to the principal and does not require a new lunar year to elapse, just as offspring of livestock are subordinate to the principal Nisāb.
*   **Banknotes:** Modern banknotes (dirham, dinar, dollar, etc.) take the ruling of gold and silver. Once their valuation reaches the equivalent Nisāb of either gold or silver, and a year has passed, Zakah (2.5%) becomes due.

#### 4. Women's Jewelry
Women's jewelry made of gold or silver is treated like money, especially if it reaches the Nisāb and a lunar year has elapsed. Zakah is due on it, even if it is intended for personal use or lending, according to the most correct of the two scholarly opinions. 

This is supported by the general statement of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم):
> “There is no owner of gold or silver who does not pay its Zakah except that on the Day of Resurrection they will be made for him sheets of fire.”[^5]

[^5]: Narrated by Muslim, no. (987).

Additionally, it is authentically reported that the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) saw a woman wearing two gold bracelets, and he said:
> “Do you give Zakah on this?” She said: “No.” He said: “Would it please you that Allah adorns you with two bracelets of fire on the Day of Judgment because of them?” So, she threw them away and said: “They are for Allah and His Messenger.”[^6]

[^6]: Narrated by Abu Dāwūd, no. (1563), and An-Nasā’i, no. (2270), with a Hasan (sound) chain of narration.

It is also reported that ’Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her) used to wear gold ornaments and asked, “O Messenger of Allah, is this hoarded wealth (*Kanz*)?” He replied:
> «مَا بَلَغَ أَنْ يُزَكَّى فَزُكِّيَ فَلَيْسَ بِكَنْزٍ».
> 
> “Whatever reaches the amount liable for Zakah and its Zakah is paid is not considered hoarded wealth.”[^7]

[^7]: Narrated by Abu Dāwūd, no. (1564).

#### 5. Commercial Goods and Real Estate
*   **Merchandise:** Items prepared for sale should be evaluated at current market prices at the end of the lunar year, and 2.5% of their value must be paid, whether the value is equal to, more than, or less than the original purchase price. This is based on the Hadīth of Samurah (may Allah be pleased with him):
    > “The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) used to command us to give charity from what we prepare for sale.”[^8]
    > This includes lands, buildings, cars, water-lifting machines, and other goods prepared for resale.
*   **Rental Property:** Real estate prepared for rental purposes is not subject to Zakah on the property's intrinsic value. Rather, Zakah is due on the rental income accumulated, provided it reaches the Nisāb and a lunar year passes over it.
*   **Personal Property:** Private vehicles and properties intended for personal use are exempt from Zakah.
*   **General Assets:** If a taxi driver or any business owner accumulates cash that reaches the Nisāb, Zakah is obligatory upon the completion of a lunar year, regardless of whether the money was set aside for expenses, marriage, asset acquisition, or debt repayment.

[^8]: Narrated by Abu Dāwūd, no. (1562).

### Crucial Administrative Rulings of Zakah
*   **Debts and Zakah:** The correct scholarly view is that outstanding debts do not prevent the obligation of paying Zakah on the cash assets in one's possession.
*   **Orphans and the Mentally Incapacitated:** The wealth of orphans and those with mental disabilities is subject to Zakah. Their legal guardians must calculate and pay the Zakah from their assets upon the completion of each lunar year.
*   **Recipient Verification:** Zakah is a divine right, and it is strictly prohibited to show favoritism by giving it to those who do not qualify, or to use it for personal benefit, self-protection, or to avert blame. It must be paid solely to the eight categories decreed by Allah in the Qur'an:

> ﴿إِنَّمَا الصَّدَقَاتُ لِلْفُقَرَاءِ وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَالْعَامِلِينَ عَلَيْهَا وَالْمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَفِي الرِّقَابِ وَالْغَارِمِينَ وَفِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ ۖ فَرِيضَةً مِّنَ اللَّهِ ۗ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ ﴿٦٠﴾﴾
> 
> {Alms [i.e., Zakah] is only for the poor and the needy; those in charge of it; those whose hearts may be attracted [to Islam]; for freeing those in bondage; for those in debt; for the cause of Allah; and for [the stranded] traveler – as ordained by Allah, for Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.} [Surat at-Tawbah: 60]

The conclusion of this verse with Allah’s names, "the All-Knowing, All-Wise," serves as a reminder that He knows who is truly deserving of charity, and His legislation is built on complete wisdom, putting all funds in their rightful place.

We ask Allah Almighty to guide us and the Muslims to understand His religion properly, to be sincere in our dealings with Him, to hasten towards what pleases Him, and to keep away from what incurs His wrath.

---

## The Second Treatise: The Merit of Fasting and Qiyām during Ramadan

From ‘Abdul-‘Azīz ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Bāz to those among the Muslims who observe it—may Allah guide me and them to the path of the people of faith, and grant me and them understanding of the Sunnah and the Qur’an, Amen.

And may Allah’s peace, mercy, and blessings be upon you.

### Virtues of the Month of Ramadan
It is authentically reported that the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) used to give glad tidings to his Companions about the coming of the month of Ramadan, informing them that the gates of mercy and Paradise are opened, the gates of Hellfire are closed, and the devils are chained. He would say:

> “When the first night of Ramadan arrives, the gates of Paradise are opened, and not a single gate is closed; the gates of Hellfire are closed, and not a single gate is opened; the devils are chained, and a caller announces: 'O seeker of good, come forward, and O seeker of evil, desist.' And Allah will free some people from Hellfire, and that is every night.”

He (صلى الله عليه وسلم) also said:

> “Ramadan has come to you, a month of blessings in which Allah envelops you: He sends down mercy, absolves sins, and answers supplications. Allah observes your competition in it and boasts of you to His angels; so let Allah see something good from yourselves, for indeed, the miserable one is he who is deprived of Allah’s mercy in it.”

And:

> “Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward from Allah will have his past sins forgiven; and whoever performs Qiyām during Ramadan, faithfully and expecting its reward from Allah, will have his past sins forgiven; and whoever offers Qiyām during the Night of Qadr (Decree), faithfully and expecting its reward from Allah, will have his past sins forgiven.”

And:

> “Allah says: 'Every deed of the son of Adam is for him; a good deed is multiplied ten times up to seven hundred times, except for fasting, which is for Me, and I give the reward for it. He leaves his desires, food, and drink for My sake.' The fasting person has two joys: one when he breaks his fast, and another when he meets his Lord. Indeed, the smell of the mouth of a fasting person is more pleasant to Allah than the fragrance of musk.”

### Obligations of the Believer During Ramadan

A believer must seize this magnificent opportunity to hasten toward righteous deeds and completely avoid sins.

#### 1. Preservation of the Five Daily Prayers
The daily prayers are the pillar of Islam and the greatest of obligations after the two testimonies of faith. It is incumbent upon every Muslim to observe them at their prescribed times with humility and tranquility. Men must pray in congregation in the mosques, as commanded by Allah:

> ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ وَارْكَعُوا مَعَ الرَّاكِعِينَ ﴿٤٣﴾﴾
> 
> {And establish prayer, give Zakah, and bow [to Allah] with those who bow.} [Surat al-Baqarah: 43]

The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said:
> «الْعَهْدُ الَّذِي بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُمُ الصَّلَاةُ فَمَنْ تَرَكَهَا فَقَدْ كَفَرَ».
> 
> “The covenant between us and them is the prayer; whoever abandons it has disbelieved.”

#### 2. Guarding the Fast from Forbidden Matters
Fasting is not merely abstaining from food, drink, and intimacy; its true purpose is to submit to Allah, discipline the soul, and practice patience in avoiding prohibitions. The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said:

> «الصِّيَامُ جُنَّةٌ، فَإِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ صَوْمِ أَحَدِكُمْ فَلَا يَرْفُثْ وَلَا يَصْخَبْ، فَإِنْ سَابَّهُ أَحَدٌ أَوْ قَاتَلَهُ فَلْيَقُلْ: إِنِّي صَائِمٌ».
> 
> “Fasting is a shield. When any of you is fasting, he should avoid obscene language and loud voice, and if anyone curses him or quarrels with him, he should say: I am fasting.”

He (صلى الله عليه وسلم) also said:
> «مَنْ لَمْ يَدَعْ قَوْلَ الزُّورِ وَالْعَمَلَ بِهِ وَالْجَهْلَ فَلَيْسَ لِلَّهِ حَاجَةٌ فِي أَنْ يَدَعَ طَعَامَهُ وَشَرَابَهُ».
> 
> “Whoever does not give up false speech and acting upon it and does not abandon foolishness, Allah is in no need of him giving up his food and drink.”

### Rulings and Misconceptions Concerning Fasting

#### 1. Involuntary Incidents
The following occurrences **do not** invalidate the fast:
*   Accidental wounds or injuries.
*   Nosebleeds.
*   Involuntary vomiting.
*   Accidentally swallowing water or gasoline without choice.
*   *Note on deliberate vomiting:* If a person vomits intentionally, their fast is broken. The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said:
    > “Whoever is overcome by vomiting is not required to make up, but whoever vomits intentionally must make up.”

#### 2. Delaying the Ritual Bath (Ghusl)
*   If a person is in a state of *Janābah* (major ritual impurity) or a woman's menstruation/post-partum bleeding ceases before dawn, they may initiate their fast and delay taking their Ghusl until after dawn has broken.
*   However, they must not delay Ghusl until sunrise; they are obligated to bathe and perform the Fajr prayer in its proper time.

#### 3. Medical Injections and Blood Tests
*   **Blood Tests:** Do not invalidate the fast.
*   **Injections:** Routine therapeutic injections (non-nutritive) do not break the fast. However, delaying them until nightfall is highly encouraged as a precautionary measure to preserve the integrity of worship.

#### 4. The Principle of Tranquility in Prayer (Tarāwīh and Obligatory)
*   Tranquility (*Tuma'nīnah*) and focus (*Khushū‘*) are essential pillars of prayer. 
*   Many people rush through the Tarāwīh prayer, pecking like birds without proper bowing, prostrating, or standing still. A prayer performed in such a hasty manner is **invalid**, and the person is sinful rather than rewarded.

#### 5. Flexibility in the Number of Rak‘ahs for Tarāwīh
There is a widespread misconception that Tarāwīh must be exactly twenty Rak‘ahs, or that it cannot exceed eleven or thirteen Rak‘ahs. 

The authentic Sunnah shows that the night prayer is highly flexible and has no strict upper or lower limit:
*   The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) prayed eleven or thirteen Rak‘ahs in most cases, both within and outside of Ramadan.
*   When asked about the night prayer, he (صلى الله عليه وسلم) replied:
    > «مَثْنَى مَثْنَى، فَإِذَا خَشِيَ أَحَدُكُمُ الصُّبْحَ صَلَّى رَكْعَةً وَاحِدَةً تُوتِرُ لَهُ مَا قَدْ صَلَّى».
    > 
    > “Two and two, and if any of you fears the approach of dawn, let him offer one Rak‘ah as Witr for what he has prayed.”
*   During the caliphate of ‘Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), the Companions prayed twenty-three Rak‘ahs in some instances and eleven in others.
*   The righteous predecessors (*Salaf*) varied greatly: some prayed thirty-six Rak‘ahs with three Witr, while others performed forty-one. 
*   Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah clarified that if a person prolongs the recitation, bowing, and prostrations, it is preferable to perform fewer Rak‘ahs (e.g., eleven or thirteen). If they shorten the physical components, they may increase the number of Rak‘ahs to compensate. Both approaches are valid.

#### 6. Remaining with the Imam until the End
It is highly recommended for the worshiper to complete the entire Tarāwīh service with the Imam until he departs, as the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said:
> “Indeed, when a man performs Qiyām along with the Imam until he leaves, Allah shall record for him the reward of Qiyām for one whole night.”

### Encouraged Good Deeds in Ramadan
Muslims are encouraged to excel in diverse forms of worship:
*   Voluntary prayers and constant Qur'anic recitation with reflection.
*   Adhkar (remembrance): *Tasbīh*, *Tahlīl*, *Tahmīd*, and *Takbīr*.
*   Calling to Allah, enjoining good, and forbidding evil.
*   Acts of social solidarity: feeding the poor, maintaining family ties, honoring neighbors, and visiting the sick.
*   **Performing 'Umrah:** The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said:
    > “‘Umrah in Ramadan is equivalent to Hajj–or he said: Hajj with me.”

We ask Allah Almighty to grant us and all Muslims success in all that pleases Him, to accept our fasting and Qiyām, to rectify our affairs, and to protect us all from trials that lead us astray.

*May the peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you all.*

qa_dataset.answer: The author presents a chronological and contextual abrogation argument. The initial instruction to cut leather socks below the ankles was delivered by the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) while in Madīnah when asked about the general rules of Ihram clothing. However, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, while addressing the massive congregation at the plains of 'Arafāt, the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) publicly permitted wearing leather socks if sandals were unavailable, yet did not mention the requirement to cut them. Because many individuals present at 'Arafāt had not heard the earlier instruction in Madīnah, and because delaying a vital clarification beyond the time of need is legally impermissible (*la yajūz ta'khīr al-bayan 'an waqt al-hājah*), the absolute permission at 'Arafāt without the cutting condition establishes that the requirement to cut the socks was officially abrogated.
qa_dataset.question: What legal-methodological (Usūli) argument is presented to prove that the Prophetic command to cut leather socks (Khuff) below the ankles in the absence of sandals has been abrogated?

qa_dataset.answer: The author argues that actions must be evaluated based on the capacity and legal status of the individual. During his earthly life, the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) was physically alive and capable of making supplication (*Du'ā*) on behalf of another, which is the essence of seeking intercession in this world. After death, however, a person enters the life of the *Barzakh*. According to authentic Hadith, when a person dies, all their deeds cease except for three specified categories. Asking the deceased for intercession, healing, or relief is an act of worship directed toward someone who no longer possesses the worldly agency to act or supplicate on demand. Seeking such spiritual intervention from the dead is the exact practice of the pre-Islamic polytheists (*Jāhiliyyah*), who invoked intermediaries with the claim that they merely seek closeness to Allah, thereby violating the fundamental Islamic principle of directing all worship, supplication, and hope exclusively to Allah.

During the stoning, the pebbles must fall directly into the designated basin surrounding the stoning pillar; they do not need to remain there, but they must land in it. On the Day of Nahr (10th of Dhul-Hijjah), the stoning of Jamrat al-'Aqabah begins after sunrise (or late night for the weak and excused). For the three subsequent days of Tashrīq (11th, 12th, and 13th), the stoning of all three Jamarat must take place strictly after the sun passes its zenith (*Zawāl*). Stoning before noon on these days is invalid. Additionally, the correct sequence must be maintained: starting with the first Jamrah (nearest to Al-Khayf Mosque), then the middle Jamrah, and finally the third Jamrah (Jamrat al-'Aqabah).

He should document what he owes and what is owed to him, and take witnesses for that. He must hasten to repent sincerely from all sins, as Allah Almighty says: $$\{...وَتُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ\}$$ >{And turn to Allah in repentance all together, O [^11]: Narrated by An-Nasā’i, no. (2620). [^12]: Narrated by Al-Bukhāri, no. (1773) and Muslim, no. (1349).

If he has no good deeds, then some of that person's bad deeds will be taken and loaded upon him."[^13] He should select for his Hajj and ‘Umrah a pure expenditure from lawful earnings, as it is authentically reported that the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: «إِنَّ اللهَ تَعَالَى طَيِّبٌ لَا يَقْبَلُ إِلَّا طَيِّبًا».
