# The Ruling on Magic, Divination, and Related Matters

**English | إنجليزي**

---

### بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ

Praise be to Allah Alone, and may Allah’s peace and blessings be upon the one after whom there is no prophet. To proceed:

In view of the recent proliferation of charlatans who claim to practice medicine and treat through magic or divination, and their spread in some countries, exploiting the naïve among people who are predominantly ignorant, I deemed it necessary, as sincere advice for the sake of Allah Almighty and His servants, to clarify the great danger this poses to Islam and Muslims, as it involves reliance on other than Allah Almighty and contravenes His command and the command of His Messenger (ﷺ).

I say, seeking the help of Allah Almighty, that seeking treatment is unanimously permissible. A Muslim may consult a doctor specializing in internal medicine, surgery, neurology, or similar fields to diagnose his illness and treat it with medications that are lawfully permissible according to Shariah, based on the knowledge of medicine. This is part of utilizing ordinary means and does not conflict with reliance on Allah Almighty. Indeed, Allah Almighty has sent down both the disease and its cure; those who know it recognize it, and those who are ignorant of it remain unaware. However, He Almighty has not placed the healing of His servants in what He has prohibited for them.

It is not permissible for a sick person to go to soothsayers who claim to know the unseen to learn about his illness, nor is it permissible for him to believe what they tell him, as they speak conjectures about the unseen or summon jinn to assist them in what they want. The ruling on these individuals is that they are upon disbelief and misguidance if they claim knowledge of the unseen.

Muslim narrated in his Sahīh Collection that the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

> «مَنْ أَتَى عَرَّافًا فَسَأَلَهُ عَنْ شَيْءٍ، لَمْ تُقْبَلْ لَهُ صَلَاةٌ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا».
>
> “Whoever goes to a diviner and asks him about something, his prayer will not be accepted for forty days.”

And on the authority of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

> «مَنْ أَتَى كَاهِنًا فَصَدَّقَهُ بِمَا يَقُولُ، فَقَدْ كَفَرَ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ».
>
> “Whoever goes to a Kāhin (soothsayer) and believes what he says has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ).”

Narrated by Abu Dāwūd, and by the authors of the four Sunan Compilations, and Al-Hākim classified it as Sahīh (authentic), from the Prophet (ﷺ) with the wording:

> «مَنْ أَتَى عَرَّافًا أَوْ كَاهِنًا فَصَدَّقَهُ بِمَا يَقُولُ، فَقَدْ كَفَرَ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ».
>
> “Whoever goes to a ‘Arrāf (diviner) or a Kāhin (soothsayer) and believes what he says has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad.”

‘Imrān ibn Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

> «لَيْسَ مِنَّا مَنْ تَطَيَّرَ أَوْ تُطُيِّرَ لَهُ، أَوْ تَكَهَّنَ أَوْ تُكُهِّنَ لَهُ، أَوْ سَحَرَ أَوْ سُحِرَ لَهُ، وَمَنْ أَتَى كَاهِنًا فَصَدَّقَهُ بِمَا يَقُولُ، فَقَدْ كَفَرَ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ».
>
> “He is not one of us who seeks omens or has omens interpreted for him, or who practices soothsaying or has it done for him, or who practices sorcery or has it done for him. And whoever goes to a soothsayer and believes in what he says has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ).” [Narrated by Al-Bazzār with a good Isnād]

In these noble Hadīths, there is a prohibition against going to diviners, soothsayers, magicians, and their like, asking them questions, and believing them, and therein lies the warning against such actions.

It is not permissible to be deceived by their truthfulness in some matters or by the large number of people who come to them, as they are ignorant, and people should not be misled by them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has forbidden approaching, asking, or believing them due to the great evil, severe danger, and dire consequences involved, as they are deceitful liars.

These Hadīths also provide evidence for the disbelief of the soothsayer and magician, as they claim knowledge of the unseen, which is disbelief. Moreover, they achieve their aims only by serving the jinn and worshiping them instead of Allah Almighty, which is disbelief in Allah and associating partners with Him, Exalted be He. Whoever believes them in their claim to know the unseen is like them, and anyone who receives these matters from those who practice them has been disavowed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Also, it is not permissible for a Muslim to submit to what they claim as treatment, such as their use of talismans or pouring lead, and other such superstitions they practice. This is considered soothsaying and deception of the people. Whoever is content with this has aided them in their falsehood and disbelief.

It is also not permissible for any Muslim to go to them to inquire about whom his son or relative will marry, or about matters between spouses and their families, such as love and loyalty or enmity and separation, and the like. This is because it is part of the unseen that no one knows except Allah Almighty.

It is incumbent upon the rulers, the people of Hisbah (vice control), and others who possess power and authority to denounce the act of going to soothsayers and diviners and their like, to prevent anyone from engaging in such practices in the markets and elsewhere, to express the strongest disapproval of them, and to denounce those who come to them.

Similarly, magic is among the prohibited acts of disbelief, as Allah Almighty says regarding the two angels:

> ﴿... وَمَا يُعَلِّمَانِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌ فَلَا تَكْفُرْ ۖ فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنْهُمَا مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِ ۚ وَمَا هُم بِضَارِّينَ بِهِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ ۚ وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مَا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلَا يَنفَعُهُمْ ۚ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُوا لَمَنِ اشْتَرَاهُ مَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ ۚ وَلَبِئْسَ مَا شَرَوْا بِهِ أَنفُسَهُمْ ۚ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾
>
> {But these two angels did not teach anyone without telling them, “We are only a test, so do not disbelieve.” Yet they would learn from them what would cause separation between a man and his wife. But they could not harm anyone except by Allah’s permission. They would learn what harmed them and did not benefit them, although they already knew that whoever gets into it would not have any share in the Hereafter. How terrible was the price for which they sold themselves, if only they knew!} [Surat al-Baqarah: 102]

These noble verses indicate that sorcery is disbelief and that sorcerers cause separation between a man and his wife. They also show that sorcery cannot cause benefit or harm by itself, but is only effective by Allah’s universal will and predestination, because Allah Almighty is the One Who created both good and evil.

The noble verse also indicates that those who learn magic only learn what harms them and does not benefit them and that they have no share with Allah Almighty. This is a severe warning that signifies their great loss in this world and the Hereafter, and that they have sold themselves for the lowest price. Thus, Allah Almighty reproached them for this by saying:

> ﴿... وَلَبِئْسَ مَا شَرَوْا بِهِ أَنفُسَهُمْ ۚ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾
>
> {How terrible was the price for which they sold themselves, if only they knew!} [Surat al-Baqarah: 102]

*(The verse uses the Arabic term Shirā’ “buying” in the sense of selling).*

The harm has indeed become severe, and the situation has worsened due to these fabricators who inherited these sciences from the polytheists and confused the weak-minded with them. To Allah we belong and to Him we shall return. Allah is Sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.

We ask Allah Almighty for well-being and safety from the evils of sorcerers, soothsayers, and all other deceivers. We also implore Him, Glorified be He, to protect Muslims from their harm and guide the Muslim rulers to be vigilant regarding them and to enforce Allah's judgment upon them so that the people may be relieved from their harm and wicked deeds. Indeed, He is All-Generous, All-Kind.

Allah Almighty has legislated for His servants means of protecting themselves from the evil of magic before it occurs, and He, out of His mercy and benevolence towards them, has clarified the remedy for it after it has occurred, completing His favor upon them.

---

## Preventative Measures Against the Danger of Magic (Before It Occurs)

The most important and beneficial means of protection is fortifying oneself with the prescribed Adhkār, supplications, and transmitted protective invocations.

### 1. Reciting Ayah al-Kursī
Recite the verse of Kursī—the greatest verse in the Noble Qur’an—after every obligatory prayer following the Taslīm, and also before sleeping:

> ﴿اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَّهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ﴾
>
> {Allah: none has the right to be worshiped except Him, the Ever-Living, the All-Sustaining. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on earth. Who is there that can intercede with Him except with His permission? He knows what was before them and what will be after them, while they encompass nothing of His knowledge, except what He wills. His Kursī [i.e., footstool] extends over the heavens and earth, and safeguarding of both does not weary Him, for He is the Most High, the Most Great.} [Surat al-Baqarah: 255]

It has been authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said:
> «مَنْ قَرَأَ آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ فِي لَيْلَةٍ، لَمْ يَزَلْ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ اللَّهِ حَافِظٌ، وَلَا يَقْرَبُهُ شَيْطَانٌ حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ».
>
> “Whoever recites the verse of Kursī at night, he will still be guarded by Allah, and no devil will approach him until the morning.”

### 2. Reciting the Three Mu'awwidhat (Surahs of Protection)
Recite the following Surahs after every obligatory prayer, and repeat them three times at the beginning of the day (after Fajr) and at the beginning of the night (after Maghrib):
* **Surat al-Ikhlās:** `{Say: “He is Allah, the One;”}`
* **Surat al-Falaq:** `{Say, “I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak,”}`
* **Surat an-Nās:** `{Say, “I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind,”}`

### 3. Reciting the Last Two Verses of Surat al-Baqarah
Recite these verses at the beginning of the night:
> ﴿آمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِن رَّبِّهِ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ ۚ كُلٌّ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِّن رُّسُلِهِ ۚ وَقَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا ۖ غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾
>
> {The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, as do the believers. All of them believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, and His messengers...} [Surat al-Baqarah: 285-286]

The Prophet (ﷺ) said:
> «مَنْ قَرَأَ الآيَتَيْنِ مِنْ آخِرِ سُورَةِ البَقَرَةِ فِي لَيْلَةٍ كَفَتَاهُ».
>
> “Whoever recites the last two verses of Surat al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him.” *(Meaning: protect him from all harm).*

### 4. Seeking Refuge in Allah's Perfect Words
Frequently say this supplication during the day, night, and when alighting or staying in any place:
> «أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ».
>
> “A‘ūdhu bikalimātillāhi at-tammāti min sharri ma khalaq” (I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created).

The Prophet (ﷺ) said:
> «مَنْ نَزَلَ مَنْزِلًا فَقَالَ: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ، لَمْ يَضُرَّهُ شَيْءٌ حَتَّى يَرْتَحِلَ مِنْ مَنْزِلِهِ ذَلِكَ».
>
> “Whoever alights somewhere and says [this], nothing will harm him until he leaves that place.”

### 5. Prophetic Morning and Evening Supplication
Recite three times at the beginning of the day and night:
> «بِسْمِ اللهِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ، وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ».
>
> “Bismillāhi alladhi la yadurru ma‘a ismihi shay’un fil-ardi wala fi as-samā’i wa huwa as-samī‘ al-‘alīm” (In the Name of Allah, with Whose name nothing can cause harm on the earth or in the heaven and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing).

---

## Methods of Treating Magic (After Its Occurrence)

### Method 1: Supplication
Frequent supplication to Allah Almighty, asking Him to lift the harm and remove the affliction.

### Method 2: Finding and Destroying the Magic Physical Object
Exerting efforts to locate where the magical item has been hidden (e.g., in the ground, on a mountain, etc.). Once found, extracting and physically destroying it completely nullifies the magic. This is one of the most effective direct treatments.

### Method 3: Permissible Ruqyah (Spiritual Incantation)
The following formulas are established from Islamic tradition:

* **The Prophetic Ruqyah (Recited 3 times):**
  > «اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ النَّاسِ، أَذْهِبِ الْبَأْسَ، وَاشْفِ أَنْتَ الشَّافِي، لَا شِفَاءَ إِلَّا شِفَاؤُكَ، شِفَاءً لَا يُغَادِرُ سَقَمًا».
  >
  > “Allāhumma rabba an-nās adh'hib al-ba’s washfi anta ash-shāfi, lā shifā’ illa shifā’uk, shifā’an la yughādir saqama” (O Allah, the Lord of humankind, remove the disease and heal; You are the Healer; there is no cure but Yours, a cure that leaves behind no illness).

* **The Ruqyah of Gabriel (Jibrīl) (Recited 3 times):**
  > «بِسْمِ اللهِ أَرْقِيكَ، مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ يُؤْذِيكَ، وَمِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ نَفْسٍ أَوْ عَيْنِ حَاسِدٍ، اللهُ يَشْفِيكَ، بِسْمِ اللهِ أَرْقِيكَ».
  >
  > “Bismillāhi arqīk min kolli shay’in yu’dhīk wa min sharri kolli nafsin aw ‘aynin hāsidin Allāh yashfīk, bismillāhi arqīk” (In the Name of Allah, I recite Ruqyah over you, from everything that harms you, from the evil of every soul or envious eye. May Allah cure you. In the Name of Allah, I recite Ruqyah over you).

### Method 4: Lote Tree (Sidr) Treatment
This treatment is highly beneficial, particularly for a man who has been magically prevented from being intimate with his wife:
1. Take seven green leaves of the lote tree (Sidr).
2. Crush them with a stone or a similar object.
3. Place them in a container and pour enough water over them to bathe with.
4. Recite the following Surahs and verses over the water:
   * **Ayah al-Kursī** (Surat al-Baqarah: 255)
   * **Surat al-Kāfirūn**
   * **Surat al-Ikhlās**
   * **Surat al-Falaq**
   * **Surat an-Nās**
   * **Surat al-A‘rāf (Verses 117-119):**
     > ﴿وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ أَنْ أَلْقِ عَصَاكَ ۖ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَلْقَفُ مَا يَأْفِكُونَ * فَوَقَعَ الْحَقُّ وَبَطَلَ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ * فَغُلِبُوا هُنَالِكَ وَانقَلَبُوا صَاغِرِينَ﴾
     >
     > {We inspired Moses, “Throw your staff,” and it suddenly swallowed up all their illusionary devices. Thus, the truth prevailed, and all that they did was proven to be false. They were defeated right there and were utterly humiliated.}
   * **Surat Yūnus (Verses 79-82):**
     > ﴿وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ ائْتُونِي بِكُلِّ سَاحِرٍ عَلِيمٍ * فَلَمَّا جَاءَ السَّحَرَةُ قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰ أَلْقُوا مَا أَنتُم مُّلْقُونَ * فَلَمَّا أَلْقَوْا قَالَ مُوسَىٰ مَا جِئْتُم بِهِ السِّحْرُ ۖ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَيُبْطِلُهُ ۖ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُصْلِحُ عَمَلَ الْمُفْسِدِينَ * وَيُحِقُّ اللَّهُ الْحَقَّ بِكَلِمَاتِهِ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾
     >
     > {Pharaoh said, “Bring me all learned magicians.” ... Moses said, “All that you have brought is mere magic; Allah will surely make it useless...}
   * **Surat Tā-ha (Verses 65-69):**
     > ﴿قَالُوا يَا مُوسَىٰ إِمَّا أَن تُلْقِيَ وَإِمَّا أَن نَّكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَىٰ ... إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا كَيْدُ سَاحِرٍ ۖ وَلَا يُفْلِحُ السَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ﴾
     >
     > {... They have only contrived a magic trick, and the magician will never prosper, wherever he goes.”}
5. After completing the recitation over the water, the afflicted person should **drink three sips** of it, and **bathe with the remaining portion**.
6. If necessary, the process can be repeated until the symptoms are completely cured.

---

## Prohibited Remedies: Treatment via Sorcerers ("Nushrah")

A significant theological error is attempting to treat magic by employing other sorcerers or offering sacrifices and vows to the jinn. This is forbidden, as it is considered the work of Satan and constitutes major Shirk (associating partners with Allah).

It is also strictly forbidden to seek treatment from soothsayers, diviners, and charlatans, as they deny faith (Imān) and claim to possess knowledge of the unseen.

The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about **Nushrah** (counteracting magic by using magic), and he replied:
> «هِيَ مِنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطَانِ».
>
> “It is from the work of Satan.” [Narrated by Imam Ahmad and Abu Dāwūd, with a good Isnād]

This refers to the pre-Islamic practice where people asked a sorcerer to remove magic using another spell. However, removing magic through the legal Shar‘i Ruqyah, refuge-seeking invocations, and permissible natural remedies is perfectly acceptable and highly recommended, as affirmed by major scholars like Ibn al-Qayyim and Shaykh ‘Abdur-Rahmān ibn Hasan.

We ask Allah Almighty to grant Muslims safety from all harm, to preserve their religion for them, to bless them with an understanding of it, and to protect them from everything that contradicts His Shariah.

And may Allah’s peace and blessings be upon His slave and Messenger Muhammad, and his family and Companions.

qa_dataset.answer: The eight requirements of the testimony of faith are: 1) Knowledge that negates ignorance, 2) Certitude that negates doubt, 3) Sincerity that negates polytheism, 4) Truthfulness that negates falsehood, 5) Love that negates hatred, 6) Submission that negates abandonment, 7) Acceptance that negates rejection, and 8) Rejection (disbelief) of everything else that is worshipped besides Allah.
qa_dataset.question: What are the eight necessary requirements of the testimony of faith (La ilāha illa Allah) as detailed in the text?

qa_dataset.answer: The text classifies Shirk into three categories: Major Shirk, Minor Shirk, and Hidden Shirk. Major Shirk nullifies all of a person's good deeds and dooms them to eternal punishment in Hellfire if they die upon it without repentance. Minor Shirk (such as swearing by other than Allah, minor showing off in deeds, or using 'and' to link human and divine will) does not cause apostasy or eternal hellfire, but it severely compromises the obligatory perfection of Tawhid. Hidden Shirk (such as beautifying one's prayer because others are watching) can fall under either major or minor Shirk depending on the degree of intent, such as the major Shirk of hypocrites who conceal absolute disbelief.
qa_dataset.question: How does the text classify Shirk (polytheism), and what are the theological implications of each category?

qa_dataset.answer: The nine conditions are Islam, sanity, age of discernment, state of purity, removal of impurity, covering the 'awrah, commencement of prayer time, facing the Qiblah, and intention. The fourteen pillars are standing if able, opening Takbir, reciting Al-Fatihah, bowing, standing upright after bowing, prostration on seven body parts, rising from prostration, sitting between the two prostrations, tranquility in all actions, observing the proper sequence of pillars, the final Tashahhud, sitting for it, sending blessings upon the Prophet, and the two Taslims. The eight obligatory acts are all Takbirs other than the opening one, saying 'Sami'allahu liman hamidah' (Imam/individual), saying 'Rabbana wa laka al-hamd' (everyone), saying 'Subhana Rabbi Al-'Azhim' in bowing, saying 'Subhana Rabbi Al-A'la' in prostration, saying 'Rabbi ighfir li' between prostrations, the first Tashahhud, and sitting for it.
qa_dataset.question: Identify the nine conditions, fourteen pillars, and eight obligatory acts of prayer according to the text.

qa_dataset.answer: According to the author, merely touching a woman does not invalidate ablution under any circumstances, whether it occurs with desire or without, as long as no physical emission (such as Madhi or Mani) occurs. This is based on the prophetic practice where Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) kissed some of his wives and went directly to pray without performing a new ablution. The author clarifies that the Qur'anic phrase {...or had sexual contact with women...} in Surat an-Nisa and Surat al-Ma'idah refers specifically to actual sexual intercourse, which is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, the predecessors, and later scholars.
qa_dataset.question: Explain the ruling regarding touching a woman and its effect on state of ritual purity (Wudū’) as presented by the author.

qa_dataset.answer: For a male: 1) Cover his 'Awrah, press the abdomen gently, clean the private parts using a barrier cloth, perform a standard prayer ablution, and wash the head and beard with water and lote-leaves (Sidr). 2) Wash the right side, then the left, repeating 3 to 7 times. 3) Apply perfume to prostration points and incense the shroud. 4) Shroud him in three white wrapping sheets without a shirt or turban. For a female: The washing process is similar, but her hair must be braided into three braids and positioned behind her back. Her shroud is different, consisting of five distinct pieces: a shirt, a head veil, a lower garment (Izār), and two wrapping sheets.
qa_dataset.question: Describe the proper procedure for washing and shrouding a deceased Muslim male in comparison to a deceased Muslim female.

qa_dataset.answer: It is impermissible and forbidden for the family of the deceased to prepare food for the attendees, as companion Jarir ibn 'Abdullah al-Bajali stated that the companions considered gathering with the family of the deceased and making food after the burial to be a form of prohibited wailing (Niyahah). Instead, the correct Islamic practice is for the relatives and neighbors of the deceased's family to prepare food for them, as the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered food to be prepared for the family of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib when news of his death arrived, noting that they were preoccupied with their affliction.

### Lesson One: Surat al-Fātihah and the short Surahs

Surat al-Fātihah and as many of the short Surahs as possible, from Surat az-Zalzalah to Surat an-Nās, are to be learnt, corrected in recitation, memorized, and explained for what is obligatory to be understood.

### Lesson Two: The pillars of Islam

Explanation of the five pillars of Islam, the first and greatest of which is: Testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, with an explanation of its meanings, along with clarifying the requirements of “There is no god but Allah.” Its meaning is: “There is no god,” negating all that is worshiped besides Allah, “except Allah,” affirming worship to Allah alone, without a partner.

As for the requirements of “There is no god but Allah”, they are: knowledge that negates ignorance, certitude that negates doubt, sincerity that negates polytheism, truthfulness that negates falsehood, love that negates hatred, submission that negates abandonment, acceptance that negates rejection, and disbelief in what is worshipped besides Allah. They are summed up in the following two poetic verses:

> Knowledge, certainty, and your sincerity...along with love, submission, and its acceptance
> Then add the eighth, which is your rejection of...everything

### Lesson Three: The pillars of Imān (faith)

They are six: to believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and to believe that predestination, with its good and bad aspects, is from Allah Almighty.

### Lesson Four: Categories of Tawhīd and categories of Shirk

The clarification of the categories of Tawhīd, which are three: Tawhīd ar-Rubūbiyyah (the Oneness of Lordship), Tawhīd al-’Ulūhiyyah (the Oneness of worship), and Tawhīd al-Asmā’ wa as-Sifāt (the Oneness of Allah's names and attributes).

1. **Tawhīd ar-Rubūbiyyah (Oneness of Lordship):** It is to believe that Allah Almighty is the Creator of everything and the Disposer of all affairs, with no partner in that.
2. **Tawhīd al-’Ulūhiyyah (Oneness of worship):** It

### Lesson Five: Ihsān (Excellence in worship)

**The pillar of Ihsān:** It is to worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you cannot see Him, He indeed sees you.

### Lesson Six: Conditions of prayer

They are nine:

Islam, sanity, reaching the age of discernment, being in a state of ritual purity, removal of najāsah (tangible impurity), covering the ‘awrah (parts of the body that must be covered during the prayer), commencement of the prayer time, facing the qiblah (direction of the Ka‘bah), and the intention.

### Lesson Seven: Pillars of the prayer

They are fourteen:

Standing if one is able to, the opening Takbīr, recitation of Surat al-Fātihah, bowing, standing upright after bowing, prostration on seven body parts, rising from prostration, sitting between the two prostrations, tranquility in all actions, observing the prescribed order among the pillars, the final Tashahhud, sitting for it, invoking Allah’s peace and blessings upon the Prophet ($\text{\small ﷺ}$), and

---

making two Taslīms.

### Lesson Eight: Obligatory acts of prayer

They are eight:

All the Takbīrs except the opening Takbīr; saying: "Sami‘allāhu liman hamidah (Allah hears whoever praises Him)" by the Imam and the one praying alone; saying: "Rabbana wa laka al-hamd (Our Lord, to You belongs all praise)" by everyone; saying: "Subhāna Rabbi Al-‘Azhīm (Glory be to my Lord, the Most Magnificent)" during bowing; saying: "Subhāna Rabbi Al-A‘la (Glory be to my Lord, the Most High)" during prostration; saying: "Rabbi ighfir li (O Lord, forgive me)" between the two prostrations; the first Tashahhud; and sitting for it.

### Lesson Nine: Explanation of Tashahhud

It is to say:

“At-tahiyyātu lillāhi was-salawātu wat-tayyibātu, as-salāmu ‘alayka ayyuha an-nabiyyu wa rahmatullāhi wa barakātuh; as-salāmu ‘alaynā wa ‘alā ‘ibādillāhi as-sālihīn; ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh, wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan ‘abduhu wa rasūluh.”

*(Greetings, prayers, and good things are due to Allah. May the peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you, O Prophet. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.)*

### Lesson Ten: Sunnah acts of prayer

These include:

1. The Istiftāh (opening) invocation.
2. Placing the palm of the right hand over the left one on the chest while standing, before and after Rukū‘ (bowing).
3. Raising both hands with fingers joined and extended to the level of the shoulders or ears during the initial Takbīr, when bowing, upon rising from bowing, and when standing from the first Tashahhud to perform the third Rak‘ah.
4. Saying more than once Tasbīh (glorification of Allah) in Rukū‘ (bowing) and Sujūd (prostration).
5. What exceeds the saying of "Rabbana wa lakal-hamd" (Our Lord, to You belongs all praise) after rising from Rukū‘ (bowing), and what exceeds one utterance of seeking forgiveness between the two Sujūd (prostrations).
6. Keeping the head level with the back during Rukū‘.
7. Keeping the arms away from the sides, the abdomen away from the thighs, and the thighs away from the shanks during Sujūd (prostration).
8. Lifting the arms off the ground during

### Lesson Eleven: Invalidators of prayer

They are eight:

1. Intentional talking while remembering and being aware (of its prohibition). However, the prayer of the one who forgot or was unaware (of its prohibition) is not invalidated by that.
2. Laughing.
3. Eating.
4. Drinking.
5. Exposure of ‘Awrah (must-cover body parts).
6. Excessive diversion from the Qiblah direction.
7. Excessive and continuous fiddling during the prayer.
8. Nullification of Tahārah (ritual purity).

### Lesson Twelve: Conditions of ablution

They are ten:

Islam, sanity, reaching the age of discernment, intention and continuing to maintain it without intending to interrupt it until his purification is complete, the cessation of what necessitates ablution, performing Istinjā’ (cleaning the private

### Lesson Thirteen: Obligatory acts of ablution

They are six:

Washing the face, which includes rinsing the mouth and sniffing water into the nostrils, washing the hands including the elbows, wiping over the whole head including the ears, washing the feet including the ankles, observing the prescribed order, and doing all this in succession. It is recommended to repeat the washing of the face, hands, and feet three times, as well as rinsing the mouth and sniffing water into the nostrils, while the obligatory act is to do each action once. As for wiping over the head, it is not recommended to repeat it, as indicated by authentic Hadīths.

### Lesson Fourteen: Invalidators of ablution

They are six:

What comes out of the two passages; the excessive impure secretions from the body; the loss of consciousness due to sleep or otherwise; touching the private parts (penis, vagina, or anus) with the hand without a barrier; eating camel meat,

### Lesson Fifteen: Adorning oneself with the prescribed morals for every Muslim

Among them are: truthfulness, honesty, chastity, bashfulness, bravery, generosity, loyalty, abstaining from all that Allah has forbidden, good neighborliness, assisting those in need according to one's ability, and other morals that the Qur’an or Sunnah has prescribed.

### Lesson Sixteen: Observing Islamic manners

Among them are: greeting with peace, cheerfulness, eating and drinking with the right hand, saying Bismillāh (in the Name of Allah) at the beginning, and Alhamdulillāh (praise be to Allah) upon finishing, praising Allah (saying Alhamdulillāh) after sneezing, responding to the snezer if they praise Allah, visiting the sick, following the funeral for prayer and burial, observing the Islamic etiquettes when entering or leaving the mosque or home, during travel, with parents, relatives, neighbors, the elderly and the young, offering congratulations for a newborn, invoking blessings for marriage, offering condolences in times of affliction, and other Islamic etiquettes in wearing and removing clothes and shoes.

### Lesson Seventeen: Warning against Shirk and various types of sins

Among them are the seven destructive sins; namely: associating partners with Allah, magic (sorcery), killing a person whom Allah has prohibited from being killed except by legal right, consuming Riba, devouring the property of an orphan, fleeing from the battlefield, and slandering chaste, innocent, believing women.

Among them are also: undutifulness to parents; severing ties of kinship; bearing false witness; false oaths; harming one's neighbor; wronging people concerning their blood (killing), wealth, and honor; consuming intoxicants; gambling, i.e., Maysir; backbiting; slander; and other matters prohibited by Allah Almighty, or His Messenger ($\text{\small ﷺ}$).

**Second:** Once his death is certain, his eyes should be closed, and his jaw should be tied, as reported in the Sunnah.

**Third:** It is obligatory to wash the deceased Muslim unless he is a martyr who died in the battle. He is not to be washed or offered the funeral prayer; rather, he is to be buried in his clothes, for the Prophet ($\text{\small ﷺ}$) did not wash the martyrs of ’Uhud nor offer the funeral prayer over them.

**Fourth:** The manner of washing the deceased:

His ‘Awrah (private parts) should be covered, then he should be slightly lifted and have his abdomen pressed gently. The washer should wrap a cloth or something similar around his hand to clean the deceased’s private parts with it. Then, he makes ablution for him like that for prayer. He washes his head and beard with water and Sidr (lote tree leaves) or something similar. Then, he washes his right side, then the left side. He washes him in the same manner a second and third time, passing his hand over his abdomen each time; if

If the deceased's mustache or nails are long, he should trim them, but if he leaves them, there is no harm. He should neither comb his hair, nor shave his pubic hair, or circumcise him, as there is no evidence for that. As for a woman, her hair should be braided into three braids and left to hang down her back.

**Fifth:** Shrouding the deceased

It is better that a man be shrouded in three white sheets, with neither a shirt nor a turban, as was done with the Prophet ($\text{\small ﷺ}$), wrapping him therein completely. However, if he is shrouded in a shirt, an Izār (lower garment), and a wrap, there is no harm.

A female deceased is shrouded in five garments: a shirt, a head veil, a lower garment, and two wrapping sheets. A male child is shrouded in one to three garments, and a female child is shrouded in a

---

dress and two wrapping sheets.

The obligation for everyone is a single garment that covers the entire deceased's body. However, if the deceased is in a state of Ihrām, he should be washed with water and Sidr and shrouded in his Izār and Ridā’ or other garments. His head and face should not be covered, nor should he be perfumed, for he will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment reciting Talbiyah, as authentically reported in a Hadīth of the Messenger of Allah ($\text{\small ﷺ}$). If the person in Ihrām is a woman, she is shrouded like others, but she should not be perfumed, nor should her face be covered with a Niqāb, nor her hands with gloves. Instead, her face and hands should be covered with the shroud in which she is wrapped, as previously explained in the description of shrouding a woman.

**Sixth:** The most entitled person to wash the deceased, offer the funeral prayer over him, and bury him

The person appointed by the deceased in his will to do that, then the father, then the grandfather, then the next in nearness, and so on from among the paternal male relatives. This applies to a deceased male.

The most entitled to wash a deceased woman are those women she has appointed in her will, followed by her mother, then her grandmother, and then the closest female relatives. Each of the two spouses can wash the other, for As-Siddīq (may

One should make four Takbīrs. After the first Takbīr, he recites Al-Fātihah. Then, he makes the second Takbīr and invokes Allah’s peace and blessings upon the Prophet ($\text{\small ﷺ}$), as he does in the Tashahhud. Then, he makes the third Takbīr and says:

> “O Allah, forgive those of us who are living and those of us who are dead, those of us who are present and those of us who are absent, those of us who are young and those of us who are old, those of us who are males and those who are females. O Allah, whoever of us You give life, let him live upon Islam, and whoever of us You take in death, let him die in a state of faith. O Allah, forgive him and have mercy upon him. Grant him wellness and pardon him. Make his resting place a noble one, and facilitate his entry. Wash him with water, snow, and hail. Purify him from sins as a white garment is cleansed of dirt. Give him in exchange a home better than his home (on earth) and a family better than his family. Grant him entrance to Paradise and protect him from the trials of the grave and the torture of Hellfire. Expand his grave for him and

> illuminate it for him. O Allah, deprive us not of his reward, and do not lead us astray after him.”

Then, he should make the fourth Takbīr and make one Taslīm to his right.

It is recommended to raise the hands with each Takbīr. If the deceased is a woman, it is said: (O Allah, forgive her...) and so on. If there are two deceased, it is said: (O Allah, forgive them both...) and so on. If there are more than that, it is said: (O Allah, forgive them...) and so on. However, if the deceased is a child, instead of supplicating for forgiveness, it is said:

> “O Allah, make him a forerunner and reward in store for his parents, and an accepted intercessor; O Allah, make their scales heavy and their rewards great on account of him, join him with the righteous believing predecessors, put him in the care of Abraham (peace be upon him) and save him by Your mercy from the punishment of Hellfire.”

According to the Sunnah, the Imām should stand at the head of a man and the middle of a woman’s body. If there are male and female deceased people, the man should be closest to the Imām, and the woman should be closest to the Qiblah. If there are children among them, the boy should be placed before the woman, then the woman, and then the girl. The head of the boy should be aligned with the head of the man, and the middle of the woman should be aligned with the head of the man.

It is prescribed to deepen the grave to the middle of a man’s height, and to have a Lahd (niche) on the side facing the Qiblah. The deceased should be placed in the Lahd on his right side, and the shroud knots should be untied but not removed, and the face should not be uncovered, whether the deceased is a man or a woman. Then bricks should be set up over him and plastered to secure them and protect him from the dirt. If bricks are not available, then other materials such as planks, stones, or wood may be used to protect him from the dirt. Then dirt should be poured over him. It is recommended to say at that time: “Bismillāh wa ‘ala millati rasūlillāh.” (In the Name of Allah, and upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah). The grave should be raised a handspan above the ground, and if possible, gravel should be placed on it and it should be sprinkled with water.

It is prescribed for those attending the funeral to stand by the grave and supplicate for the deceased, as the Prophet ($\text{\small ﷺ}$) would stand at the grave whenever he finished burying a deceased, and say:

# The Important Lessons for the General Ummah

### His Eminence Shaykh ‘Abdul-‘Azīz bin ‘Abdullah bin Bāz

---

## Foreword

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and the good end is certainly for the righteous. May Allah’s peace and blessings be upon His slave and Messenger, our Prophet Muhammad, and his family and all his Companions.

These are concise words elucidating some of what the general public must know about the religion of Islam, which I have named: **The Important Lessons for the General Ummah**.

I ask Allah to make it beneficial for the Muslims and accept it from me; indeed, He is the Most Generous and Bounteous.

*‘Abdul-‘Azīz ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Bāz*

---

## Lesson One: Surat al-Fātihah and the Short Surahs

Surat al-Fātihah and as many of the short Surahs as possible, from Surat az-Zalzalah to Surat an-Nās, are to be learnt, corrected in recitation, memorized, and explained for what is obligatory to be understood.

---

## Lesson Two: The Pillars of Islam

Explanation of the five pillars of Islam, the first and greatest of which is: Testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, with an explanation of its meanings, along with clarifying the requirements of “There is no god but Allah.” 

### The Meaning of the Testimony
* **“There is no god”**: Negates all that is worshiped besides Allah.
* **“except Allah”**: Affirms worship to Allah alone, without a partner.

### Requirements of the Testimony
The requirements of *“La ilāha illa Allah”* are:
1. Knowledge that negates ignorance.
2. Certitude that negates doubt.
3. Sincerity that negates polytheism.
4. Truthfulness that negates falsehood.
5. Love that negates hatred.
6. Submission that negates abandonment.
7. Acceptance that negates rejection.
8. Disbelief in what is worshipped besides Allah.

These requirements are summed up in the following two poetic verses:
> *Knowledge, certainty, and your sincerity... along with love, submission, and its acceptance*
> *Then add the eighth, which is your rejection of... everything that is worshipped besides the true God.*

### Testimony of Muhammad's Messengerhood
The implications of the testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah ($\text{\small ﷺ}$) are:
* To believe in what he informed.
* To obey his commands.
* To avoid what he forbade and warned against.
* To worship Allah only in the manner prescribed by Allah Almighty and His Messenger ($\text{\small ﷺ}$).

### Remaining Pillars of Islam
* Prayer (*Salah*).
* Zakah.
* Fasting the month of Ramadan.
* Performing Hajj to the Sacred House of Allah for those who are able to do so.

---

## Lesson Three: The Pillars of Imān (Faith)

They are six:
1. Belief in Allah.
2. His angels.
3. His books.
4. His messengers.
5. The Last Day.
6. Belief in Al-Qadar (predestination), with its good and bad aspects, as being from Allah Almighty.

---

## Lesson Four: Categories of Tawhīd and Categories of Shirk

### 1. Categories of Tawhīd
The categories of Tawhīd are three:

* **Tawhīd ar-Rubūbiyyah (Oneness of Lordship):** Believing that Allah Almighty is the Creator of everything and the Disposer of all affairs, with no partner in that.
* **Tawhīd al-’Ulūhiyyah (Oneness of Worship):** Believing that Allah Almighty is the only true deity worthy of worship, having no partner in this regard. This is the meaning of *“La ilāha illa Allah”*. All acts of worship, such as prayer, fasting, and others, must be devoted solely to Allah alone.
* **Tawhīd al-Asmā’ wa as-Sifāt (Oneness of Allah's Names and Attributes):** Believing in all that is mentioned in the Noble Qur’an or the authentic Hadīths regarding Allah’s names and attributes, affirming them for Allah alone in a manner befitting His Majesty, without *Tahrīf* (distortion), *Ta‘tīl* (denial), *Takyīf* (asking how), or *Tamthīl* (likening).

Allah the Exalted says:
> ﴿ قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ ١ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ ٢ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ ٣ وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ ٤ ﴾
> *{Say: “He is Allah, the One; Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him.”}* [Surat al-Ikhlās: 1-4]

And He says:
> ﴿ ... لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ ۖ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ ﴾
> *{There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.}* [Surat ash-Shūra: 11]

Some scholars incorporate *Tawhīd al-Asmā’ wa as-Sifāt* into *Tawhīd ar-Rubūbiyyah*, making them two categories. There is no contention in this, as the core meaning is clear in both classifications.

---

### 2. Categories of Shirk (Polytheism)
Shirk is divided into three categories: Major Shirk, Minor Shirk, and Hidden Shirk.

#### A. Major Shirk (Shirk Akbar)
It renders all deeds worthless and causes a person to abide eternally in the Hellfire if they die upon it.

Allah Almighty says:
> ﴿ ... وَلَوْ أَشْرَكُوا لَحَبِطَ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ ﴾
> *{If they were to associate others with Him, all their deeds would have been nullified.}* [Surat al-An‘ām: 88]

He also says:
> ﴿ ... إِنَّهُ مَن يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدْ حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْجَنَّةَ وَمَأْوَاهُ النَّارُ ۖ وَمَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ أَنصَارٍ ﴾
> *{Whoever associates any partners with Allah, Allah has forbidden Paradise for him, and his abode will be the Fire. And the wrongdoers will have no helpers.}* [Surat al-Mā’idah: 72]

* **Examples:** Supplication to the dead and idols, seeking help from them, making vows to them, offering sacrifices to them, and similar practices.

#### B. Minor Shirk (Shirk Asghar)
It is what has been established by the texts of the Qur’an or the Sunnah as being called “Shirk,” but does not reach the level of major Shirk. It does not constitute apostasy or cause eternal damnation in Hellfire, but it negates the perfect obligatory Tawhīd.

* **Examples:**
  * **Ar-Riyā’ (Showing off in deeds):** The Prophet ($\text{\small ﷺ}$) said:
    > « أَخْوَفُ مَا أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمُ الشِّرْكُ الْأَصْغَرُ » فَسُئِلَ عَنْهُ، فَقَالَ: « الرِّيَاءُ » .
    > *“The thing that I fear most for you is the minor Shirk.” When asked what it was, he said: “Ar-Riyā’” (showing off).* [Narrated by Ahmad]
  * **Swearing by other than Allah:** The Prophet ($\text{\small ﷺ}$) said:
    > « مَنْ حَلَفَ بِغَيْرِ اللهِ فَقَدْ كَفَرَ أَوْ أَشْرَكَ » .
    > *“Whoever swears by other than Allah has disbelieved or associated partners with Allah.”* [Narrated by Abu Dāwūd and At-Tirmidhi]
  * **Associating human will with Allah’s will using "and":** Saying: “What Allah wills and so-and-so wills.” Rather, one should say: “What Allah wills, *then* so-and-so wills.”

#### C. Hidden Shirk (Shirk al-Khafī)
The evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet ($\text{\small ﷺ}$):
> « أَلَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِمَا هُوَ أَخْوَفُ عَلَيْكُمْ عِنْدِي مِنَ الْمَسِيحِ الدَّجَّالِ؟ » قَالُوا: بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، قَالَ: « الشِّرْكُ الْخَفِيُّ، يَقُومُ الرَّجُلُ فَيُصَلِّي فَيُزَيِّنُ صَلَاتَهُ لِمَا يَرَى مِنْ نَظَرِ الرَّجُلِ إِلَيْهِ » .
> *“Shall I tell you what I fear more for you than the Antichrist?” They said: “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Hidden Shirk; when a man gets up to pray and beautifies his prayer because he sees another man watching him.”* [Narrated by Ahmad]

Shirk can also be divided into only two categories: Major and Minor. Under this division, Hidden Shirk is incorporated into both categories. It can occur as Major Shirk (such as the hypocrisy of those who conceal disbelief and show Islam outwardly out of show-off or fear) or as Minor Shirk (such as a passing desire to show off, *Riyā’*).

---

## Lesson Five: Ihsān (Excellence in Worship)

**The single pillar of Ihsān:** To worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you cannot see Him, He indeed sees you.

---

## Lesson Six: Conditions of Prayer

They are nine:
1. Islam.
2. Sanity.
3. Reaching the age of discernment (*Tamyīz*).
4. Being in a state of ritual purity (*Tahārah*).
5. Removal of *Najāsah* (tangible impurity) from the body, clothes, and place of prayer.
6. Covering the *‘Awrah* (parts of the body that must be covered).
7. Commencement of the prayer time.
8. Facing the *Qiblah* (direction of the Ka‘bah).
9. Intention (*Niyyah*).

---

## Lesson Seven: Pillars of the Prayer

They are fourteen:
1. Standing if one is able to.
2. The opening *Takbīr* (*Takbīrat-ul-Ihrām*).
3. Recitation of Surat al-Fātihah.
4. Bowing (*Rukū‘*).
5. Standing upright after bowing.
6. Prostrating on seven body parts (*Sujūd*).
7. Rising from prostration.
8. Sitting between the two prostrations.
9. Tranquility (*Tuma'nīnah*) in all actions.
10. Observing the prescribed order among the pillars.
11. The final *Tashahhud*.
12. Sitting for the final *Tashahhud*.
13. Invoking Allah’s peace and blessings upon the Prophet ($\text{\small ﷺ}$).
14. Making the two *Taslīms*.

---

## Lesson Eight: Obligatory Acts of Prayer

They are eight:
1. All the *Takbīrs* except the opening *Takbīr*.
2. Saying: *"Sami‘allāhu liman hamidah"* (Allah hears whoever praises Him) by the Imam and the one praying alone.
3. Saying: *"Rabbana wa laka al-hamd"* (Our Lord, to You belongs all praise) by everyone (Imam, follower, and individual).
4. Saying: *"Subhāna Rabbi Al-‘Azhīm"* (Glory be to my Lord, the Most Magnificent) during bowing.
5. Saying: *"Subhāna Rabbi Al-A‘la"* (Glory be to my Lord, the Most High) during prostration.
6. Saying: *"Rabbi ighfir li"* (O Lord, forgive me) between the two prostrations.
7. The first *Tashahhud*.
8. Sitting for the first *Tashahhud*.

---

## Lesson Nine: Explanation of Tashahhud

The worshipper says:
> “At-tahiyyātu lillāhi was-salawātu wat-tayyibātu, as-salāmu ‘alayka ayyuha an-nabiyyu wa rahmatullāhi wa barakātuh; as-salāmu ‘alaynā wa ‘alā ‘ibādillāhi as-sālihīn; ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh, wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan ‘abduhu wa rasūluh.”
> *(Greetings, prayers, and good things are due to Allah. May the peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you, O Prophet. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.)*

Then, in the final Tashahhud, one invokes peace and blessings upon the Prophet ($\text{\small ﷺ}$), saying:
> “Allahumma salli ‘ala muhammadin, wa ‘ala āli muhammadin, kama sallayta ‘ala ibrahima wa ‘ala āli ibrahima, innaka hamidum majid, wa bārik ‘ala muhammadin, wa ‘ala āli muhammadin, kama barakta ‘ala ibrahima, wa ‘ala āli ibrahima, innaka hamidum majid”
> *(O Allah, exalt the mention of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You have exalted the mention of Abraham and the family of Abraham; indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You have blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham; indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.)*

Following this, one seeks refuge with Allah from four trials:
1. The torment of Hellfire.
2. The torment of the grave.
3. The trials of life and death.
4. The trial of the Al-Masīh ad-Dajjāl (Anti-Christ).

One may then choose any legislated or reported supplication, such as:
> “O Allah, help me remember You, show gratitude to You, and worship You properly. O Allah, I have wronged myself too much, and none forgives sins but You. So, forgive me with forgiveness from You, and have mercy on me. Indeed, You are the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.”

---

## Lesson Ten: Sunnah Acts of Prayer

These are the voluntary actions and sayings in prayer, which include:

1. The *Istiftāh* (opening) invocation.
2. Placing the palm of the right hand over the left hand on the chest while standing, before and after *Rukū‘*.
3. Raising both hands with fingers joined and extended to the level of the shoulders or ears during:
   * The opening *Takbīr*.
   * Going into *Rukū‘*.
   * Rising from *Rukū‘*.
   * Standing up after the first *Tashahhud*.
4. Saying the *Tasbīh* during bowing and prostration more than the single obligatory once.
5. What exceeds the obligatory utterances of praises after rising from *Rukū‘* and seeking forgiveness between the two prostrations.
6. Keeping the head level with the back during *Rukū‘*.
7. Keeping the arms away from the sides, the abdomen away from the thighs, and the thighs away from the shanks during *Sujūd*.
8. Lifting the forearms off the ground during prostration.
9. *Iftirāsh:* Resting on the left foot with the right foot erected during the first *Tashahhud* and between the two prostrations.
10. *Tawarruk:* Sitting on the posterior with the left foot placed under the right leg while keeping the right foot erect during the final *Tashahhud* of three- or four-Rak‘ah prayers.
11. Pointing with the index finger during the first and second *Tashahhud* from the moment of sitting until the end, and moving it during supplication.
12. Invoking peace and blessings upon Muhammad and his family, and Abraham and his family, during the first *Tashahhud*.
13. Making supplications in the final *Tashahhud*.
14. Audible recitation in Fajr, Jumu‘ah, Eid, *Istisqā’* (rain-seeking), and the first two Rak‘ahs of Maghrib and ‘Ishā’ prayers.
15. Inaudible recitation in Zhuhr, ‘Asr, the third Rak‘ah of Maghrib, and the last two Rak‘ahs of ‘Ishā’ prayers.
16. Reciting a portion from the Qur’an in addition to Surat al-Fātihah in the first two Rak‘ahs.
17. Placing the hands on the knees with fingers spread out during *Rukū‘*.

---

## Lesson Eleven: Invalidators of Prayer

They are eight:
1. Intentional talking while remembering and being aware of its prohibition. (The prayer of one who speaks out of forgetfulness or ignorance is not invalidated).
2. Laughing.
3. Eating.
4. Drinking.
5. Exposure of the *‘Awrah*.
6. Excessive deviation from the *Qiblah* direction.
7. Excessive and continuous movement/fiddling during the prayer.
8. Nullification of *Tahārah* (ritual purity).

---

## Lesson Twelve: Conditions of Ablution (Wudū’)

They are ten:
1. Islam.
2. Sanity.
3. Reaching the age of discernment (*Tamyīz*).
4. Intention (*Niyyah*), and continuing to maintain it without intending to interrupt it until purification is complete.
5. Cessation of what necessitates ablution.
6. Performing *Istinjā’* (cleaning private parts with water) or *Istijmār* (using stones/tissues) prior to ablution.
7. The water must be pure (*Tahūr*) and lawfully obtained.
8. Removing any substance that hinders water from reaching the skin (e.g., wax, thick grease).
9. The commencement of prayer time for those with constant ritual impurity (e.g., urinary incontinence).

---

## Lesson Thirteen: Obligatory Acts of Ablution

They are six:
1. Washing the face, which includes rinsing the mouth (*Madmadah*) and sniffing water into the nostrils (*Istinshāq*).
2. Washing the hands up to and including the elbows.
3. Wiping over the entire head, including the ears.
4. Washing the feet up to and including the ankles.
5. Observing the prescribed order (*Tartīb*).
6. Performing the actions in direct succession without prolonged delay (*Muwalāt*).

*Note:* It is recommended to wash the face, hands, and feet three times, as well as rinsing the mouth and nose three times. The obligatory requirement, however, is to do so once. Wiping the head must only be done once.

---

## Lesson Fourteen: Invalidators of Ablution

They are six:
1. Anything emitted from the two private passages (urine, feces, gas, etc.).
2. Excessive impure bodily secretions (such as blood or pus).
3. Loss of consciousness due to sleep, fainting, or otherwise.
4. Touching the private parts (penis, vagina, or anus) directly with the hand without a barrier.
5. Eating camel meat.
6. Apostasy from Islam.

### Special Notes on Ablution:
* **Washing a deceased person:** The correct view among scholars is that washing a corpse does not nullify the washer's ablution, unless the washer’s hand directly touches the private parts of the deceased without a barrier.
* **Touching a woman:** Simply touching a woman does not invalidate ablution, regardless of whether it is done with or without desire, as long as nothing is emitted. The Prophet ($\text{\small ﷺ}$) kissed some of his wives and prayed without repeating his ablution.
* **The Qur'anic Verse** *{...or had sexual contact with women...}* [Surat an-Nisā’: 43]: The correct interpretation, as stated by Ibn ‘Abbās and others, is that this refers specifically to sexual intercourse.

---

## Lesson Fifteen: Adorning Oneself with Prescribed Islamic Morals

Every Muslim should embody high moral characters, including:
* Truthfulness and honesty.
* Chastity and bashfulness.
* Bravery and generosity.
* Loyalty and keeping promises.
* Abstaining from all that Allah has forbidden.
* Good neighborliness.
* Assisting those in need according to one's ability.

---

## Lesson Sixteen: Observing Islamic Manners

A Muslim must practice standard Islamic etiquettes, which include:
* Greeting with peace (*As-Salāmu ‘Alaykum*).
* Maintaining a cheerful countenance.
* Eating and drinking with the right hand.
* Saying *Bismillāh* before eating/drinking, and *Alhamdulillāh* upon finishing.
* Saying *Alhamdulillāh* after sneezing, and responding with *Yarhamukallāh* to someone who sneezes and praises Allah.
* Visiting the sick.
* Attending funerals (for prayer and burial).
* Observing the specific prayers/supplications when entering or leaving the mosque or home, and during travel.
* Showing kindness to parents, relatives, neighbors, the elderly, and the young.
* Congratulating someone on a newborn, invoking blessings for marriage, and offering condolences in times of grief.
* Observing proper Islamic manners when wearing and removing clothes and shoes.

---

## Lesson Seventeen: Warning Against Shirk and Various Types of Sins

### The Seven Destructive Sins (*Al-Mūbiqāt*)
1. Associating partners with Allah (*Shirk*).
2. Magic (sorcery).
3. Killing a person whom Allah has prohibited from being killed, except by legal right.
4. Consuming usury (*Riba*).
5. Devouring the property of an orphan.
6. Fleeing from the battlefield during war.
7. Slandering chaste, innocent, believing women.

### Other Major Prohibitions
* Undutifulness to parents.
* Severing ties of kinship.
* Bearing false witness and false oaths.
* Harming neighbors.
* Violating the blood, wealth, and honor of others.
* Consuming intoxicants.
* Gambling (*Maysir*).
* Backbiting (*Ghībah*) and slander (*Namīmah*).

---

## Lesson Eighteen: Preparation, Funeral Prayer, and Burial of the Deceased

### 1. The Deathbed
* It is prescribed to gently encourage a dying person to say: *"La ilāha illallāh"*, in accordance with the Hadīth:
  > « لَقِّنُوا مَوْتَاكُمْ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ » .
  > *“Exhort your dying people to say: La ilāha illallāh.”* [Narrated by Muslim]

### 2. Immediate Steps After Death
* Once death is confirmed, the deceased’s eyes should be closed, and the jaw should be gently bound.

### 3. Washing the Deceased (*Ghusl*)
* Washing a deceased Muslim is a communal obligation (*Fard Kifāyah*), except for a martyr who died on the battlefield. The martyr is buried in his clothes, without being washed or having the funeral prayer offered over him.
* **Washing Method:**
  1. Cover the deceased's *‘Awrah* (private parts).
  2. Lift the body slightly and gently press the abdomen to expel any wastes.
  3. The washer wraps a cloth around his hand and washes the deceased's private parts.
  4. Perform ablution (*Wudū’*) for the deceased, just like the ablution for prayer.
  5. Wash the head and beard with water and *Sidr* (lote-tree leaves) or soap.
  6. Wash the right side of the body, then the left side.
  7. Repeat this process a second and third time. If any impurity is still expelled, wash it, plug the exit with cotton or medical tape, and repeat the ablution.
  8. The final wash should contain a little camphor.
  9. Dry the body. Trim the mustache or nails if they are excessively long. Do not comb the hair, shave pubic hair, or circumcise the body.
  10. For women, the hair should be braided into three braids and left to hang down behind her back.
  11. Apply perfume to the body folds, prostration points, or the entire body, and incense the shroud.

### 4. Shrouding the Deceased (*Kafan*)
* **For Men:** Preferably three white wrapping sheets without a shirt or turban. He is wrapped completely. An *Izār* (lower garment), shirt, and wrap are also acceptable.
* **For Women:** Shrouded in five garments: a shirt, a head veil, a lower garment (*Izār*), and two wrapping sheets.
* **For Children:** A male child is wrapped in one to three sheets; a female child is wrapped in a dress and two wrapping sheets.
* **Deceased in State of Ihram:** Wash with water and *Sidr*, and shroud in their *Izār* and *Ridā’* (pilgrimage garments). Do not cover their head or face (for men), and do not apply any perfume.

### 5. Who is Most Entitled to Wash, Pray, and Bury
* **For Men:** The person designated in the deceased's will, followed by the father, grandfather, and closest paternal male relatives.
* **For Women:** The women designated in her will, followed by her mother, grandmother, and closest female relatives.
* **Spouses:** Either spouse is permitted to wash the other. Abu Bakr was washed by his wife, and ‘Ali washed his wife Fātimah.

### 6. The Funeral Prayer (*Salāt al-Janāzah*)
The Imam makes four *Takbīrs* while standing:
* **After the First Takbīr:** Recite Surat al-Fātihah. Reciting a short Surah after it is also good.
* **After the Second Takbīr:** Send blessings upon the Prophet ($\text{\small ﷺ}$) as done in the final Tashahhud.
* **After the Third Takbīr:** Supplicate for the deceased:
  > “O Allah, forgive those of us who are living and those of us who are dead, those of us who are present and those of us who are absent, those of us who are young and those of us who are old, those of us who are males and those who are females. O Allah, whoever of us You give life, let him live upon Islam, and whoever of us You take in death, let him die in a state of faith. O Allah, forgive him and have mercy upon him. Grant him wellness and pardon him. Make his resting place a noble one, and facilitate his entry. Wash him with water, snow, and hail. Purify him from sins as a white garment is cleansed of dirt. Give him in exchange a home better than his home and a family better than his family. Grant him entrance to Paradise and protect him from the trials of the grave and the torture of Hellfire. Expand his grave for him and illuminate it for him. O Allah, deprive us not of his reward, and do not lead us astray after him.”
  * *If the deceased is a child, supplicate instead:*
    > “O Allah, make him a forerunner and reward in store for his parents, and an accepted intercessor; O Allah, make their scales heavy and their rewards great on account of him, join him with the righteous believing predecessors, put him in the care of Abraham (peace be upon him) and save him by Your mercy from the punishment of Hellfire.”
* **After the Fourth Takbīr:** Say one *Taslīm* to the right.

#### Alignment of the Body
* **For a Man:** The Imam stands in line with the deceased's head.
* **For a Woman:** The Imam stands in line with the middle of her body.
* **For multiple bodies:** The male bodies are placed closest to the Imam, followed by boys, then women, then girls (closest to the *Qiblah*).

### 7. Burial
* Dig the grave to a depth of half a man's height, with a *Lahd* (niche) in the side facing the *Qiblah*.
* Place the deceased on their right side facing the *Qiblah*. Untie the shroud knots but do not remove the shroud.
* Cover the niche with bricks or planks, and pour dirt over it.
* Say when placing the body: *“Bismillāh wa ‘ala millati rasūlillāh”* (In the Name of Allah, and upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah).
* Raise the grave about a handspan above the ground, and place gravel or sprinkle water over it.
* Stand at the grave and pray for the deceased's firmness, in accordance with the Prophet’s command:
  > « اسْتَغْفِرُوا لِأَخِيكُمْ، وَاسْأَلُوا لَهُ التَّثْبِيتَ، فَإِنَّهُ الْآنَ يُسْأَلُ » .
  > *“Ask forgiveness for your brother and implore Allah to make him firm, for he is being questioned now.”*

### 8. Condolences, Mourning, and Visitation
* **Late Prayer:** One who missed the funeral prayer may pray at the grave within a month of the burial.
* **Food Preparation:** The family of the deceased should not prepare food for the people (as this is considered a form of wailing). Rather, relatives and neighbors should prepare food *for* the grieving family.
* **Mourning Period:** A woman must not mourn for any deceased relative for more than three days, except for her husband, for whom she must mourn for four months and ten days (unless pregnant, in which case her mourning ends upon childbirth). Men are not permitted to adopt formal mourning practices.
* **Visiting Graves:** It is highly encouraged for men to visit graves to remember the Hereafter and supplicate for the dead. It is forbidden for women to visit graves or follow funeral processions.

qa_dataset.answer: The author explains that belief in destiny does not negate human free will and power, which are affirmed by both Sharia texts (e.g., Quranic verses on choice and capacity like Surat an-Naba': 39, Surat al-Baqarah: 223, Surat at-Taghābun: 16, Surat al-Baqarah: 286) and reality (the observable difference between voluntary and involuntary actions). Arguments against using destiny as an excuse include: Allah's own refutation of polytheists who used it (Surat al-An'ām: 148); the purpose of sending messengers was to remove excuses (Surat an-Nisa': 165); the Prophet's instruction to work despite destiny, as everyone is eased towards what they were created for; Allah not burdening souls beyond their capacity; destiny being a hidden secret unknown until it occurs; and practical human behavior in worldly affairs, where individuals pursue beneficial paths regardless of destiny. The author also cites the anecdote of Umar ibn al-Khattāb cutting off a thief's hand, stating it was 'according to the destiny of Allah,' in response to the thief's excuse.
qa_dataset.question: How does the author reconcile the human free will with the Islamic concept of divine destiny (Qadar), and what are the primary arguments against using destiny as an excuse for actions?

qa_dataset.answer:
The text presents two perceptible aspects proving Allah's existence: 
1. **Answered Supplications**: This refers to witnessing prayers being answered and relief coming to people in distress. The text cites instances like Noah's supplication (Surat al-Anbiyā': 76), Allah's response to those seeking help in battle (Surat al-Anfāl: 9), and a Bedouin's request for rain to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), which resulted in immediate rainfall as recorded in Sahih Al-Bukhāri. This demonstrates Allah's active intervention and responsiveness.
2. **Prophetic Miracles (Signs)**: These are extraordinary events beyond human capability, which Allah caused to happen to support His messengers. Examples include Moses parting the sea with his staff (Surat ash-Shu'arā': 63), Jesus giving life to the dead (Surat Al-'Imrān: 49), and Prophet Muhammad splitting the moon (Surat al-Qamar: 1-2). These miracles serve as conclusive proof of the existence of the One Who sent them, namely Allah Almighty.
qa_dataset.question: What are the two aspects of perceptible evidence for the existence of Allah Almighty discussed in the text, and how does each illustrate His presence?

qa_dataset.answer: Angels are unseen beings created by Allah from light, fully submissive to His commands, and incapable of lordship or divinity. They are numerous, constantly glorifying Allah without weariness (Surat al-Anbiyā': 19-20). Specific angels have distinct roles: Jibril (Gabriel) conveys divine revelation, Mika'il manages rain and plants, Israfil blows the Trumpet, the Angel of Death takes souls, Malik is the gatekeeper of Hellfire, and other angels are entrusted with embryos, recording deeds, and questioning the dead in the grave. Belief in angels yields several benefits: recognizing Allah's greatness and power, appreciating Allah's care for humankind (through angels' protection and record-keeping), and fostering love for angels due to their worship. The text refutes the idea that angels are merely spiritual powers by citing Quranic verses and Hadith that describe angels as having physical forms (e.g., possessing wings in Surat Fātir: 1, appearing as men, beating disbelievers in Surat al-Anfāl: 50, descending from heaven in Surat ar-Ra'd: 23-24) and performing tangible actions, affirming that they are bodies, not just abstract forces.
qa_dataset.question: Explain the distinct roles and characteristics of angels as described in the text, and how the belief in angels benefits a Muslim. Additionally, how does the text refute the deviant view that angels are merely spiritual powers?

qa_dataset.answer:
Belief in Allah's names and attributes involves affirming what Allah has affirmed for Himself in the Quran (e.g., Surat al-A'raf: 180, Surat ar-Rūm: 27) and Sunnah, in a manner that befits Him, without Tahrīf (distortion), Ta'tīl (denial), Takyīf (asking how), or Tamthīl (likening) (Surat ash-Shūra: 11).

The text addresses two deviant groups:
1.  **The Mu'attilah (Deniers)**: They deny Allah's names or attributes, claiming that affirming them leads to likening Allah to His creation. The text refutes this by arguing that such a claim implies contradictions in Allah's own words (He affirms attributes yet states 'nothing is like Him'). Furthermore, it's unnecessary for two entities sharing an attribute to be similar; differences exist even among created beings (e.g., human vs. animal eyes), so the difference between Creator and creation is far clearer and greater.
2.  **The Mushabbihah (Comparers)**: They affirm Allah's names and attributes but liken Him to His creation, believing the meaning is literal and human-like. The text refutes this by stating that likening Allah to creation is false by reason and Sharia, and sacred texts cannot imply falsehood. While Allah addresses humanity in an understandable way regarding fundamental meanings (e.g., 'hearing' means discerning sounds), the *reality and essence* of these attributes for Allah are unknown and unique to Him, differing vastly from created beings.
qa_dataset.question: Detail the four categories of belief in Allah's names and attributes, and explain how the text addresses the two groups that deviated in this area: the Mu'attilah and the Mushabbihah.

qa_dataset.answer:
The Islamic creed aims to achieve noble purposes that benefit individuals and societies:
1.  **Worshiping Allah Almighty alone with sincere intention**: This objective establishes pure monotheism (Tawhid), freeing individuals from servitude to anything other than their Creator. It directs all acts of worship solely to Allah, ensuring spiritual clarity and preventing the chaos of worshipping multiple entities.
2.  **Freeing people's minds and thinking from chaotic confusion**: By providing a clear and coherent framework of belief, the creed liberates individuals from superstitions, erroneous beliefs, and the emptiness of materialism. It offers mental and intellectual ease, linking believers to their Creator and fostering contentment with divine decree, thereby promoting inner peace and intellectual stability.
3.  **Adopting a firm and serious approach to life**: Belief in the resurrection and accountability for deeds motivates believers to strive for good and avoid sins, driven by the desire for divine rewards and fear of punishment (Surat al-Anʻām: 132). This encourages moral uprightness, diligent effort, and resilience, as exemplified by the teaching to 'Adhere to whatever brings you benefit, seek the help of Allah, and do not feel helpless' (Narrated by Muslim). This leads to individuals who are proactive in good deeds and patient in adversity, which ultimately strengthens the community.
qa_dataset.question: The text outlines several objectives of the Islamic creed. Elaborate on at least three of these objectives and explain how they contribute to individual and societal well-being.

qa_dataset.answer:
Belief in the Last Day encompasses three main components:
1.  **Resurrection (Al-Ba'th)**: This is the revival of the dead when the Trumpet is blown a second time, bringing all people back to life, naked, barefooted, and uncircumcised, to stand before Allah (Surat al-Anbiyā': 104, Surat al-Mu'minūn: 15-16). The text emphasizes this as a firm truth established by the Quran, Sunnah, and Muslim consensus, implying that earthly life is not an end but a prelude to accountability.
2.  **Reckoning and Recompense (Al-Hisab wal-Jaza')**: Everyone will be held accountable for their deeds and rewarded or punished accordingly. Good deeds are multiplied, while evil deeds are repaid in kind, with no injustice (Surat al-Ghāshiyah: 25-26, Surat al-An'am: 160, Surat al-Anbiyā': 47). This belief serves as a powerful deterrent against sin and an encouragement for righteous conduct, knowing that every action, no matter how small, will be weighed.
3.  **Paradise and Hellfire (Al-Jannah wal-Nar)**: These are the eternal abodes for humanity. Paradise is for pious believers, offering unimaginable bliss (Surat al-Bayyinah: 7-8, Surat as-Sajdah: 17), while Hellfire is for disbelievers and transgressors, containing severe and unimaginable punishment (Surat Al 'Imrān: 131, Surat al-Kahf: 29, Surat al-Ahzāb: 64-66). This component motivates believers to strive for Paradise and avoid the actions that lead to Hellfire, shaping their life choices and moral compass.
Additionally, the text mentions **post-death events** such as the trial of the grave (questioning by angels) and the punishment or bliss experienced within the grave, reinforcing immediate accountability after death.

Islam is a creed and a Sharia (law). It is complete
in terms of its beliefs and laws:
1- It enjoins belief in the Oneness of Allah
Almighty and forbids polytheism.
2- It enjoins truthfulness and forbids lying.
3- It enjoins justice and forbids injustice. Justice
is to treat what is similar equally and differentiate
between what is different. It is not absolute
equality, which is advocated by some when they say
that Islam is the religion of equality in absolute
terms. Indeed, treating different things equally is a
form of injustice in Islam.
4- It enjoins honesty and forbids treachery.
5- It enjoins loyalty and forbids betrayal.
6- It enjoins dutifulness to one's parents and
forbids ingratitude towards them.
7- It enjoins upholding kinship ties and forbids
severing them.
8- It enjoins good neighborliness and forbids the
opposite.
Generally, Islam enjoins every good manner and
righteous act and forbids every bad manner and
evil act.

truthfully. This is because other elements of the

good only if it adheres to this religion properly, and

Belief in Allah Almighty
Belief in Allah comprises four things:
First: Belief in the existence of Allah Almighty:
His existence is established through evidence of
Fitrah (innate inclination), logic, the Sharia, and
perception.
As for how the Fitrah indicates the existence of
Allah Almighty: Indeed, every created being came
into existence with a natural belief in his Creator
without prior thinking or education. No one
swerves from this Fitrah except one whose heart
gets influenced by something that turns it away
from it. The Prophet (ﷺ) said:
«مَا مِنْ مَوْلُودٍ إِلَّا يُولَدُ عَلَى الْفِطْرَةِ، فَأَبَوَاهُ يُهَوِّدَانِهِ أَوْ يُنَصِّرَانِهِ أَوْ يُمَحِّسَانِهِ».
"No child is born except upon Fitrah, and then
his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a
Magian."²
2- With regard to the logical evidence for the
existence of Allah Almighty: Indeed, all created

Two groups have fallen into misguidance
concerning this matter:
29

One group: The Muʻattilah (deniers), who deny
the Names and Attributes of Allah, or some of
them—claiming that acknowledging them requires
likening Allah to His creation. This claim is false for
several reasons, like the following:
First: It entails false implications, like
contradictions in the words of Allah, Who
established specific names and attributes for
Himself and said that there is nothing like Him. If
acknowledging those names and attributes
requires likening, this would also entail the
existence of contradiction in the words of Allah, as
some parts of them contradict others.
Second: It is unnecessary that two entities
sharing a name or attribute should be similar. We
see, for example, two persons sharing the attributes
of humanity: hearing, seeing, and speaking. Still,
they are not necessarily like each other regarding
human capacities and in their hearing, seeing and
speech.
Likewise, we see animals with hands, legs, and
eyes, but this does not necessarily mean they have
similar hands, legs, or eyes.
If there is a clear difference among the created
beings in terms of the names and attributes they
share, such a difference between the Creator and
His creation is far clearer and greater.
The second group: The Mushabbihah (who draw
comparison), who confirm the names and
30

attributes of Allah. Yet, they likened Him to His
creation, claiming that this meaning is derived from
the relevant texts, for Allah addresses His servants
in the way they understand. This claim is false for
several reasons, such as the following:
First: Likening Allah Almighty to His creation is
established as false by reason and by the Sharia,
and the texts of Qur'an and the Sunnah cannot
entail something false.
Second: Allah Almighty addresses His servants
in the way they understand, in terms of the
fundamental meaning; however, the reality and
essence of this meaning is part of the knowledge
possessed by Allah Almighty alone concerning His
Essence and Attributes.
So, if Allah establishes that He is All-Hearing,
then hearing is indeed known in its fundamental
sense: discerning voices and sounds. But the reality
of this with regard to Allah's hearing is unknown. In
fact, the reality of hearing differs even among the
created beings, and it is even far more different
between the Creator and His creation.
And if Allah Almighty states that He has risen
over the Throne, “Istiwā" (rising over) is known as
a fundamental meaning, but what is unknown to us
is the reality of His rising over the Throne. The
reality of Istiwā' even differs among the created
beings. Rising over a steady chair differs from doing
so over an unruly camel. If this differs among the
31

created beings, there is an even more apparent and
significant difference between the Creator and His
creation.
Belief in Allah yields great benefits for the
believers, such as the following:
First: Fulfilling belief in the Oneness of Allah,
having no hope for or fear from other than Him, and
worshiping none but Him.
Second: Perfecting love and exaltation of Allah
Almighty by virtue of His beautiful Names and
sublime Attributes.
Third: Fulfilling the worship of Allah by
observing His commands and avoiding His
prohibitions.

Belief in the Angels
Angels belong to the realm of the unseen. Allah
Almighty created them, and they worship Him.
They possess nothing of the traits of lordship or
divinity. Allah created them out of light and made
them totally submissive to His commands and
made them capable to implement them. Allah
Almighty says:
... وَمَنْ عِندَهُ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَلَا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ يُسَبِّحُونَ
الَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ لَا يَفْتُرُونَ )
{Those [angels] who are with Him are not too
proud to worship Him, nor do they ever grow
32

weary. They glorify [Him] night and day, never
wavering.} [Surat al-Anbiyā': 19-20]
They are numerous in number; only Allah
Almighty knows their number. It is authentically
reported in the Two Sahīh Collections, in a Hadīth
narrated by Anas (may Allah be pleased with him)
about the story of Al-Mi'raj (ascension), that the
Prophet (ﷺ) was shown Al-Bayt Al-Ma'mūr (The
Frequented House) in heaven, wherein seventy
thousand angels pray every day; when they come
out, they never return to it.
Belief in the angels comprises four things:
First: Belief in their existence.
Second: Belief in those among them whose
names are known to us, like Jibril (Gabriel); and
those whose names are unknown to us, we believe
in them as a whole.
Third: Belief in their descriptions, which are
known to us, like the description of Gabriel. The
Prophet (ﷺ) related that he saw him in his real form
and had six hundred wings blocking the horizon.
By the command of Allah, an angel could turn
into the form of a man. This happened to Gabriel
(peace be upon him) when Allah sent him to Mary
in the form of a man, and when he came to the
Prophet (ﷺ) while he was sitting among his
Companions, he came in the form of a man with
very white clothing and very dark hair, with no
trace of travel apparent on him, and none of the
33
