# The Manner of Performing ‘Umrah

### By Samāhat al-Shaykh ‘Abdul-‘Azīz ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Bāz (may Allah have mercy upon him)

$$\text{بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ}$$

All praise is due to Allah alone, and may Allah's peace and blessings be upon His servant and Messenger. To proceed:

This is an overview of the rituals of ‘Umrah. Here is a further clarification for the reader:

---

## I. Preparation and Assuming Ihrām

### 1. Cleanliness at the Mīqāt
When the performer of ‘Umrah reaches the Mīqāt, it is recommended for him to make Ghusl (ritual bath) and cleanse himself. The same applies to a woman, even if she is menstruating or experiencing post-natal bleeding; however, she should not perform Tawāf around the Ka‘bah until she attains purity and makes Ghusl.

*   **Perfume:** A man may apply perfume to his body but not to his Ihrām clothes. 
*   **Ghusl in Makkah:** If he could not make Ghusl at the Mīqāt, there is nothing wrong, but it is recommended for him to make Ghusl upon reaching Makkah before performing Tawāf, if possible.

### 2. Ihrām Attire
*   **For Men:** A male pilgrim should remove all stitched clothing and put on an upper and lower Ihrām sheet (Ridā’ and Izār). It is recommended that they be white and clean.
*   **For Women:** Women assume Ihrām in their normal clothes that are neither adorned nor prominent, and neither tight-fitting nor transparent.

### 3. Niyyah (Intention) and Talbiyah
The pilgrim makes the intention in his heart to enter into the rituals by saying out loud:

> "Labbayka ‘Umrah" (Here I am to perform ‘Umrah) 
>
> *or* 
>
> "Allāhumma labbayka ‘Umrah" (O Allah, here I am to perform ‘Umrah).

#### Making a Condition (Ishtirāt)
If the Muhrim (pilgrim in Ihrām) fears that he may not be able to complete his rituals due to illness, fear of an enemy, or the like, it is permissible for him to make a condition upon assuming Ihrām, saying:

$$\text{«فَإِنْ حَبَسَنِي حَابِسٌ، فَمَحِلِّي حَيْثُ حَبَسْتَنِي»}$$

> *“If something hinders me, I shall end my Ihrām wherever I am hindered,”* based on the Hadīth of Dubā‘ah bint Az-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with her).[^1]

[^1]: As-Sunan Al-Kubrā by Al-Bayhaqi, No. (10117).

#### Reciting the Talbiyah
He then frequently recites the Talbiyah of the Prophet (ﷺ) until he reaches the Ka‘bah:

$$\text{«لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ»}$$

> *Labbayka allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharīka laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wan-ni‘mata laka wal-mulk, la sharīka lak* 
> 
> (Here I am at Your service, O Allah, here I am at Your service; here I am at Your service, You have no partner, here I am at Your service. Indeed, the praise, the favor, and the dominion belong to You. You have no partner).

He frequently recites this Talbiyah, remembers Allah Almighty, and supplicates to Him. Men should raise their voices with the Talbiyah, while women should lower theirs, as the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) did.

---

## II. Tawāf (Circumambulation)

### 1. Entering the Mosque and Reaching the Black Stone
When the pilgrim reaches the House (the Ka‘bah), he stops reciting the Talbiyah and proceeds to the Black Stone, facing it.

*   **Touching and Kissing:** He should touch it with his right hand and kiss it if possible, without harming people by crowding. Upon touching it, he says: *"Bismillah wa Allahu Akbar"* (In the name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest).
*   **Alternatives:** If kissing is difficult, he may touch it with his hand, a stick, or a similar object and then kiss what he touched. If touching it is difficult, he should point to it and say, *"Allahu Akbar"* (Allah is the Greatest), without kissing the object he is pointing with.

> **Rule on Ritual Purity:** For the validity of Tawāf, it is required that the pilgrim be in a state of ritual purity from both minor and major Hadath (ritual impurity), as Tawāf is akin to prayer, except that speaking is permitted during it.

### 2. Performing the Seven Rounds
He must keep the Ka‘bah to his left and perform Tawāf around it for seven rounds.

*   **The Yemeni Corner:** When he reaches the Yemeni Corner, he should touch it with his right hand if possible and say: *"Bismillah, Allahu Akbar"* without kissing it. If touching is difficult, he should leave it and continue his Tawāf without pointing at it or saying Takbīr, as this was not reported from the Prophet (ﷺ).
*   **The Black Stone:** Whenever he aligns with the Black Stone, he should touch and kiss it as previously mentioned; otherwise, he should point to it and say Takbīr (*Allahu Akbar*).
*   **Ramal:** It is recommended for men to perform Ramal—which is to walk in fast, short steps—during the first three rounds of the Tawāf of Qudūm (Arrival Tawāf).
*   **Idtibā‘:** It is recommended for a man to perform Idtibā‘ throughout all the rounds of the Tawāf of Qudūm. Idtibā‘ consists of placing the middle of his upper robe under his right shoulder and its ends over his left shoulder.
*   **Dhikr and Supplication:** It is recommended to make Dhikr frequently and make supplications with whatever is easy in all the rounds. There is no specific supplication or Dhikr for Tawāf; rather, one should supplicate and remember Allah with whatever is easy. However, between the two corners (the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone), it is Sunnah to say in every round:

$$\text{﴿... رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةٗ وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ حَسَنَةٗ وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ ﴾}$$

> *{Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.}* [Surat al-Baqarah: 201]

He concludes the seventh round by touching and kissing the Black Stone if possible, or pointing to it while saying Takbīr.

### 3. Actions After Tawāf
*   **Ihrām Sheet Adjustment:** After completing the Tawāf, he wears his Ridā’ (upper Ihrām sheet) normally again, placing it over both shoulders with its ends on his chest.
*   **Two Rak‘ahs of Tawāf:** He should offer two Rak‘ahs behind the Maqām (Standing place of Ibrāhīm), if possible; if he is unable to do so, he may offer them anywhere in the mosque.
    *   In the first Rak‘ah, after Al-Fātihah, he recites: *{Say, O disbelievers}* [Surat al-Kāfirūn: 1].
    *   In the second Rak‘ah, after Al-Fātihah, he recites: *{Say: “He is Allah, the One”}* [Surat al-Ikhlās: 1].
    *   There is no harm if he recites other Surahs.
*   **Returning to the Black Stone:** After concluding the two Rak‘ahs with Taslīm, he proceeds to the Black Stone and touches it with his right hand, if possible.
*   **Drinking Zamzam:** It is Sunnah to drink Zamzam water after performing the two Rak‘ahs of Tawāf, if possible.

---

## III. Sa‘y (Walking between Safa and Marwah)

### 1. Commencing at Safa
He then goes out to Safa, ascends it or stands by it, although ascending is preferable if possible. He begins at Safa and says:

$$\text{"نَبْدَأُ بِمَا بَدَأَ اللهُ بِهِ"}$$

> *"We begin with what Allah began with,"*

And he recites the verse:

$$\text{﴿ إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ ٱللَّهِ... ﴾}$$

> *{Indeed, Safa and Marwah [mounts] are among the symbols of Allah...}* [Surat al-Baqarah: 158]

He faces the Qiblah, raises his hands, and praises Allah and supplicates three times, repeating this Prophetic Dhikr:

$$\text{"اللهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللهُ أَكْبَرُ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ، اللهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللهُ أَكْبَرُ وَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَحْدَهُ أَنْجَزَ وَعْدَهُ، وَنَصَرَ عَبْدَهُ، وَهَزَمَ الْأَحْزَابَ وَحْدَهُ".}$$

> *"Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar, lā ilāha illallāh, Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar wa lillāhil-hamd, lā ilāha illallāhu wahdahu lā sharīka lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa ‘ala kulli shay’in qadīr, lā ilāha illallāhu wahdahu anjaza wa‘dah wa nasara ‘abdah wa hazama al-ahzāba wahdah"* 
>
> (Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, there is no deity worthy of worship but Allah, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, and to Allah belongs all praise. None has the right to be worshiped except Allah alone, Who has no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise, and He is competent over all things. There is no deity worthy of worship but Allah alone. He fulfilled His promise, granted His servant victory, and He Alone defeated the Confederates).[^2]

He makes whatever individual supplications are easily possible, repeating the Dhikr and supplication three times.

[^2]: Narrated by Muslim No. (1218).

### 2. Traversing to Marwah
He then descends Safa and proceeds toward Marwah.

*   **Walking Briskly (for Men):** Upon reaching the first green sign, men should walk briskly until they reach the second sign.
*   **Rulings for Women:** It is not prescribed for women to walk briskly between the green signs, as this is not indicated in the Sunnah or the practice of the female Companions, and because they are ‘Awrah.
*   **Arriving at Marwah:** He ascends Marwah or stands by it (ascending is preferable). He performs the exact same Dhikr and supplications as done on Safa, **except** that he does not repeat the verse *{Indeed, Safa and Marwah...}* and does not say *"We begin with what Allah began with."*

### 3. Completing the Seven Rounds
*   He performs Sa‘y for **seven rounds**. The journey from Safa to Marwah counts as one round, and the return from Marwah to Safa counts as another.
*   **Riding:** There is no harm in performing Sa‘y while riding, especially if there is a physical need.
*   **Purity during Sa‘y:** It is recommended to remain in a state of ritual purity (from major and minor Hadath) and make frequent Dhikr during Sa‘y, though performing Sa‘y without being in a state of wudu (purity) is still valid.

---

## IV. Shaving or Shortening the Hair

Once the seven rounds of Sa‘y are completed:

*   **For Men:** A man should either shave his entire head or shorten his hair all over. Shaving is preferable. However, if his arrival in Makkah is close to the season of Hajj, shortening is preferable so that he may shave the rest of his head during the subsequent Hajj rituals.
*   **For Women:** A woman should gather her hair together and cut from the ends the length of a fingertip or less.

---

## V. Completion of ‘Umrah

Once the pilgrim has performed these actions, the ‘Umrah is completed. Everything that was prohibited during the state of Ihrām becomes lawful again.

> *Note on post-’Umrah prayers:* The Prophet (ﷺ) did not pray two Rak‘ahs after completing the Sa‘y of ‘Umrah, so whoever loves him should follow his example.

$$\text{﴿ لَّقَدۡ كَانَ لَكُمۡ فِي رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ أُسۡوَةٌ حَسَنَةٞ لِّمَن كَانَ يَرۡجُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلۡيَوۡمَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَ وَذَكَرَ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرٗا ٢١ ﴾}$$

> *{Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah, you have an excellent example for those who look forward to Allah and the Last Day and remember Allah much.}* [Surat al-Ahzāb: 21]

May Allah grant us and all our fellow Muslims understanding of His religion and steadfastness upon it, and accept from all; indeed, He is Most Generous and Most Bounteous.

May Allah’s peace and blessings be upon His slave and Messenger, our Prophet Muhammad, his family, his Companions, and those who follow them with righteousness until the Day of Judgment.

***

qa_dataset.question: What are the four issues that every Muslim is required to learn as outlined in the introduction of the text, and what textual proof supports them?

qa_dataset.answer: The three issues are: 1) That Allah created us, provided for us, and did not leave us neglected, but sent a messenger whose obedience leads to Paradise and disobedience leads to Hell; 2) That Allah does not accept partners in His worship, whether an angel or prophet; 3) That those who obey the Messenger and believe in Tawhid must not ally with those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they are close relatives. The proof that Allah does not accept partners is Surat al-Jinn, verse 18: 'The mosques are for Allah alone, so do not supplicate anyone along with Allah.'
qa_dataset.question: According to the author, what are the three issues that every Muslim must learn and act upon, and what is the specific proof that Allah does not accept partners in worship?

qa_dataset.answer: The Hanifiyyah is the religion of Abraham, which is to worship Allah alone, sincerely devoting the religion to Him. Tawhid is the greatest command from Allah, meaning to single Him out with worship. Shirk is the gravest sin forbidden by Allah, meaning calling upon others along with Him. The proof is Surat an-Nisa', verse 36: 'Worship Allah and do not associate any partners with Him...'
qa_dataset.question: How does the text define the Hanifiyyah, Tawhid, and Shirk, and what Quranic verse is brought as evidence?

qa_dataset.answer: The three fundamental principles are structured as three essential realizations every person must master regarding their existence: 1) Knowledge of one's Lord (Who created, nourished, and sustains everything); 2) Knowledge of one's religion (Islam, with its evidence and levels); and 3) Knowledge of one's Prophet, Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) (his lineage, mission, and message).
qa_dataset.question: How are the three fundamental principles that every person must know structured, and what are they?

qa_dataset.answer: The three levels are: 1) Islam, which has five pillars (Testimony of faith, establishing prayer, giving Zakah, fasting Ramadan, and performing Hajj); 2) Iman (Faith), which has six pillars (Belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine destiny, both pleasant and unpleasant); and 3) Ihsan (Excellence/Benevolence), which has a single pillar (To worship Allah as if you see Him, for if you cannot see Him, He indeed sees you).
qa_dataset.question: Explain the three levels of the religion of Islam as described in the text, highlighting their respective pillars.

qa_dataset.answer: Citing Ibn al-Qayyim, 'Tāghūt' means everything by which a slave exceeds limits, whether worshiped, followed, or obeyed. The five main Tāghūts are: 1) Satan (may Allah curse him); 2) Anyone worshiped who is content with being worshiped; 3) Anyone who calls people to worship him; 4) Anyone who claims knowledge of the unseen; and 5) Anyone who judges by other than what Allah revealed. The proof of rejection is Surat al-Baqarah, verse 256: 'Whoever rejects Tāghoot and believes in Allah, has indeed grasped the strong handhold that never breaks.'

### بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ

## The Three Fundamental Principles and Their Proofs
#### Shaykh Muhammad at-Tamīmi (may Allah have mercy upon him)

In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful

You should know, may Allah have mercy upon you, that we must learn four issues:

*   **First:** Knowledge, that is to know about Allah, His Prophet, and the religion of Islam with the relevant proofs.
*   **Second:** To act upon this knowledge.
*   **Third:** To call people to it.
*   **Fourth:** To be patient with the harm one receives in the cause.

The evidence is His saying: *Bismillāhir-Rahmān ar-Rahīm* (In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful).

> ﴿ وَالْعَصْرِ ﴿١﴾ إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ ﴿٢﴾ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ ﴿٣﴾ ﴾

{By the time, man is in utter loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and exhort one another to the truth and exhort one another to patience.} \[Surat al-‘Asr: 1-3]

---

# Page 5

Ash-Shāfi‘i (may Allah have mercy upon him) said: “Were this surah to be the only argument that Allah Almighty has sent down upon His creation, it would have been sufficient for them.”

Al-Bukhāri (may Allah have mercy upon him) said: Chapter: "Knowledge comes before statements and actions. The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty: {So know [O Muhammad] that there is no deity except Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin...} [Muhammad: 19]. So He began with knowledge before statements and actions.

Know, may Allah have mercy upon you, that every Muslim, male or female, must learn these three issues and act upon them:

*   **First:** That Allah has created us and provided for us. He did not neglect us, but instead, He sent for us a messenger so that whoever obeys him will enter Paradise and whoever disobeys him will enter the Fire.

The proof is Allah Almighty's saying:

> ﴿ إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ رَسُولًا شَاهِدًا عَلَيْكُمْ كَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولًا ﴿١٥﴾ فَعَصَىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ فَأَخَذْنَاهُ أَخْذًا وَبِيلًا ﴿١٦﴾ ﴾

{Indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger to be a witness over you, just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger. But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a severe punishment.} \[Surat al-Muzzammil: 15-16]

---

# Page 6

*   **Second:** Allah does not accept anyone to be associated with Him in worship, be it a close angel or a sent prophet. The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty:

> ﴿ وَأَنَّ الْمَسَاجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلَا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَدًا ﴿١٨﴾ ﴾

{The mosques are for Allah alone, so do not supplicate anyone along with Allah.} \[Surat al-Jinn: 18]

The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: "Islam is to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish prayer, to pay Zakah, to fast Ramadan, and to perform Hajj to the House if you can find a way thereto." He said: "You have spoken the truth." It surprised us that he asked him and, at the same time, affirmed his truthfulness.

### The third fundamental principle

Knowing your Prophet, Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم): He is Muhammad ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hāshim. Hāshim was from the Quraysh, and Quraysh are from the Arabs, and the Arabs are from the offspring of Ismā‘īl ibn Ibrāhīm (Ishmael, son of Abraham), the intimate friend of Allah (peace be upon him and upon our Prophet).

He lived for sixty-three years, forty of which were before prophethood, and twenty-three as a Prophet and Messenger.

His mission of prophethood started by revealing the verse: {Read...} and he became a messenger by revealing Surat al-Muddaththir, and his city is Makkah.

Allah sent him to warn against polytheism and call to Twahīd. The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty:

---

{O you covered [in your cloak], arise and warn, and proclaim the greatness of your Lord, and purify your garments, and shun idol worshiping, and do not do a favor for a greater return, and be patient for the sake of your Lord.} \[Surat al-Muddaththir: 1-7]

And the meaning of:
> ﴿ قُمْ فَأَنذِرْ ﴾
{arise and warn,} He warns against Shirk (polytheism) and calls to the oneness of Allah.

> ﴿ وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ ﴾
{and proclaim the greatness of your Lord,} i.e., Magnify Him by affirming His Oneness.

> ﴿ وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ ﴾
{and purify your garments,} i.e., purify your deeds from polytheism.

> ﴿ وَالرُّجْزَ فَاهْجُرْ ﴾
{and shun idol worshiping,} Rijz: idols. Abandoning them: leaving them and disassociating from them and their worshipers.

He spent ten years calling to Tawhīd, then he was

---

Hijrah is an obligation upon this Ummah to migrate from the land of polytheism to the land of Islam, and this obligation remains effective until the Hour comes.

After he had settled in Madīnah, he was commanded to observe the other ordinances of Islam, like Zakah, fasting, Hajj, Adhān, Jihad, enjoining what is good, and forbidding what is evil. It took ten years to apply all these ordinances.

The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) passed away, but his religion has remained. This is his religion: he has left no aspect of good except that he guided the Ummah to it and no aspect of evil except that he warned the Ummah against it.

# Three Fundamental Principles and Their Proofs
## (ثَلَاثَةُ الْأُصُولِ وَأَدِلَّتُهَا)

### By Shaykh Muhammad at-Tamimi (may Allah have mercy upon him)

## Introduction: Four Obligatory Issues

In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

You should know, may Allah have mercy upon you, that we must learn four issues:

*   **First:** Knowledge, which is to know about Allah, His Prophet, and the religion of Islam with the relevant proofs.
*   **Second:** To act upon this knowledge.
*   **Third:** To call people to it.
*   **Fourth:** To be patient with the harm one receives in the cause.

The evidence is His saying: *Bismillāhir-Rahmān ar-Rahīm* (In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful):

> ﴿ وَالْعَصْرِ ﴿١﴾ إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ ﴿٢﴾ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ ﴿٣﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{By the time, man is in utter loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and exhort one another to the truth and exhort one another to patience.}* [Surat al-‘Asr: 1-3]

Ash-Shāfi‘i (may Allah have mercy upon him) said: 

> "Were this surah to be the only argument that Allah Almighty has sent down upon His creation, it would have been sufficient for them."

Al-Bukhāri (may Allah have mercy upon him) said: 

> "Chapter: Knowledge comes before statements and actions. The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty: *{So know [O Muhammad] that there is no deity except Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin...}* [Muhammad: 19]. So He began with knowledge before statements and actions."

---

## Three Obligatory Actions for Every Muslim

Know, may Allah have mercy upon you, that every Muslim, male or female, must learn these three issues and act upon them:

### First
That Allah has created us and provided for us. He did not neglect us, but instead, He sent for us a messenger so that whoever obeys him will enter Paradise and whoever disobeys him will enter the Fire.

The proof is Allah Almighty's saying:

> ﴿ إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ رَسُولًا شَاهِدًا عَلَيْكُمْ كَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولًا ﴿١٥﴾ فَعَصَىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ فَأَخَذْنَاهُ أَخْذًا وَبِيلًا ﴿١٦﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{Indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger to be a witness over you, just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger. But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a severe punishment.}* [Surat al-Muzzammil: 15-16]

### Second
Allah does not accept anyone to be associated with Him in worship, be it a close angel or a sent prophet. The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty:

> ﴿ وَأَنَّ الْمَسَاجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلَا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَدًا ﴿١٨﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{The mosques are for Allah alone, so do not supplicate anyone along with Allah.}* [Surat al-Jinn: 18]

### Third
It is impermissible for anyone who obeys the Messenger and believes in the oneness of Allah to be an ally of those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they are the closest relatives.

The proof is Allah Almighty's saying:

> ﴿ لَّا تَجِدُ قَوْمًا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ يُوَادُّونَ مَنْ حَادَّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَلَوْ كَانُوا آبَاءَهُمْ أَوْ أَبْنَاءَهُمْ أَوْ إِخْوَانَهُمْ أَوْ عَشِيرَتَهُمْ ۚ أُولَٰئِكَ كَتَبَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْإِيمَانَ وَأَيَّدَهُم بِرُوحٍ مِّنْهُ ۖ وَيُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا ۚ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ ۚ أُولَٰئِكَ حِزْبُ اللَّهِ ۚ أَلَا إِنَّ حِزْبُ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ ﴿٢٢﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{You will not find any people who believe in Allah and the Last Day taking as allies those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their parents, their children, their brothers, or their kindred. It is they in whose hearts Allah has instilled faith and strengthened them with a spirit from Him. He will admit them to gardens under which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Allah. They are the party of Allah. Indeed, it is the party of Allah that will be successful.}* [Surat al-Mujādalah: 22]

## The Hanifiyyah (The Religion of Abraham)

Know—may Allah guide you to His obedience—that the *Hanifiyyah*, the religion of Ibrahīm (Abraham), is to worship Allah alone, sincerely devoting the religion to Him. And with that, Allah commanded all people and created them for it, as He Almighty said:

> ﴿ وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ ﴿٥٦﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{I have not created the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.}* [Surat adh-Dhāriyāt: 56] 

The meaning of "to worship Me" is: to single Me out with worship.

*   **Tawhīd** (Oneness of Allah) is the greatest command from Allah to His slaves, and it means singling Him out with worship.
*   **Shirk** (polytheism) is the gravest sin that Allah has forbidden His slaves from, and it means calling upon others along with Him.

The proof is Allah Almighty's saying:

> ﴿ وَاعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَلَا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا... ﴾
> 
> *{Worship Allah and do not associate any partners with Him...}* [Surat an-Nisā’: 36]

## The Three Fundamental Principles

If someone asks you: *"What are the three fundamental principles that every person must know?"*

Say: **One must know his Lord, his religion, and his Prophet, Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم).**

---

### The First Fundamental Principle: Knowledge of the Lord

If you are asked: *"Who is your Lord?"*

You should say: *"My Lord is Allah, Who nourished me and nourished all the worlds with His bounties. He is my deity, and I worship none but Him."* The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty:

> ﴿ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ ﴿٢﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{All praise be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.}* [Surat al-Fātihah: 2] 

Everything other than Allah is a world (*'ālam*), and I am one of that world.

If you are asked: *"How did you come to know your Lord?"*

You should say: *"Through His signs and through His creatures."*

*   **From among His signs are:** the night and the day, and the sun and the moon.
*   **Among His creatures are:** the seven heavens and all that is in them, the seven earths and all that is in them, and all that exists between them.

The proof is Allah Almighty's saying:

> ﴿ وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ اللَّيْلُ وَالنَّهَارُ وَالشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ ۚ لَا تَسْجُدُوا لِلشَّمْسِ وَلَا لِلْقَمَرِ وَاسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ الَّذِي خَلَقَهُنَّ إِن كُنتُمْ إِيَّاهُ تَعْبُدُونَ ﴿٣٧﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{Among His signs are the night and the day, the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah Who created them, if you truly worship Him}* [Surat Fussilat: 37]

And the verse that reads:

> ﴿ إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ يَطْلُبُهُ حَثِيثًا وَالشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ وَالنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّرَاتٍ بِأَمْرِهِ ۗ أَلَا لَهُ الْخَلْقُ وَالْأَمْرُ ۗ تَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ ﴿٥٤﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{Your Lord is Allah, Who created the heavens and earth in six days and then rose over [i.e., istawa] the Throne. He makes the night and day overlap in rapid succession. He made the sun, the moon, and the stars — all subservient to His command. Behold, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, the Lord of the worlds.}* [Surat al-A‘rāf: 54]

The "Lord" means: the worshiped god. The proof is Allah Almighty's saying:

> ﴿ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ ﴿٢١﴾ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ فِرَاشًا وَالسَّمَاءَ بِنَاءً وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ رِزْقًا لَّكُمْ ۖ فَلَا تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ أَندَادًا وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ ﴿٢٢﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{O people, worship your Lord, Who created you and those before you, so that you may become righteous; He Who made the earth a resting place for you, and the sky a canopy; and sends down rain from the sky, and brings forth fruits thereby as a provision for you. So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know.}* [Surat al-Baqarah: 21-22]

Ibn Kathīr (may Allah have mercy upon him) said: 

> “The Creator of these things is the One Who alone deserves to be worshiped.”

#### Types of Worship Commanded by Allah
The types of worship that Allah has commanded include: Islam, Imān (faith), Ihsān (excellence in worship), Du‘ā’ (supplication), Khawf (fear), Rajā’ (hope), Tawakkul (reliance), Raghbah (aspiration), Rahbah (awe), Khushū‘ (submission/humility), Khashyah (apprehension), Inābah (repentance), Isti‘ānah (seeking help), Isti‘ādhah (seeking refuge), Istighāthah (seeking relief), Dhabh (sacrificing/slaughtering), Nadhr (making vows), and other acts of worship commanded by Allah.

All acts of worship must be offered exclusively to Allah. The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty:

> ﴿ وَأَنَّ الْمَسَاجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلَا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَدًا ﴿١٨﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{The mosques are for Allah alone, so do not supplicate anyone along with Allah.}* [Surat al-Jinn: 18]

Whoever dedicates any such acts of worship to other than Allah is a polytheist and disbeliever. The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty:

> ﴿ وَمَن يَدْعُ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا آخرَ لَا بُرْهَانَ لَهُ بِهِ فَإِنَّمَا حِسَابُهُ عِندَ رَبِّهِ ۚ إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الْكَافِرُونَ ﴿١١٧﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{Whoever invokes another god besides Allah, for which he has no proof, his reckoning will be with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will never succeed.}* [Surat al-Mu’minūn: 117]

#### Proofs for Individual Acts of Worship

*   **Du‘ā’ (Supplication):**
    The Hadīth states:
    > "الدُّعَاءُ مُخُّ الْعِبَادَةِ"
    > *“Supplication is the essence of worship.”*
    
    The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty:
    > ﴿ وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِي سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ ﴿٦٠﴾ ﴾
    > *{Your Lord says, “Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, utterly debased.”}* [Surat Ghāfir: 60]

*   **Khawf (Fear):**
    > ﴿ ...فَلَا تَخَافُوهُمْ وَخَافُونِ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ ﴾
    > *{Do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are [true] believers.}* [Surat Āl ‘Imrān: 175]

*   **Rajā’ (Hope):**
    > ﴿ ...فَمَن كَانَ يَرْجُو لِقَاءَ رَبِّهِ فَلْيَعْمَلْ عَمَلًا صَالِحًا وَلَا يُشْرِكْ بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِ أَحَدًا ﴾
    > *{So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and associate none in the worship of his Lord.}* [Surat al-Kahf: 110]

*   **Tawakkul (Reliance):**
    > ﴿ ...وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَتَوَكَّلُوا إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ ﴾
    > *{And put your trust in Allah, if you are believers.}* [Surat al-Ma’idah: 23]
    
    And:
    > ﴿ ...وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ... ﴾
    > *{Whoever puts his trust in Allah, He is sufficient for him.}* [Surat at-Talāq: 3]

*   **Raghbah (Aspiration), Rahbah (Awe), and Khushū‘ (Submission):**
    > ﴿ ...إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا ۖ وَكَانُوا لَنَا خَاشِعِينَ ﴾
    > *{They used to hasten in doing good deeds and used to call upon Us with hope and fear, and they were humble before Us.}* [Surat al-Anbiyā’: 90]

*   **Khashyah (Apprehension):**
    > ﴿ ...فَلَا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَاخْشَوْنِ... ﴾
    > *{So do not fear them but fear Me.}* [Surat al-Mā’idah: 3]

*   **Inābah (Repentance):**
    > ﴿ وَأَنِيبُوا إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ وَأَسْلِمُوا لَهُ... ﴾
    > *{Turn to your Lord [in repentance] and submit to Him...}* [Surat az-Zumar: 54]

*   **Isti‘ānah (Seeking Help):**
    > ﴿ إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ ﴿٥﴾ ﴾
    > *{You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.}* [Surat al-Fātihah: 5]
    
    The Hadīth reads:
    > "إِذَا اسْتَعَنْتَ فَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ"
    > *“When you seek help, seek it from Allah.”*

*   **Isti‘ādhah (Seeking Refuge):**
    > ﴿ قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ ﴿١﴾ ﴾
    > *{Say, “I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak,”}* [Surat al-Falaq: 1], and:
    > ﴿ قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ ﴿١﴾ ﴾
    > *{Say, “I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind,}* [Surat an-Nās: 1]

*   **Istighāthah (Seeking Relief):**
    > ﴿ إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ فَاسْتَجَابَ لَكُمْ... ﴾
    > *{[Remember] when you were seeking the help of your Lord and He responded to you...}* [Surat al-Anfāl: 9]

*   **Dhabh (Slaughtering/Sacrifice):**
    > ﴿ قُلْ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحْيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ ﴿١٦٢﴾ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ... ﴾
    > *{Say, “Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are all for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner...}* [Surat al-An‘ām: 162-163]
    
    The proof from the Sunnah:
    > "لَعَنَ اللَّهُ مَنْ ذَبَحَ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ"
    > *“Allah curses whoever slaughters a sacrifice to anyone other than Allah.”*

*   **Nadhr (Vows):**
    > ﴿ يُوفُونَ بِالنَّذْرِ وَيَخَافُونَ يَوْمًا كَانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيرًا ﴿٧﴾ ﴾
    > *{They fulfill their vows and fear a Day whose evil will spread far and wide,}* [Surat al-Insān: 7]

---

### The Second Fundamental Principle: Knowledge of the Religion of Islam

**Islam** is submitting to Allah by Tawhīd (monotheism), compliance to Him by obedience, and dissociating oneself from Shirk (polytheism) and its people.

It has three levels: **Islam**, **Imān**, and **Ihsān**. Each level has specific pillars.

#### Level 1: Islam
The pillars of Islam are five:
1.  **The Testimony of Faith (Shahādah):** Bearing witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.
2.  **Establishing Prayer (Salāh).**
3.  **Giving Zakah (Charity).**
4.  **Fasting the month of Ramadān.**
5.  **Performing Hajj** to the Sacred House of Allah.

##### The Proof of the Testimony of Faith:
> ﴿ شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَأُولُو الْعِلْمِ قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ ۚ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ ﴿١٨﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{Allah testifies that none has the right to be worshiped except Him, as do the angels and people of knowledge; He is the Upholder of justice. None has the right to be worshiped except Him, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.}* [Surat Āl ‘Imrān: 18]

Meaning of the Shahādah:
*   *"No god"* is a negation of all that is worshiped other than Allah.
*   *"except Allah"* is an affirmation that worship is due to Allah alone.
*   Allah has no partner in His worship, just as He has no partner in His dominion.

This is further explained in:
> ﴿ وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّنِي بَرَاءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ ﴿٢٦﴾ إِلَّا الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي... ﴾
> 
> *{And [remember] when Abraham said to his father and his people, “I disown all that you worship, except the One Who created me...}* [Surat az-Zukhruf: 26-27]
> 
> ﴿ قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ تَعَالَوْا إِلَىٰ كَلِمَةٍ سَوَاءٍ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ أَلَّا نَعْبُدَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ وَلَا نُشْرِكَ بِهِ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُنَا بَعْضًا أَرْبَابًا مِّن دُونِ اللَّهِ ۚ فَإِن تَوَلَّوا فَقُولُوا اشْهَدُوا بِأَنَّا مُسْلِمُونَ ﴿٦٤﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{Say, “O people of the Book, come to a common term between us and you, that we worship none but Allah and associate no partners with Him, and that we do not take one another as lords besides Allah.” But if they turn away, say, “Bear witness that we are Muslims [submitting to Allah].”}* [Surat Āl ‘Imrān: 64]

##### The Proof of Testifying that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah:
> ﴿ لَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ مَا عَنِتُّمْ حَرِيصٌ عَلَيْكُم بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَءُوفٌ رَّحِيمٌ ﴿١٢٨﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{There has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; he is grieved by your suffering, and is concerned for you, and is gracious and merciful towards the believers.}* [Surat at-Tawbah: 128]

The meaning of testifying that “Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah” is: to obey his orders, believe what he reported, avoid what he forbade and warned against, and worship Allah only in the manner he instructed.

##### The Proof of Prayer and Zakah:
> ﴿ وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ حُنَفَاءَ وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكَاةَ ۚ وَذَٰلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ ﴿٥﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{Although they were commanded only to worship Allah with sincere devotion to Him, being inclined to the true faith, and to establish prayer and give zakah; that is the true religion.}* [Surat al-Bayyinah: 5]

##### The Proof of Fasting:
> ﴿ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ ﴿١٨٣﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{O you who believe, fasting is prescribed upon you as it was prescribed upon those who were before you, so that you may become righteous.}* [Surat al-Baqarah: 183]

##### The Proof of Hajj:
> ﴿ ...وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا ۚ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنِ الْعَالَمِينَ ﴿٩٧﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah upon all people who are able to make their way to it; whoever disbelieves, then Allah is in no need for the worlds.}* [Surat Āl ‘Imrān: 97]

---

#### Level 2: Imān (Faith)
Imān has over seventy branches, the most excellent of which is the declaration that there is no god but Allah, and the lowest of which is the removal of what is harmful from the path; and modesty is a branch of faith.

Its **six pillars** are:
1.  Belief in **Allah**
2.  Belief in His **angels**
3.  Belief in His **books**
4.  Belief in His **messengers**
5.  Belief in the **Last Day**
6.  Belief in **Al-Qadar** (destiny), both its pleasant and unpleasant aspects.

##### The Proof of the Six Pillars of Faith:
> ﴿ لَّيْسَ الْبِرَّ أَن تُوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ قِبَلَ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ وَلَٰكِنَّ الْبِرَّ مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالْكِتَابِ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ... ﴾
> 
> *{It is not righteousness to turn your faces towards the east or the west, but righteousness is to believe in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Scriptures, and the prophets...}* [Surat al-Baqarah: 177]

##### The Proof of Belief in Destiny (Al-Qadar):
> ﴿ إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ بِقَدَرٍ ﴿٤٩﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{We have surely created everything in a determined measure.}* [Surat al-Qamar: 49]

---

#### Level 3: Ihsān (Excellence/Benevolence)
Ihsān has **one pillar**: to worship Allah as if you see Him, for if you cannot see Him, He indeed sees you.

##### Proofs of Ihsān:
> ﴿ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوا وَّالَّذِينَ هُم مُّحْسِنُونَ ﴿١٢٨﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who do good.}* [Surat an-Nahl: 128]
> 
> ﴿ وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى الْعَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ ﴿٢١٧﴾ الَّذِي يَرَاكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ ﴿٢١٨﴾ وَتَقَلُّبَكَ فِي السَّاجِدِينَ ﴿٢١٩﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{And put your trust in the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful, Who sees you when you stand up [for prayer] and your movements among those who prostrate.}* [Surat ash-Shu‘arā’: 217-219]
> 
> ﴿ وَمَا تَكُونُ فِي شَأْنٍ وَمَا تَتْلُو مِنْهُ مِن قُرْآنٍ وَلَا تَعْمَلُونَ مِنْ عَمَلٍ إِلَّا كُنَّا عَلَيْكُمْ شُهُودًا إِذْ تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ... ﴾
> 
> *{Whatever matter you [O Prophet] may be engaged in, and whatever portion of the Qur’an you may recite, and whatever deed you [O people] may do, We are a Witness over you when you are engaged in it...}* [Surat Yūnus: 61]

##### The Proof from the Sunnah (The Hadīth of Gabriel):
Narrated on the authority of ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb (may Allah be pleased with him):

> "بَيْنَمَا نَحْنُ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ، إِذْ طَلَعَ عَلَيْنَا رَجُلٌ، شَدِيدُ بَيَاضِ الثِّيَابِ، شَدِيدُ سَوَادِ الشَّعَرِ، لَا يُرَى عَلَيْهِ أَثَرُ السَّفَرِ، وَلَا يَعْرِفُهُ مِنَّا أَحَدٌ، حَتَّى جَلَسَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَسْنَدَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ إِلَى رُكْبَتَيْهِ، وَوَضَعَ كَفَّيْهِ عَلَى فَخِذَيْهِ، وَقَالَ: يَا مُحَمَّدُ! أَخْبِرْنِي عَنِ الْإِسْلَامِ؟ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: الْإِسْلَامُ: أَنْ تَشْهَدَ أَلَّا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، وَتُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةَ، وَتُؤْتِيَ الزَّكَاةَ، وَتَصُومَ رَمَضَانَ، وَتَحُجَّ الْبَيْتَ إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا، قَالَ: صَدَقْتَ - فَعَجِبْنَا لَهُ، يَسْأَلُهُ وَيُصَدِّقُهُ -. قَالَ: فَأَخْبِرْنِي عَنِ الْإِيمَانِ؟ قَالَ: أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللَّهِ، وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ، وَكُتُبِهِ، وَرُسُلِهِ، وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ، وَتُؤْمِنَ بِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ، قَالَ: صَدَقْتَ. قَالَ: فَأَخْبِرْنِي عَنِ الْإِحْسَانِ؟ قَالَ: أَنْ تَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ كَأَنَّكَ تَرَاهُ، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ تَرَاهُ فَإِنَّهُ يَرَاكَ. قَالَ: فَأَخْبِرْنِي عَنِ السَّاعَةِ؟ قَالَ: مَا الْمَسْؤُولُ عَنْهَا بِأَعْلَمَ مِنَ السَّائلِ. قَالَ: فَأَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ أَمَارَاتِهَا؟ قَالَ: أَنْ تَلِدَ الْأَمَةُ رَبَّتَهَا، وَأَنْ تَرَى الْحُفَاةَ الْعُرَاةَ الْعَالَةَ رِعَاءَ الشَّاءِ، يَتَطَاوَلُونَ فِي الْبُنْيَانِ. قَالَ: ثُمَّ انْطَلَقَ فَلَبِثْتُ مَلِيًّا، ثُمَّ قَالَ لِي: يَا عُمَرُ! أَتَدْرِي مَنِ السَّائِلُ؟ قُلْتُ: اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ، قَالَ: فَإِنَّهُ جِبْرِيلُ، أَتَاكُمْ يُعَلِّمُكُمْ دِينَكُمْ."
> 
> *While we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) one day, there appeared before us a man dressed in extremely white clothes and having very black hair. No traces of travel were visible on him, and none of us knew him. He sat down in front of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم), rested his knees against his knees, and placed his palms on his thighs. He said: "O Muhammad! Tell me about Islam."*
> 
> *The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: "Islam is to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish prayer, to pay Zakah, to fast Ramadan, and to perform Hajj to the House if you can find a way thereto." He said: "You have spoken the truth." It surprised us that he asked him and, at the same time, affirmed his truthfulness.*
> 
> *He said: "So, tell me about Imān."*
> 
> *He said: "To believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and to believe in destiny, the pleasant and unpleasant aspects thereof." He said: "You have spoken the truth."*
> 
> *He said: "Tell me about Ihsān (benevolence)."*
> 
> *He said: “To worship Allah as if you see Him; if you do not see Him, He sees you.”*
> 
> *He said: "Tell me about the Last Hour."*
> 
> *He said: "The one who is asked about it has no more knowledge than the one who asked."*
> 
> *He said: "Then tell me about its signs."*
> 
> *He said: “That the slave-girl will give birth to her mistress, and that you will see the barefoot, naked, poor shepherds of sheep competing in the construction of buildings.”*
> 
> *Then he departed, and I stayed for a while. Then he said to me: "O ‘Umar, do you know who the questioner was?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "He was Jibrīl (Gabriel). He came to teach you your religion."*

### The Third Fundamental Principle: Knowledge of the Prophet Muhammad

He is Muhammad ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hāshim. 
*   Hāshim was from the **Quraysh**, and Quraysh are from the **Arabs**, and the Arabs are from the offspring of **Ismā‘īl ibn Ibrāhīm** (Ishmael, son of Abraham), the intimate friend of Allah (peace be upon him and upon our Prophet).
*   He lived for **sixty-three years**: forty of which were before prophethood, and twenty-three as a Prophet and Messenger.
*   His prophethood started with the revelation of *{Read...}* (Surat al-Alaq), and he became a Messenger with *Surat al-Muddaththir*. His home city was **Makkah**.

Allah sent him to warn against polytheism and call to Tawhīd. The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty:

> ﴿ يَا أَيُّهَا الْمُدَّثِّرُ ﴿١﴾ قُمْ فَأَنذِرْ ﴿٢﴾ وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ ﴿٣﴾ وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ ﴿٤﴾ وَالرُّجْزَ فَاهْجُرْ ﴿٥﴾ وَلَا تَمْنُن تَسْتَكْثِرُ ﴿٦﴾ وَلِرَبِّكَ فَاصْبِرْ ﴿٧﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{O you covered [in your cloak], arise and warn, and proclaim the greatness of your Lord, and purify your garments, and shun idol worshiping, and do not do a favor for a greater return, and be patient for the sake of your Lord.}* [Surat al-Muddaththir: 1-7]

#### Explanation of the Verses:
*   *{arise and warn,}* He warns against Shirk (polytheism) and calls to the oneness of Allah.
*   *{and proclaim the greatness of your Lord,}* i.e., Magnify Him by affirming His Oneness.
*   *{and purify your garments,}* i.e., purify your deeds from polytheism.
*   *{and shun idol worshiping,}* *Rijz* refers to idols. Abandoning them means leaving them, disassociating from them, and separating from their worshipers.

He spent ten years in Makkah calling to Tawhīd, then he was taken on a journey to heaven (the *Mi'raj*), where the five obligatory prayers were enjoined upon him. He prayed in Makkah for three years, and was then commanded to migrate to Madīnah.

---

## Hijrah (Migration)

**Hijrah** is moving from the land of polytheism to the land of Islam. Hijrah is an obligation upon this Ummah to migrate from the land of polytheism to the land of Islam, and this obligation remains effective until the Hour comes.

The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty:

> ﴿ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ ظَالِمِي أَنفُسِهِمْ قَالُوا فِيمَ كُنتُمْ ۖ قَالُوا كُنَّا مُسْتَضْعَفِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ ۚ قَالُوا أَلَمْ تَكُنْ أَرْضُ اللَّهِ وَاسِعَةً فَتُهَاجِرُوا فِيهَا ۚ فَأُولَٰئِكَ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ ۖ وَسَاءَتْ مَصِيرًا ﴿٩٧﴾ إِلَّا الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ وَالنِّسَاءِ وَالْوِلْدَانِ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةً وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلًا ﴿٩٨﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{When the angels take the souls of those who have wronged themselves, they will say, “What was the matter with you?” They will say, “We were oppressed in the land.” They will say, “Was not Allah’s earth spacious enough for you to migrate?” They are those whose refuge will be Hell — what a terrible destination! Except the helpless men, women, and children who have no means nor do they know where to go.}* [Surat an-Nisā’: 97-98]

And:

> ﴿ يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَاعْبُدُونِ ﴿٥٦﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{O My believing slaves, My earth is spacious, so worship Me alone.}* [Surat al-‘Ankabūt: 56]

Al-Baghawi (may Allah have mercy upon him) said: 

> "This verse was revealed in connection with the Muslims who stayed in Makkah and did not migrate. Allah called them His believing slaves."

The proof from the Sunnah is the saying of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم):
> "لَا تَنْقَطِعُ الْهِجْرَةُ حَتَّى تَنْقَطِعَ التَّوْبَةُ، وَلَا تَنْقَطِعُ التَّوْبَةُ حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ مِنْ مَغْرِبِهَا"
> *“Hijrah (migration) does not cease until repentance ceases, and repentance does not cease until the sun rises from the west.”*

---

## Establishing the Islamic State and Finality of Prophethood

After he had settled in Madīnah, he was commanded to observe the other ordinances of Islam, such as Zakah, fasting, Hajj, Adhān, Jihad, enjoining what is good, and forbidding what is evil. It took ten years to apply all these ordinances.

The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) passed away, but his religion has remained. This is his religion: he left no aspect of good except that he guided the Ummah to it, and no aspect of evil except that he warned the Ummah against it.

*   **The good he guided the Ummah to** is Tawhīd and all that Allah loves and is pleased with.
*   **The evil he warned the Ummah against** is polytheism (Shirk) and all that Allah dislikes and disapproves.

Allah sent him to all mankind, and made it obligatory on mankind and the jinn to obey him. The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty:

> ﴿ قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ جَمِيعًا... ﴾
> 
> *{Say [O Prophet], “O people, I am the Messenger of Allah to you all...}* [Surat al-A‘rāf: 158]

And Allah completed the religion through him; and the proof is the saying of Allah Almighty:

> ﴿ ...الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكَمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الْإِسْلَامَ دِينًا... ﴾
> 
> *{Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favor upon you, and have chosen Islam as your religion.}* [Surat al-Mā’idah: 3]

The proof of his death is the saying of Allah Almighty:

> ﴿ إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وَإ وإنَّهُم مَّيِّتُونَ ﴿٣٠﴾ ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ عِندَ رَبِّكُمْ تَخْتَصِمُونَ ﴿٣١﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{You [O Prophet] will surely die, and they too will die; then on the Day of Resurrection, you will dispute with one another before your Lord.}* [Surat az-Zumar: 30-31]

---

## Resurrection, Accountability, and Messengers

People will be resurrected after their death. The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty:

> ﴿ مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ تَارَةً أُخْرَىٰ ﴿٥٥﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{From this [earth] We created you, and to it We will return you, and from it We will raise you once again.}* [Surat Taha: 55]
> 
> ﴿ وَاللَّهُ أَنبَتَكُم مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًا ﴿١٧﴾ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا ﴿١٨﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{Allah has produced you from the earth like a plant, then He will return you into it and then will bring you out again.}* [Surat Nūh: 17-18]

After resurrection, they will be called to account and receive recompense according to their deeds. The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty:

> ﴿ ...لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسَاءُوا بِمَا عَمِلُوا وَيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا بِالْحُسْنَى ﴾
> 
> *{...so that He may recompense the evildoers for what they did, and reward those who do good with the best reward,}* [Surat an-Najm: 31]

Denying the resurrection is disbelief (*kufr*). The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty:

> ﴿ زَعَمَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَن لَّن يُبْعَثُوا ۚ قُلْ بَلَىٰ وَرَبِّي لَتُبْعَثُنَّ ثُمَّ لَتُنَبَّؤُنَّ بِمَا عَمِلْتُمْ ۚ وَذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ ﴿٧﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{The disbelievers claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, “Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, and then you will surely be informed of what you did. And that is easy for Allah.”}* [Surat at-Taghābun: 7]

Allah sent all the messengers as bearers of glad tidings and as warners. The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty:

> ﴿ رُّسُلًا مُّبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى اللَّهِ حُجَّةٌ بَعْدَ الرُّسُلِ... ﴾
> 
> *{These messengers were sent as bearers of glad tidings and as warners, so that the people may have no excuse before Allah after [the coming of] the messengers.}* [Surat an-Nisā’: 165]

*   The **first** of these messengers was **Noah** (Nūh) (peace be upon him).
*   The **last** of them is **Muhammad** (صلى الله عليه وسلم), and he is the seal of the prophets; there will be no prophet after him.

> ﴿ مَّا كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبَا أَحَدٍ مِّن رِّجَالِكُمْ وَلَٰكِن رَّسُولَ اللَّهِ وَخَاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ... ﴾
> 
> *{Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the seal of the prophets...}* [Surat al-Ahzāb: 40]

The proof that Noah was the first messenger is the saying of Allah Almighty:

> ﴿ إِنَّا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ كَمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ مِن بَعْدِهِ... ﴾
> 
> *{We have sent revelation to you [O Prophet] just as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him...}* [Surat an-Nisā’: 163]

Every nation to which Allah sent a messenger, from the time of Noah to Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم), was commanded to worship Allah alone and forbidden to worship the *Tāghūt* (false gods).

> ﴿ وَلَقَدْ بَعَثْنَا فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَّسُولًا أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاجْتَنِبُوا الطَّاغُوتَ... ﴾
> 
> *{Indeed, We sent to every community a messenger, [saying], “Worship Allah and shun false gods...”}* [Surat an-Nahl: 36]

---

## Belief in Allah and Rejection of the Tāghūt

Allah has enjoined upon all people to disbelieve in false gods (*Tāghūt*) and believe in Allah.

Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy upon him) said: 

> "Tāghūt means everything by which a slave goes beyond limits, whether one who is worshipped, or followed, or obeyed."

The *Tāghūts* are many, and the **main five** are:
1.  **Satan** (may Allah curse him).
2.  The one who is worshiped while he is **content with it**.
3.  The one who **calls others** to worship him.
4.  The one who **claims knowledge of the unseen**.
5.  The one who **judges according to anything other than what Allah has revealed**.

The proof is the saying of Allah Almighty:

> ﴿ لَا إِكْرَاهَ فِي الدِّينِ ۖ قَد تَّبَيَّنَ الرُّشْدُ مِنَ الْغَيِّ ۚ فَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِالطَّاغُوتِ وَيُؤْمِن بِالطَّاغُوتِ وَيُؤْمِن بِاللَّهِ فَقَدِ اسْتَمْسَكَ بِالْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقَىٰ لَا انفِصَامَ لَهَا ۗ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ ﴿٢٥٦﴾ ﴾
> 
> *{There is no compulsion in religion; the truth has been made distinct from falsehood. Whoever rejects Tāghoot [i.e., false gods] and believes in Allah, has indeed grasped the strong handhold that never breaks. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.}* [Surat al-Baqarah: 256] 

This is the very meaning of *“There is no deity worthy of worship but Allah.”*

In the Hadīth:
> "رَأْسُ الْأَمْرِ: الْإِسْلَامُ، وَعَمُودُهُ: الصَّلَاةُ، وَذِرْوَةُ سَنَامِهِ: الْجِهَادُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ"
> 
> *“The essence of the matter is Islam, its pillar is the prayer, and its highest peak is Jihad in the cause of Allah.”*

And Allah knows best.

qa_dataset.answer: An Essential Part (Rukn) of 'Umrah, such as Ihram, Tawaf, or Sa'i, is fundamental to the validity of the pilgrimage; if omitted, the 'Umrah remains invalid and cannot be completed unless the omitted pillar is performed. In contrast, an Obligatory Part (Wajib), such as entering Ihram from the designated miqat or shaving/cutting the hair, can be compensated for if omitted. If a Wajib is left out deliberately or forgetfully, the pilgrim incurs a penalty (fidyah) but the 'Umrah remains structurally valid.
qa_dataset.question: What are the structural differences between an Essential Part (Rukn) and an Obligatory Part (Wajib) of 'Umrah according to Islamic jurisprudence as presented in the text?

qa_dataset.answer: According to the guidelines, the pilgrim must form the intention and enter the state of Ihram on the aircraft when it comes in line with one of the designated miqats before landing. Jeddah itself is not a miqat for non-residents. If the pilgrim has no physical Ihram garments with him on the plane, he must keep his trousers on, remove his thobe, place it over his shoulders and chest, and make the intention. Upon landing at the airport, he must immediately acquire and put on the proper Ihram garments and remove his trousers. Delaying Ihram until landing in Jeddah constitutes a violation of the miqat boundary, requiring a fidyah (sacrificing an animal).
qa_dataset.question: An international pilgrim travels by air directly to Jeddah with the intention of performing 'Umrah. Based on the protocols in the booklet, what is the correct procedure for entering Ihram, and what are the specific implications of landing in Jeddah before doing so?

qa_dataset.answer: If a pilgrim commits an infraction due to a necessity, it is permissible to do so, but they must offer a compensatory fidyah. The pilgrim is given a choice among three remedies: (a) fasting for three consecutive or separate days, (b) feeding six poor persons with half a sa' (approximately 1.5 kilograms) of food each, or (c) slaughtering a sheep and distributing all its meat to the poor of the Haram zone.
qa_dataset.question: What options are available to a pilgrim who violates the prohibitions of Ihram (e.g., cutting hair, using perfume, or wearing stitched clothing) due to a genuine physical need or medical condition?

qa_dataset.answer: Ishtirat is a recommended condition formulated when a pilgrim entering Ihram fears that sickness, an enemy, or an emergency might prevent them from completing the 'Umrah. The pilgrim utters: 'Fa in habasani habis fa mahilli haythu habastani' (If anything prevents me from continuing, then my place of exiting ihram will be where You caused me to be prevented). The legal benefit of this condition is that if the pilgrim is subsequently blocked or incapacitated, they are permitted to exit the state of Ihram immediately at that location without having to perform any compensatory animal sacrifice (fidyah) or penalty.
qa_dataset.question: Explain the concept, execution, and legal benefit of the conditional intention (Ishtirat) in Ihram.

qa_dataset.answer: Sa'i consists of seven laps starting at as-Safa and ending at al-Marwah (going from Safa to Marwah is one lap; returning is the second). At the beginning of the first lap only, upon drawing close to as-Safa, the pilgrim recites verse 2:158 of Surat al-Baqarah. At both hills, the pilgrim faces the Qiblah, raises their hands, and recites a specific declaration of monotheism three times, interspersed with personal supplications. During the physical walk between the hills, the pilgrim maintains a normal walking pace except when crossing the zone bounded by two green markers, where it is Sunnah to run as quickly as possible without causing annoyance to others.
qa_dataset.question: Detail the spatial markers, speed variations, and specific scriptural utterances required during the performance of Sa'i.

qa_dataset.answer: For game with an equivalent livestock animal, the pilgrim chooses between: (1) slaughtering the equivalent animal and distributing its meat to the poor of the Haram, (2) buying food equal to the animal's value and distributing it to the poor (half a sa' per person), or (3) fasting one day for each poor person that would have been fed. For game with no equivalent (like locusts), the pilgrim must determine the monetary value of the killed animal and choose between: (1) distributing that value in food to the poor (half a sa' per person), or (2) fasting one day for each poor person.
qa_dataset.question: How does the penalty structure differ for hunting violations during Ihram based on whether the hunted game has a domestic livestock equivalent?

Introduction

The miqats and entering ihram

The miqats are the places at which it is obligatory to enter ihram for the one who wants to do `umrah. The Sunnah has defined the places which the one who wants to do `umrah is not allowed to pass without being in the state of ihram. There are five miqats: **Dhul-Hulayfah:** which is now called Abyar `Ali. It is the miqat of the people of Madinah and whoever else passes through it. It is approximately 420 km from Makkah al-Mukarramah. **Al-Juhfah:** which is a village near Rabigh. It is the miqat of the people of Syria, Egypt and the Maghreb (North Africa), and whoever else passes through it. It is approximately 186 km from Makkah al-Mukarramah. The people enter ihram from Rabigh. **Qarn al-Manazil:** which is now called as-Sayl al-Kabir. It is the miqat of the people of Najd and at-Ta'if, and whoever else passes through it. It is approximately 78 km from Makkah al-Mukarramah. Wadi Mahram is in line with it; it is the highest part of Qarn al-Manazil in the direction of the Al-Hada Highway. It is approximately 75 km from Makkah al-Mukarramah. **Yalamlam:** which is the miqat of the people of Yemen and whoever else passes through it. It is approximately 120 km from Makkah al-Mukarramah. **Dhat `Irq:** which is now called ad-Daribah. It is the miqat of the people of Iraq and whoever else passes through it. It is approximately 100 km from Makkah al-Mukarramah. --- ## Page 9

8

Whoever lives closer [to Makkah] than these miqats should enter ihram for Hajj and `umrah from his house, except for one who resides in Makkah; he should go outside of the Haram zone to enter ihram for `umrah, but for Hajj the people of Makkah should enter ihram from their houses and places of residence.

Note

For one who is coming by air, intending to do Hajj or `umrah, he must enter ihram on the plane when it comes in line with one of the miqats. It is not permissible for him to delay entering ihram until he lands at the airport in Jeddah, because Jeddah is not a miqat for anyone except those who live there. If he does not have the ihram garments with him, he should keep his trousers on and take off his thobe, and put it over his shoulders and chest, and form the intention to enter ihram. Then when he lands at the airport, he should put on the ihram garments when he obtains them, and take his trousers off. For women, there are no specific garments for ihram. So a woman may enter ihram on the plane in the garments she is wearing, but if she is wearing a burqa` or niqab (types of face veils) or gloves, she must take them off, and cover her face with a khimar (head cover) when she is near non-mahram men.

The essential parts, obligatory parts and sunnahs of `umrah

#### The essential parts of `umrah: 1. Forming the intention to begin the rituals, which is called ihram. 2. Circumambulating the Ka`bah (tawaf). 3. Sa`i between as-Safa and al-Marwah. * If someone omits one of the essential parts of `umrah, his `umrah is not valid unless he does it in the prescribed manner. #### Obligatory parts of `umrah: * Entering ihram from the miqat for the one who comes to it. For one whose house is closer to Makkah than the miqat, he may enter ihram from where he starts. For one who is a resident of Makkah, if he wants to do `umrah he must go outside the Haram zone (and enter ihram from there). * Shaving the head or cutting the hair. * Whoever omits one of the obligatory parts of `umrah, if he omitted it deliberately, then he incurs sin and must offer a fidyah (compensatory sacrifice). If he did not do it deliberately, then he must offer a fidyah only. #### The Sunnahs of `umrah * Everything other than the essential parts and obligatory parts of `umrah comes under the heading of the Sunnahs of `umrah, such as idtiba` (uncovering the right shoulder) and raml (walking quickly with short steps). --- ## Page 12

11

* Whoever omits one of the Sunnahs of `umrah does not have to do anything, but he is missing out on the virtue thereof.

Things which are prohibited when in ihram

The things which are prohibited when in ihram fall into three categories: #### I. Things which are prohibited for both males and females 1. It is not permissible for the muhrim (pilgrim in ihram), after forming the intention to enter ihram, to remove anything from his hair or nails. 2. The muhrim must avoid perfume of all types. 3. It is not permissible to wear gloves. 4. The muhrim must not make a proposal of marriage, and he should not do a marriage contract for himself or for anyone else. 5. It is prohibited for the muhrim to have intercourse or to do anything that leads to it. 6. He should not harm land game animals by killing them or flushing them out, or help anyone else to do that, so long as he is in ihram. #### II. What is prohibited for males, but not females 1. It is not permissible to wear stitched garments in the manner in which it is usually worn and was tailored for. 2. It is not permissible to cover the head with anything that rests on it, such as a turban and the like. #### III. What is prohibited for females, but not males 1. It is not permissible for a woman to cover her face with a burqa`, niqab and the like, but she must cover her head with her head cover and the like when non-mahram men are nearby. --- ## Page 13

12

The ruling on one who commits any of these infractions

* If he committed the infraction out of ignorance, or because he forgot or was compelled to do it, there is no sin on him and he does not have to offer a fidyah. * If he committed the infraction due to a need, it is permissible for him to do that, but he must offer a fidyah. * If he committed the infraction with no excuse and no need, then he is sinning and he must offer a fidyah.

Categories of infractions of ihram in terms of the fidyah

I. For removing anything from his hair or nails, wearing perfume, wearing gloves, wearing stitched clothing, for a male, and covering his head, wearing niqab for a woman, touching with desire – for each of these infractions, the individual has the choice between three things: a. Fasting for three days, consecutively or separately. b. Feeding six poor persons, giving each one half a sa` (approximately 1.5 kilograms) of food, such as dates or rice and so on. c. Slaughtering a sheep and distributing the meat to the poor of the Haram. II. For one who omits one of the obligatory parts of `umrah, such as entering ihram from the miqat, he must offer a fidyah, which is an animal that is valid to be offered as an udhiyah (sacrifice), male or female, sheep or goat. He must distribute all of the meat to the poor in the Haram and not eat any of it himself. III. The fidyah for having intercourse. The one who has intercourse before doing sa`i has rendered his `umrah invalid, but he must complete it, then make it up. And he must offer a fidyah; if he cannot afford that, he must fast for ten days. --- ## Page 14

13

The one who has intercourse after doing sa`i but before shaving his head or cutting his hair does not spoil his `umrah, but he must offer a fidyah; if he cannot afford that, he must fast for ten days. #### IV. The penalty for hunting; there are two scenarios: * If the animal he hunted has an equivalent among an`am (livestock) animals, then he is given the choice between three things: a. Either he should slaughter the equivalent animal, then distribute its meat among the poor and needy in the Haram. b. Or he may find out the value of the equivalent animal, then buy food with it and distribute it to the poor, giving each poor person half a sa` (approximately 1.5 kilograms) of that food. c. Or he may fast instead of feeding the poor, one day for each poor person. * If the animal he hunted has no equivalent, such as locusts for example, then he is given the choice between two things: a. Either he should find out the value of the animal that was killed, then give the equivalent in food, distributing it to the poor, giving each poor person half a sa`. b. Or he may fast instead of feeding the poor, one day for each poor person.

Description of `umrah

**When the pilgrim arrives at the miqat:** * It is recommended (mustahabb) for him to do ghusl and apply perfume before entering ihram. * Men should put on the izar (lower garment) and rida’ (upper garment). It is recommended that they be white and clean. * For women, it is permissible for them to enter ihram wearing whatever modest and covering garments they like, but they should not wear niqab or gloves. * The pilgrim should intend in his heart to commence the rituals, and it is prescribed for him to utter out loud what he intends, so he can say: “*Labbayka `umratan* (Here I am for `umrah)” or “*Allahumma labbayka `umratan* (O Allah, here I am for `umrah).” * If the pilgrim in ihram fears that he may not be able to do the rituals – because he is sick or fears an enemy and the like – it is recommended for him to say when entering ihram: “*Fa in habasani habis fa mahilli haythu habastani* (If anything prevents me from continuing, then my place of exiting ihram will be where You caused me to be prevented [from continuing]).” The benefit of stipulating this condition is that if something happens to the pilgrim in ihram that prevents him from completing his rituals – such as sickness or an enemy – it is permissible for him to exit ihram without any penalty. * It is recommended to recite the Talbiyah a great deal, and to recite it out loud on the road to Makkah. * *Labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk. Inna al-hamda wa’n-ni`mata laka wa’l-mulk, la sharika lak* (Here --- ## Page 16

15

I am, O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Verily all praise and blessings are Yours, and all sovereignty, You have no partner). **What the pilgrim should do when he enters al-Masjid al-Haram:** * When he reaches al-Masjid al-Haram, it is Sunnah to enter it with his right foot first, and to say: “*Bismillahi was-salatu was-salaam `ala Rasulillah* (In the name of Allah, and blessings and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah).” [Narrated by Ibn Majah] “*A`udhu Billah il-`azim wa bi wajhih il-karim wa sultanih il-qadim min ash-shaytan ir-rajim* (I seek refuge in Allah the Almighty and in His Noble Countenance and in His eternal Power, from the accursed Shaytan).” [Narrated by Abu Dawud]. “*Allahumm aftah li abwaba rahmatika* (O Allah, open to me the gates of Your Mercy).” [Narrated by Muslim]. * He should proceed to the Black Stone to start tawaf (circumambulation of the Ka`bah). He should touch the Black Stone with his right hand and kiss it, if he can do that. If he cannot do that, then he should kiss his hand if he touched the stone with it. If he cannot touch it with his hand, then he should face towards the stone, point to it with his hand and say takbir (“*Allahu akbar*”), but he should not kiss his hand. The best is not to push and shove, bothering other people and being bothered by them. * When touching the stone, he should say, “*Bismillah wa Allahu akbar* (in the name of Allah, and Allah is most great).” * Then he should turn to his right, with the Ka`bah on his left, and start his tawaf. When he reaches the Yemeni Corner (*ar-rukn al-Yamani*), he should touch it but not kiss it, and he should not point to it or say takbir, or push and shove to reach it. Between --- ## Page 17

16

the two corners (the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone corner) he should say: {*Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah wa fil-akhirati hasanah wa qina `adhab an-nar* (Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire)} [al-Baqarah 2:201]. * He should uncover his right shoulder (*idtiba`*) from when he starts tawaf until he finishes it. And when he has finished tawaf, he should cover both of his shoulders. * He should walk quickly with short steps (*raml*) in the first three circuits only. * When he has completed the seven circuits of tawaf, he should go to Maqam Ibrahim if he can, then pray two rak`ahs there, reciting al-Fatihah and Surat al-Kafirun in the first rak`ah and al-Fatihah and Surat al-Ikhlas in the second. * Then when he has finished his prayer, it is recommended for him to drink Zamzam water if he is able to do so, then he should go to the Black Stone and touch it if he can. * Then he should go to as-Safa and recite {Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs `umrah - there is no blame upon him for walking between them. And whoever does good of his own accord - then indeed, Allah is Appreciative and All-Knowing} [al-Baqarah 2:158]. He should recite this verse when he draws close to as-Safa before climbing the mountain, and he should not recite it anywhere except in this place and at the beginning of the first lap only; he should not repeat it in every lap. * Then he should climb as-Safa until he can see the Ka`bah, then he should turn to face it, and say, “Allahu akbar (Allah is most --- ## Page 18

17

great),” and raise his hands, and praise Allah and call upon Him in supplication. It was narrated from the Prophet (blessings and peace of Allah be upon him) that he said: “*La ilaha ill-Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulk wa lahul-hamd wa huwa `ala kulli shay’in qadir; La ilaha ill-Allah wahdahu, anjaza wa`dah wa nasara `abdah wa hazama al-ahzaba wahdah* (There is no god worthy of worship except Allah Alone, with no partner or associate; His is the dominion and to Him be praise, and He has power over all things; there is no god worthy of worship except Allah Alone, He fulfilled His promise and granted victory to His slave and defeated the confederates alone).” He should repeat this dhikr three times, and offer whatever supplication he wishes in between. * Then he should come down from as-Safa and head towards al-Marwah, walking at a normal pace, remembering Allah and calling upon Him in whatever words of supplication he can – praying for himself, his family and those whom he loves – until he reaches the first green marker. At that point he should start to run as quickly as he can until he reaches the second green marker, then he should walk at a normal pace, and keep walking until he climbs al-Marwah. When he reaches al-Marwah, he should climb it and turn to face the qiblah, and say the same as he said at as-Safa. * Then he should do seven laps of sa`i; from as-Safa to al-Marwah is one lap, and from al-Marwah to as-Safa is another lap. When he reaches the area between the two green markers, he should run, but without annoying those around him. He should continue to do that until he has completed seven laps. * Then he should shave his head, or cut his hair. A woman should gather her hair together, then remove the length of a fingertip from it. --- ## Page 19

18

* With these actions, `umrah is completed, and he may now do everything that was prohibited to him whilst in ihram. May Allah send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon all his family and companions.
